des: Fuel Pressure Sensor B Circuit Low
knowledge: The fuel pressure regulator uses a spring-loaded valve to return excess gasoline to the tank, thereby maintaining constant pressure in the fuel line. There is a vacuum tube on the fuel pressure regulator that is connected to the intake manifold to provide the appropriate gasoline pressure under different engine operating conditions (engine load is determined by the vacuum level). Most cars have the fuel pressure regulator located on the fuel rail, but some cars have the fuel pressure regulator located inside the fuel tank. The fuel pressure sensor is responsible for measuring the fuel pressure near the injector. The electronic control unit (ECU) uses this signal to adjust the injector pulse width and measure the amount of fuel entering the combustion chamber. The electronic control unit (ECU) continuously monitors the fuel pressure sensor signal voltage. If this voltage is lower than the minimum calibrated value for a set period of time, this fault code will appear.

des: O2 Sensor Slow Response - Rich to Lean (Bank 1, Sensor 2)
knowledge: The function of the oxygen sensor is to measure the oxygen content in the engine exhaust to correct the injection amount so that the engine can obtain the best air-fuel ratio. In the OBD fault code, you will often see the oxygen sensor in the row. The first row refers to the row where cylinder 1 is located, and the remaining row is the second row. Regardless of which row, the first sensor always refers to the upstream oxygen sensor (before the catalyst box), and the second sensor always refers to the downstream oxygen sensor (after the catalyst box). If the electronic control unit (ECU) finds that the acceptable oxygen sensor signal voltage change rate is not detected during the process of the air-fuel ratio changing from rich to lean, this fault code will appear.

des: Gear Lever X Position Circuit Intermittent
Knock Sensor 2 Circuit High (Bank 2)
knowledge: The knock sensor is responsible for detecting vibrations when the engine speed changes. The knock sensor then expresses this vibration in the form of voltage. When necessary, the electronic control module (ECU) will delay the ignition to avoid knocking. If this voltage is higher than the calibrated maximum value, this fault code will appear. Fault causes include faults in the knock sensor circuit, loose knock sensor, faults in the knock sensor itself, incorrect fuel grade used, loose engine module parts, and faults in the electronic control module (PCM or ECM).

des: Fuel Pressure Relief Control Circuit/Open
knowledge: The function of the fuel system overpressure relief valve is to release the fuel line pressure when the fuel line pressure is too high due to a dirty filter, blocked line, etc. If the fuel pressure release control circuit fails, this fault code will appear.

des: Hybrid Battery Voltage Sense R Circuit Range/Performance
knowledge: The function of the hybrid battery voltage monitoring circuit is to transmit the battery block voltage to the control module to monitor the charging and discharging of the battery block, as well as possible short circuits and open circuits.

des: Shift Timing Solenoid A
knowledge: The shift solenoid valve controls the hydraulic pressure to the transmission clutch by opening or closing the transmission fluid control valve to control its separation and engagement, thereby achieving gear shifting. The causes of this fault code include low transmission fluid level, dirty transmission fluid, mechanical failure of the shift solenoid valve, circuit, connector, or transmission control module (TCM) failure, etc.

des: Hybrid Battery Pack Voltage Sense D Circuit Range/Performance
Transmission Range Sensor A Circuit Low
knowledge: The transmission gear position sensor is responsible for transmitting the position of the transmission lever (PRNDL) to the electronic control unit (ECU) in the form of an electrical signal. If the ECU detects that the voltage of the transmission gear position (TR) sensor circuit is lower than the calibrated minimum value for more than a set period of time, this fault code will appear. Fault causes include the transmission gear position (TR) sensor, its circuit is open or shorted to ground, the connector is faulty, or the electronic control module (PCM or ECM) is faulty.

des: Hybrid Battery Voltage Sense I Circuit High
knowledge: The function of the hybrid battery voltage monitoring circuit is to transmit the battery block voltage to the control module to monitor the charging and discharging of the battery block, as well as possible short circuits and open circuits.

des: Rough Road Sensor A Signal Circuit
knowledge: The ECU detects cylinder misfire by monitoring changes in crankshaft rotation speed. However, changes in wheel speed caused by bad road conditions may also cause changes in crankshaft speed, thus affecting cylinder misfire detection. The anti-lock brake (ABS) and traction control (TCS) systems can determine whether the vehicle is driving in bad road conditions through the signal of the wheel speed sensor. If the system detects a serious bad road condition that affects misfire detection, it will notify the ECU to turn off misfire detection to prevent recording of erroneous fault information. The bad road condition sensor signal is generally a square wave transmitted from the control module of the ABS (anti-lock brake) system/drive anti-skid traction control (TCS) system to the powertrain control module (PCM).

des: Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch F Circuit Range/Performance
knowledge: The shift solenoid valve controls the hydraulic pressure to the transmission clutch by opening or closing the transmission fluid control valve to control its separation and engagement, thereby achieving gear shifting. Accurate control of the transmission fluid pressure is very important for smooth gear shifting. The function of the transmission fluid pressure (TFP) sensor is to transmit the transmission fluid pressure in the form of an electrical signal to the transmission control module (TCU) as a reference for the operation of the transmission fluid pressure control solenoid valve.

des: Fan Speed Sensor Circuit No Signal
knowledge: The causes of the failure include the fan speed sensor, its circuit, connector, fan motor mechanical failure, or electronic control unit (ECU), etc.

des: HO2S Heater Control Circuit High (Bank 1, Sensor 1)
knowledge: The function of the oxygen sensor is to measure the oxygen content in the engine exhaust to correct the injection amount so that the engine can obtain the best air-fuel ratio. In the OBD fault code, you will often see the oxygen sensor in which bank. Bank 1 refers to the bank where cylinder 1 is located, and the remaining bank is bank 2. Regardless of which bank, the first sensor always refers to the upstream oxygen sensor (before the catalyst box), and the second sensor always refers to the downstream oxygen sensor (after the catalyst box). The electronic control unit (ECU) maintains the temperature of the oxygen sensor at 780oC by controlling the on/off of the oxygen sensor heater. If the control circuit voltage of the heater is higher than the calibrated maximum value, this fault code will appear.

des: HO2S Heater Control Circuit High (Bank 1, Sensor 2)
knowledge: The function of the oxygen sensor is to measure the oxygen content in the engine exhaust to correct the injection amount so that the engine can obtain the best air-fuel ratio. In the OBD fault code, you will often see the oxygen sensor in which bank. Bank 1 refers to the bank where cylinder 1 is located, and the remaining bank is bank 2. Regardless of which bank, the first sensor always refers to the upstream oxygen sensor (before the catalyst box), and the second sensor always refers to the downstream oxygen sensor (after the catalyst box). The electronic control unit (ECU) maintains the temperature of the oxygen sensor at 780oC by controlling the on/off of the oxygen sensor heater. If the control circuit voltage of the heater is higher than the calibrated maximum value, this fault code will appear.

des: Hybrid Battery Pack Cooling Fan 1 Control Circuit/Open
knowledge: The battery pack fan motor controller is responsible for regulating the voltage of the hybrid battery pack cooling fan. If the cooling fan 1 control circuit voltage exceeds the normal range of the target voltage, this fault code will appear.

des: Hybrid Battery Voltage Sense F Circuit
knowledge: The function of the hybrid battery voltage monitoring circuit is to transmit the battery block voltage to the control module to monitor the charging and discharging of the battery block, as well as possible short circuits and open circuits.

des: Drive Motor B Phase W Current Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
knowledge: The Hybrid Vehicle Electronic Control Unit (HV ECU) is responsible for monitoring the drive motor inverter current sensor. If the HV ECU detects an error, this fault code will appear.

des: Throttle Actuator Control Lamp Control Circuit
knowledge: In the electronic throttle control (ETC) system, the accelerator pedal position (APP) sensor transmits the position of the accelerator pedal to the throttle control module in the form of an electrical signal, which serves as a reference for the throttle actuator to control the throttle valve opening. The throttle actuator is a stepper motor, which is responsible for controlling the throttle opening according to the instructions of the throttle control module.

des: EVAP Purge Flow Sensor Circuit Low
knowledge: The EVAP system directs gasoline vapors from the fuel tank into a tank containing activated carbon that absorbs gasoline vapors. The engine then uses fresh air to purge these gasoline vapors into the engine combustion chambers. The Electronic Control Unit (ECU) has detected that the EVAP purge flow sensor signal voltage is below the calibrated minimum value.

des: Transmission Fluid Level Sensor Circuit High
knowledge: The function of the transmission fluid level sensor is to transmit the transmission fluid level to the electronic control unit (ECU) in the form of an electrical signal. This fault code indicates that the voltage of the transmission fluid level sensor signal circuit is higher than the calibrated maximum value. The causes of the fault include the transmission fluid level sensor, circuit, connector, or ECU.

des: Cylinder 12 Injector Circuit Range/Performance
knowledge: The function of the fuel injector is to atomize the fuel so that it meets the requirements of combustion. The working principle is that when the electromagnetic coil is energized, suction is generated, the needle valve is sucked up, the spray hole is opened, and the fuel is sprayed out at high speed through the annular gap between the needle pin at the head of the needle valve and the spray hole to form a mist. The electronic control unit controls the injection amount by controlling the time interval (also called pulse width) of the injector opening. If the electronic control unit (ECU) detects an error in the circuit of the 12th cylinder injector, this fault code will appear.

des: Catalyst Temperature Sensor Circuit (Bank 2, Sensor 2)
knowledge: The catalytic converter (also known as the catalytic purification converter) is an exhaust purification device that uses the action of a catalyst to convert CO, HC and NOx in the exhaust into gases that are harmless to the human body. It is generally located before the muffler of the exhaust pipe. This fault code indicates that the catalytic converter temperature sensor circuit is faulty. The causes of the fault include the catalytic converter temperature sensor, its circuit, connector, or electronic control unit (ECU).

des: Charge Air Cooler Bypass Position Sensor A Circuit Range/Performance
knowledge: The charge air cooler (also called intercooler) is used to cool the charge air coming out of the supercharger. After the air passes through the supercharger, the pressure and temperature increase. The charge air cooler can reduce the charge air temperature, thereby increasing the air density and charging efficiency, so as to achieve the purpose of increasing engine power and reducing emissions. The charge air cooler bypass valve is used to bypass part of the air around the air cooler. This air is then mixed with the air cooled by the air cooler and enters the engine to ensure that the intake air temperature is higher than the dew temperature. If the air cooler bypass valve position sensor A circuit voltage is wrong, this fault code will appear.

des: Hybrid Battery Temperature Sensor C Circuit High
knowledge: The battery control module controls the battery fan on/off based on the signal from the battery temperature sensor. If the battery control module detects that the battery temperature sensor signal circuit voltage is higher than the calibrated maximum value, this fault code will appear.

des: Generator Over Temperature
knowledge: The generator is in an over-temperature state.

des: Cylinder 4 Glow Plug Control Circuit Low
knowledge: The function of the glow plug is to heat the compressed gas in the diesel engine combustion chamber through the electric heating coil, so that the diesel engine can be started easily in cold weather. The glow plug control module can automate the preheating and cycling process of the glow plug. If the electronic control unit (ECU) detects that the voltage of the cylinder 4 glow plug circuit is lower than the calibrated minimum value, this fault code will appear.

des: Drive Motor A Temperature Sensor Circuit High
knowledge: The temperature sensor circuit of the drive motor A is faulty. The causes of the fault include the circuit, connector, electronic control unit, drive motor, etc. The drive motor temperature sensor of some vehicles is integrated with the drive motor. Therefore, if it is determined that the problem is with the temperature sensor itself, it may be necessary to replace the entire drive motor.

des: Knock Sensor 1 Circuit Range/Performance (Bank 1 or Single Sensor)
knowledge: The knock sensor is responsible for detecting vibrations when the engine speed changes. The knock sensor then expresses this vibration in the form of voltage. When necessary, the electronic control module (ECU) will delay the ignition to prevent knocking. If this voltage is wrong, this fault code will appear. Fault causes include faults in the knock sensor circuit, connectors, itself, or electronic control module (PCM or ECM) failure.

des: Generator Phase W Current High
knowledge: The Hybrid Vehicle Electronic Control Unit (HV ECU) is responsible for monitoring the generator inverter current sensor. If the HV ECU detects an error, this fault code will appear.

des: High Voltage Fuse
knowledge: When the interlock switch is open, the voltage between VBB9 and VBB10 terminals is lower than the normal value.

des: Radiator Coolant Temperature Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
knowledge: The (water tank) radiator coolant temperature sensor uses the principle of thermistor to transmit the radiator temperature signal to the electronic control unit (ECU) in the form of voltage. If the ECU detects that the (water tank) radiator coolant temperature sensor signal voltage is wrong, this fault code will appear.

des: Cold Start B Camshaft Position Timing Over-Advanced (Bank 1)
knowledge: The function of the camshaft is to control the opening and closing of the valve. When the cold engine is started, if the electronic control unit (ECU) detects that the B (exhaust/right/rear) camshaft timing exceeds the maximum setting value or is always in the advanced state, this fault code will appear.

des: Internal Control Module Accelerator Pedal Position Performance
knowledge: The engine control module, also called the engine control unit (in some cars, the engine control module and the transmission control module are integrated into a powertrain control module), controls the operation of the entire engine. Its most important function is to control the optimal fuel injection amount and ignition timing of the engine. Another important function is to monitor the components of exhaust emission control. In the electronic throttle control (ETC) system, the accelerator pedal position (APP) sensor is used to transmit the position of the accelerator pedal to the throttle control module in the form of an electrical signal, which serves as a reference for the throttle actuator to control the throttle valve opening.

des: Manifold Absolute Pressure/Barometric Pressure Circuit Range/Performance
knowledge: The function of the Manifold Absolute Pressure (MAP) sensor is to measure the pressure (vacuum) in the intake manifold. The powertrain control module (PCM) then uses the difference between the intake manifold pressure and the atmospheric pressure (which is linearly related to the engine load) as a basis for determining the basic injection amount of the injector to help the engine achieve the best air-fuel ratio under different loads. The function of the atmospheric pressure sensor (sometimes called the high altitude compensator, HAC) is to transmit the atmospheric pressure to the electronic control module in the form of an electrical signal. Atmospheric pressure varies with weather and altitude. The lower the pressure, the thinner the air. The powertrain control module (PCM) will correct the fuel supply based on the atmospheric pressure value to help the engine achieve the best air-fuel ratio. If the electronic control unit (ECU) detects that the manifold absolute pressure (MAP) sensor/barometric pressure sensor signal voltage is out of the normal range of calibration, this fault code will appear. The fault causes include MAP sensor circuit, connector or sensor itself; atmospheric pressure (BARO) sensor circuit, connector or sensor itself; or electronic control module (PCM or ECM) fault, etc.

des: Transmission Friction Element H Performance/Stuck Off
Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch B Circuit
knowledge: The shift solenoid valve controls the hydraulic pressure to the transmission clutch by opening or closing the transmission fluid control valve to control its separation and engagement, thereby achieving gear shifting. Accurate control of the transmission fluid pressure is very important for smooth gear shifting. The function of the transmission fluid pressure (TFP) sensor is to transmit the transmission fluid pressure in the form of an electrical signal to the transmission control module (TCU) as a reference for the operation of the transmission fluid pressure control solenoid valve.

des: Hybrid Battery Pack Cooling Fan Sense Circuit/Open
Pressure Control Solenoid A Control Circuit Range/Performance
knowledge: The shift solenoid valve controls the hydraulic pressure to the transmission clutch by opening or closing the transmission fluid control valve to control its separation and engagement, thereby achieving gear shifting. Accurate control of the transmission fluid pressure is very important for smooth gear shifting. The function of the pressure control solenoid valve is to control the pressure of the transmission fluid. The causes of this fault code include the pressure control solenoid valve itself, the circuit, the connector, etc. At the same time, it should be noted that in some cases, the failure of the transmission control solenoid valve is not due to electronic problems, but due to pipeline blockage or mechanical problems. Many times, many such failures are caused simply because the transmission oil is too dirty.

des: Secondary Air Injection System Switching Valve A Circuit Shorted
knowledge: When the engine is just started, the secondary air injection system oxidizes harmful gases such as hydrocarbons and carbon monoxide by forcing air into the exhaust manifold. This process also accelerates the warming process of the catalytic converter. If the electronic control unit (ECU) detects a short circuit in the secondary air injection system control solenoid valve circuit, this fault code will appear. The causes of the fault include a short circuit to the positive pole of the secondary air injection actuator circuit, an actuator failure, a relay failure, or a failure of the electronic control module (PCM or ECM).

des: Engine Mount A Control Circuit Low
knowledge: The electronically controlled suspension of a car can adjust the suspension hardness, damping, and body height according to driving needs, improving the vehicle's form stability and handling. If the control module detects that the voltage of the control circuit of the suspension system is lower than the calibrated minimum value, this fault code will appear.

des: Fuel Shutoff Valve A Control Circuit High
knowledge: The function of the fuel cut-off valve is to cut off the fuel supply to the engine when the car encounters an emergency (such as rollover). This fault code indicates that the electronic control unit (ECU) detects that the voltage of the fuel cut-off valve A control circuit is higher than the calibrated maximum value.

des: Transmission Fluid Level Too Low
knowledge: The transmission fluid level sensor indicates that the transmission fluid level is too low.

des: O2 Sensor Circuit (Bank 1, Sensor 2)
knowledge: The function of the oxygen sensor is to measure the oxygen content in the engine exhaust to correct the injection amount so that the engine can obtain the best air-fuel ratio. In the OBD fault code, you will often see the oxygen sensor in the row. The first row refers to the row where cylinder 1 is located, and the remaining row is the second row. Regardless of which row, the first sensor always refers to the upstream oxygen sensor (before the catalyst box), and the second sensor always refers to the downstream oxygen sensor (after the catalyst box). If the electronic control unit (ECU) detects a problem with the circuit used to measure the oxygen content in the exhaust gas, this fault code will appear. The causes of the fault include leakage in the exhaust pipe or exhaust manifold, intersection of the oxygen sensor signal circuit and the ground circuit, oxygen sensor contamination or failure by fuel, electronic control module (PCM or ECM) failure, etc.

des: Intake Manifold Tuning Valve Control Circuit High (Bank 1)
knowledge: If the length of the intake manifold runner is optimal, the pressure wave generated by the valve closing will help guide the fuel-air mixture into the engine. The problem is that the optimal intake manifold runner lengths for different engine speeds are also different. The function of the manifold tuning valve (MTV) is to guide the intake air into intake manifolds of different lengths according to the engine speed, so as to optimize the engine torque at different speeds. If the electronic control unit (ECU) detects that the intake manifold tuning valve control circuit voltage is higher than the calibrated maximum value during self-test, this fault code will appear.

des: Vehicle Speed Sensor A
knowledge: The function of the vehicle speed sensor (VSS) is to transmit the speed of the car to the electronic control unit (ECU) in the form of an electrical signal, which is used as a reference for controlling engine idle speed, automatic transmission shifting, torque converter lock, engine cooling fan opening and closing, cruise control and other functions. The electronic control unit (ECU) believes that if the engine speed is higher than the stall speed of the torque converter (automatic transmission) and the engine load is high, then the vehicle must be moving. If the vehicle speed sensor (VSS) shows zero speed in this case, this fault code will appear.

des: PCM/ECM/TCU Internal Temperature Sensor B Circuit High
knowledge: The engine control module, also called the engine control unit (the engine control module and transmission control module on some cars are integrated into the powertrain control module), controls the operation of the entire engine. Its most important function is to control the optimal fuel injection amount and ignition timing of the engine. Another important function is to monitor the components responsible for exhaust emission control. The transmission control module (TCM or TCU) collects information from various sensors and the engine control module to help the transmission decide when and how to shift gears, so that the car can improve performance, shift smoothly, and save fuel. This fault code indicates that the voltage of the temperature sensor signal circuit inside the control module exceeds the maximum range of calibration. The cause of the fault is the internal temperature sensor, circuit, connector, or control module.

des: B Camshaft Profile Control Circuit High (Bank 1)
knowledge: The function of the camshaft is to control the opening and closing of the valves. In the variable valve timing system, the electronic camshaft adjustment valve (or oil control valve, OCV) adjusts the angle of the camshaft according to the instructions from the engine control module (ECM) by changing the oil pressure to the camshaft adjuster (mechanical type) to ensure that the valve opens and closes at the best time. This optimizes the efficiency and power of the engine in all speed ranges. This fault code indicates that the voltage of the B (exhaust/right/rear) camshaft profile control circuit is higher than the calibrated maximum value.

des: O2 Sensor Circuit Slow Response (Bank 2, Sensor 1)
knowledge: The function of the oxygen sensor is to measure the oxygen content in the engine exhaust to correct the injection amount so that the engine can obtain the best air-fuel ratio. In the OBD fault code, you will often see the oxygen sensor in the bank. Bank 1 refers to the bank where cylinder 1 is located, and the remaining bank is bank 2. Regardless of which bank, the first sensor always refers to the upstream oxygen sensor (before the catalyst box), and the second sensor always refers to the downstream oxygen sensor (after the catalyst box). The heated oxygen sensor monitor tracks the voltage change rate during the rise and fall of the oxygen sensor signal. When the voltage change rate is lower than the calibration value, the electronic control unit (ECU) will begin to modify the air-fuel ratio and try to increase the voltage change rate of the oxygen sensor. If the ECU has reached the acceptable fuel trim limit or has exceeded the acceptable fuel trim time, and still does not monitor an acceptable voltage change rate, this fault code will appear. Fault causes include oxygen sensor contamination due to silicon in the fuel, open circuit of oxygen sensor signal circuit, oxygen sensor itself failure, exhaust pipe or exhaust manifold leakage, electronic control module (PCM or ECM) failure, etc.

des: Rough Road Sensor B Signal Circuit
knowledge: The ECU detects cylinder misfire by monitoring changes in crankshaft rotation speed. However, changes in wheel speed caused by bad road conditions may also cause changes in crankshaft speed, thus affecting cylinder misfire detection. The anti-lock brake (ABS) and traction control (TCS) systems can determine whether the vehicle is driving in bad road conditions through the signal of the wheel speed sensor. If the system detects a serious bad road condition that affects misfire detection, it will notify the ECU to turn off misfire detection to prevent recording of erroneous fault information. The bad road condition sensor signal is generally a square wave transmitted from the control module of the ABS (anti-lock brake) system/drive anti-skid traction control (TCS) system to the powertrain control module (PCM).

des: Motor Electronics Coolant Pump A Control Performance
knowledge: The Motor Electronics Cooling System (MECS) is an independent system that provides cooling for the transmission (e.g. eCVT) motor, control module and DC/DC converter. It has its own radiator, coolant pump, coolant temperature sensor, etc. The MECS coolant pump is a 12 volt electric pump controlled by the Electronic Control Unit (ECU).

des: Cylinder 10 - Fuel Trim at Min Limit
knowledge: Fuel trimming refers to the electronic control unit (ECU) controlling fuel delivery by increasing or decreasing the time the injectors are open to achieve the best air-fuel ratio (14.7:1 air-to-gasoline mass ratio) for the engine. Too rich an air-fuel ratio means too much fuel is delivered, and too lean an air-fuel ratio means too little fuel is delivered. This fault code will appear if fuel trim reaches and stays at the minimum limit for more than a certain period of time.

des: Hybrid Battery Pack Cooling Fan Supply Voltage Circuit/Open
A Camshaft Position - Timing Over-Advanced or System Performance (Bank 2)
knowledge: The function of the camshaft is to control the opening and closing of the valve. In the variable valve timing system, the electronic camshaft adjustment valve (or oil control valve, OCV) adjusts the angle of the camshaft according to the command from the engine control module (ECM) by changing the oil pressure to the camshaft adjuster (mechanical type) to ensure that the valve opens and closes at the best time. The causes of P0021 include A intake/left/front camshaft timing is not set properly, the camshaft is mechanically stuck, or the actuator valve is stuck in the open position.

des: Cylinder 6 - Injector Restricted
knowledge: The function of the fuel injector is to atomize the fuel so that it meets the requirements of combustion. The working principle is that when the electromagnetic coil is energized, suction is generated, the needle valve is sucked up, the spray hole is opened, and the fuel is sprayed out at high speed through the annular gap between the needle pin at the head of the needle valve and the spray hole to form a mist. The electronic control unit controls the injection amount by controlling the time interval (also called pulse width) of the fuel injector opening. This fault code indicates that the performance of the 6th cylinder fuel injector is wrong.

des: Transmission Friction Element G Slip Detected
Hybrid Battery Voltage Sense G Circuit High
knowledge: The function of the hybrid battery voltage monitoring circuit is to transmit the battery block voltage to the control module to monitor the charging and discharging of the battery block, as well as possible short circuits and open circuits.

des: Engine Oil Temperature Sensor Circuit High
knowledge: The engine oil temperature (EOT) sensor transmits the oil temperature to the electronic control unit (ECU) in the form of an electrical signal based on the principle of thermistor. If the electronic control unit (ECU) detects that the signal voltage of the oil temperature sensor is continuously higher than the calibrated upper limit (low temperature) for a set period of time, this fault code will appear. The cause of the fault includes the oil temperature sensor, its circuit, or connector.

des: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Circuit Low (Bank 1, Sensor 1)
knowledge: The exhaust temperature sensor is used to transmit the exhaust temperature to the electronic control unit (ECU) in the form of an electrical signal. The exhaust temperature produced by the correct air-fuel ratio is lower than the exhaust temperature produced by too rich or too lean air-fuel ratio. Excessive exhaust temperature (>160 degrees Celsius) will damage the engine. If the electronic control unit (ECU) detects that the exhaust temperature sensor signal voltage is lower than 0.1 volts (or 0.2 volts) within a set time period (15 seconds), this fault code will appear.

des: Hydraulic Pressure Unit
Sensor Reference Voltage B Circuit Range/Performance
knowledge: The electronic control unit (ECU) has detected an error in the 5 volt reference voltage circuit B. Causes of the fault include a short circuit or short circuit from the 5 volt reference voltage circuit to a sensor, a short circuit or open circuit in one or more sensors, the ECU, etc.

des: Ignition/Distributor Engine Speed Input Circuit No Signal
knowledge: The causes of the fault include engine speed sensor failure, sensor wheel failure or mismatch, electronic control module (PCM or ECM) failure, etc.

des: Exhaust Gas Recirculation Temperature Sensor A Circuit Low
knowledge: The function of the exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) system is to introduce a small amount of exhaust gas into the intake manifold when the engine is running at high load. The presence of these exhaust gases reduces the temperature and pressure of the combustion chamber, thereby reducing the emission of nitrogen oxide pollutants. If the electronic control unit (ECU) detects that the signal voltage of the exhaust gas recirculation valve (EGR) temperature sensor is lower than the calibrated minimum value (0.15 volts) within the set time period (5 seconds), this fault code will appear.

des: Crankshaft Position - Camshaft Position Correlation (Bank 1, Sensor B)
knowledge: The function of the crankshaft is to convert the up and down motion of the piston into rotational motion. The function of the camshaft is to control the opening and closing of the valve. The electronic control unit (ECU) will continuously monitor the timing position of the variable camshaft and check the relative position between the camshaft and the crankshaft. If the relative position misalignment exceeds 1 gear tooth, this fault code will appear. The causes of the fault include camshaft position sensor itself or its circuit failure, crankshaft position sensor itself or its circuit failure, engine speed sensor failure, oil contamination, variable camshaft solenoid valve stuck, etc.

des: 14 Volt Power Module System Performance
Camshaft Position Sensor B Circuit Low (Bank 2)
knowledge: The function of the camshaft is to control the opening and closing of the valves. In the variable valve timing system, the electronic camshaft adjustment valve (or oil control valve, OCV) adjusts the angle of the camshaft according to the instructions from the engine control module (ECM) by changing the oil pressure to the camshaft adjuster (mechanical type) to ensure that the valves open and close at the best time. The function of the camshaft position (CMP) sensor is to transmit the camshaft position (relative position of the valve) to the electronic control unit (ECU) in the form of a voltage signal. If the electronic control unit (ECU) detects that the voltage of the camshaft sensor B circuit is lower than the calibrated minimum value, this fault code will appear. The causes of the fault include the camshaft position (CMP) sensor circuit, connector, its own fault, or electronic control module (PCM or ECM) fault, etc.

des: Hybrid Battery Pack Current Sensor B Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
knowledge: The battery control module monitors the charge and discharge of the battery through the signal from the battery current sensor. If the control module finds that the battery current sensor is faulty, this fault code will appear.

des: Engine Oil Over Temperature
knowledge: The Electronic Control Unit (ECU) has detected that the engine is in a state of excessive oil temperature. This means that the high oil temperature protection has been activated. The ECU will avoid high engine speeds by disabling the injectors, etc., to reduce engine damage caused by excessive oil temperature.

des: Drive Motor B Phase U Current Sensor Circuit
knowledge: The Hybrid Vehicle Electronic Control Unit (HV ECU) is responsible for monitoring the drive motor inverter current sensor. If the HV ECU detects an error, this fault code will appear.

des: Turbocharger/Supercharger Turbine Overspeed
knowledge: A turbocharger uses the inertial force of the exhaust gas discharged by the engine to drive the turbine, which in turn drives the coaxial impeller to increase the intake pressure, thereby increasing the power of the vehicle. A supercharger is an air compressor used to increase the intake air for an internal combustion engine. More intake air provides more oxygen to the engine, allowing the control module to provide more fuel, thereby increasing output power. This fault code indicates that the turbine speed is fast. Possible causes include boost controller, wastegate actuator, etc.

des: Actuator Supply Voltage A Circuit High
knowledge: The Powertrain Control Module (PCM) has detected that the voltage of the transmission actuator power supply A circuit is too high. Fault causes include circuit or connector failure, automatic transmission hydraulic sensor failure, solenoid valve failure, transmission control module failure, transmission input speed (RPM) sensor failure, transmission output speed (RPM) sensor failure, etc.

des: Park/Neutral Switch Input Circuit Low
knowledge: The function of the park/neutral position switch is to transmit information about whether the automatic transmission is in park/neutral or other gears to the electronic control unit (ECU) as a reference for determining whether the engine is idling or increasing the load. The switch is also used in the starter relay circuit to prevent the car from starting in gears other than park/neutral.

des: A Camshaft Profile Control Circuit High (Bank 2)
knowledge: The function of the camshaft is to control the opening and closing of the valves. In the variable valve timing system, the electronic camshaft adjustment valve (or oil control valve, OCV) adjusts the angle of the camshaft according to the instructions from the engine control module (ECM) by changing the oil pressure to the camshaft adjuster (mechanical type) to ensure that the valves open and close at the best time. This optimizes the efficiency and power of the engine in all speed ranges. If the electronic control unit (ECU) detects that the voltage of the A (intake/left/front) camshaft profile control circuit is higher than the calibrated maximum value for a period of time, this fault code will appear.

des: HO2S Heater Control Circuit (Bank 1, Sensor 2)
knowledge: The function of the oxygen sensor is to measure the oxygen content in the engine exhaust to correct the injection amount so that the engine can obtain the best air-fuel ratio. In the OBD fault code, you will often see the oxygen sensor in the row. The first row refers to the row where cylinder 1 is located, and the remaining row is the second row. Regardless of which row, the first sensor always refers to the upstream oxygen sensor (before the catalyst box), and the second sensor always refers to the downstream oxygen sensor (after the catalyst box). The electronic control unit (ECU) maintains the temperature of the oxygen sensor at 780oC by controlling the on/off of the oxygen sensor heater. If the oxygen sensor does not reach the required temperature within the set time, or the ECU cannot maintain the set temperature, this fault code will appear.

des: Hybrid Battery Voltage Sense E Circuit
knowledge: The function of the hybrid battery voltage monitoring circuit is to transmit the battery block voltage to the control module to monitor the charging and discharging of the battery block, as well as possible short circuits and open circuits.

des: Hybrid Battery Voltage Sense Y Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
knowledge: The function of the hybrid battery voltage monitoring circuit is to transmit the battery block voltage to the control module to monitor the charging and discharging of the battery block, as well as possible short circuits and open circuits.

des: Cylinder 3 Glow Plug Circuit Range/Performance
knowledge: The function of the glow plug is to heat the compressed gas in the diesel engine combustion chamber through the electric heating coil, so that the diesel engine can be started easily in cold weather. The glow plug control module can automate the preheating and cycling process of the glow plug. If the electronic control unit (ECU) detects a fault in the cylinder 3 glow plug circuit, this fault code will appear.

des: 14 Volt Power Module System Voltage
knowledge: The control module detects that the system voltage is too high or too low.

des: Drive Motor B Position Sensor Circuit Intermittent
knowledge: The causes of the fault include the drive motor B position sensor circuit, connector, or sensor itself; hybrid drive motor; hybrid vehicle electronic control unit (HV ECU).

des: Fuel Pressure Sensor B Circuit High
knowledge: The fuel pressure regulator uses a spring-loaded valve to return excess gasoline to the tank, thereby maintaining constant pressure in the fuel line. There is a vacuum tube on the fuel pressure regulator that is connected to the intake manifold to provide the appropriate gasoline pressure under different engine operating conditions (according to the vacuum level to determine the engine load). Most cars have the fuel pressure regulator located on the fuel rail, but some cars have the fuel pressure regulator located inside the fuel tank. The fuel pressure sensor is responsible for measuring the fuel pressure near the injector. The electronic control unit (ECU) uses this signal to adjust the injector pulse width and measure the amount of fuel entering the combustion chamber. The electronic control unit (ECU) continuously monitors the fuel pressure sensor signal voltage. If this voltage is higher than the highest calibrated value for a set period of time, this fault code will appear.

des: A Camshaft Position Slow Response (Bank 2)
knowledge: The function of the camshaft is to control the opening and closing of the valves. In the variable valve timing system, the electronic camshaft regulating valve (or oil control valve, OCV) adjusts the angle of the camshaft according to the command from the engine control module (ECM) by changing the oil pressure to the camshaft adjuster (mechanical type) to ensure that the valve opens and closes at the best time. The causes of P000C include the intake/left/front camshaft regulating valve (oil control valve), its circuit, connector, dirty oil or ECU.

des: Hybrid Battery Voltage Sense U Circuit Low
knowledge: The function of the hybrid battery voltage monitoring circuit is to transmit the battery block voltage to the control module to monitor the charging and discharging of the battery block, as well as possible short circuits and open circuits.

des: Fuel Cap Lamp Control Circuit
knowledge: The cause of the fault includes the fuel tank cap indicator light, circuit, connector, or electronic control unit (ECU)

des: Variable A/C Compressor Control Circuit Low
knowledge: The variable (displacement) air conditioning compressor controls the displacement of the compressor refrigerant being compressed by changing the angle of the splash plate. This fault code indicates that the voltage of the variable (displacement) air conditioning compressor control circuit is lower than the calibrated minimum value.

des: Gear Shift Control Module B Performance
Drive Motor A Position Sensor Not Learned
O2 Sensor Delayed Response - Rich to Lean (Bank 1, Sensor 1)
knowledge: The function of the oxygen sensor is to measure the oxygen content in the engine exhaust to correct the injection amount so that the engine can obtain the best air-fuel ratio. In the OBD fault code, you will often see the oxygen sensor in the row. The first row refers to the row where cylinder 1 is located, and the remaining row is the second row. Regardless of which row, the first sensor always refers to the upstream oxygen sensor (before the catalyst box), and the second sensor always refers to the downstream oxygen sensor (after the catalyst box). The heated oxygen sensor monitor tracks the voltage change rate during the rise and fall of the oxygen sensor signal. If the electronic control unit (ECU) finds that the voltage change rate lags behind during the process of the air-fuel ratio changing from rich to lean, this fault code will appear.

des: Hybrid Battery Voltage Sense C Circuit
knowledge: The function of the hybrid battery voltage monitoring circuit is to transmit the battery block voltage to the control module to monitor the charging and discharging of the battery block, as well as possible short circuits and open circuits.

des: TCU Power Relay Sense Circuit Low
knowledge: The transmission control module (TCM or TCU) collects information from various sensors and the engine control module to help the transmission decide when and how to shift gears, so that the car can improve performance, shift smoothly, and save fuel. The function of the control module relay is to continue to keep the control module powered after the ignition switch is turned off until the control module completes the shutdown process.

des: Cylinder 10 - Fuel Trim at Max Limit
knowledge: Fuel trimming refers to the electronic control unit (ECU) controlling fuel delivery by increasing or decreasing the time the injectors are open to achieve the best air-fuel ratio (14.7:1 air-to-gasoline mass ratio) for the engine. Too rich an air-fuel ratio means too much fuel is delivered, and too lean an air-fuel ratio means too little fuel is delivered. This fault code will appear if fuel trim reaches and stays at the maximum limit for more than a certain period of time.

des: Fuel Temperature Sensor B Circuit
knowledge: The fuel temperature sensor is responsible for monitoring the temperature of the fuel going to the fuel pump to avoid vapor lock caused by excessive temperature (120 degrees Celsius), which may cause damage to the fuel pump or injector. The electronic control unit (ECU) continuously monitors the fuel temperature sensor signal voltage. If this voltage exceeds the normal calibration value within a set period of time, this fault code will appear.

des: Crankcase Pressure Sensor Circuit
knowledge: The function of the crankcase pressure sensor is to transmit the pressure in the crankcase to the electronic control unit (ECU) in the form of an electrical signal to detect the working status of the crankcase forced ventilation system. This fault code indicates that the ECU has detected a fault in the crankcase pressure sensor circuit.

des: Ambient Air Temperature Sensor Circuit
knowledge: The function of the ambient air temperature sensor is to transmit the external air temperature to the electronic control unit (ECU) in the form of an electrical signal to help the engine achieve the best air-fuel ratio. The sensor is generally located in front of or on both sides of the radiator. This fault code indicates that the signal voltage of the ambient air temperature sensor exceeds the normal range of calibration.

des: Motor Electronics Coolant Pump B Control Performance
knowledge: The Motor Electronics Cooling System (MECS) is an independent system that provides cooling for the transmission (e.g. eCVT) motor, control module and DC/DC converter. It has its own radiator, coolant pump, coolant temperature sensor, etc. The MECS coolant pump is a 12 volt electric pump controlled by the Electronic Control Unit (ECU).

des: Cylinder 10 - Injector Leaking
knowledge: The function of the fuel injector is to atomize the fuel so that it meets the requirements of combustion. The working principle is that when the electromagnetic coil is energized, suction is generated, the needle valve is sucked up, the spray hole is opened, and the fuel is sprayed out at high speed through the annular gap between the needle pin at the head of the needle valve and the spray hole to form a mist. The electronic control unit controls the injection amount by controlling the time interval (also called pulse width) of the fuel injector opening. This fault code indicates that the 10th cylinder fuel injector is leaking.

des: Drive Motor B Phase U Current High
knowledge: The Hybrid Vehicle Electronic Control Unit (HV ECU) is responsible for monitoring the drive motor inverter current sensor. If the HV ECU detects an error, this fault code will appear.

des: Immobilizer Key Not Programmed - ECM/PCM
knowledge: The function of the anti-theft control module is to ensure that the car will not be allowed to start unless the special key exists and it matches various components. The engine control module, also called the engine control unit (the engine control module and the transmission control module on some cars are integrated into the powertrain control module), controls the operation of the entire engine. Its most important function is to control the optimal injection amount and ignition timing of the engine. Another important function is to monitor the exhaust emission control components.

des: Fuel System Over Pressure Relief Valve Activated
knowledge: The function of the fuel system overpressure relief valve is to release the fuel line pressure to avoid damage to the line when the line pressure is too high due to a dirty filter, blocked line, etc. This fault code indicates that the electronic control unit (ECU) detects that the fuel system is in an overpressure state and the fuel system overpressure relief valve is activated. Excessive pressure may be caused by problems such as the fuel pressure regulator, fuel line blockage, fuel pressure sensor, and fuel pump control module.

des: Shift Solenoid C Stuck On
knowledge: The shift solenoid valve controls the hydraulic pressure to the transmission clutch by opening or closing the transmission fluid control valve to control its separation and engagement, thereby achieving gear shifting. The causes of this fault code include low transmission fluid level, dirty transmission fluid, mechanical failure of the shift solenoid valve, circuit, connector, or transmission control module (TCM) failure, etc.

des: Stuck in Gear 1
knowledge: While the vehicle is driving, the electronic control unit (ECU) detects that the shift solenoid valve is faulty (stuck), causing the transmission to be stuck in 1st gear. The causes of the fault include the shift solenoid valve, input shaft speed sensor, output shaft speed sensor, circuit, connector, control module, and transmission mechanical failure, etc.

des: Engine Hot Lamp Output Control Circuit
Intake Valve Control Solenoid Circuit High (Bank 2)
knowledge: The function of the camshaft is to control the opening and closing of the valves. In the variable valve timing system, the electronic camshaft adjustment valve (or oil control valve, OCV) adjusts the angle of the camshaft by changing the oil pressure to the camshaft adjuster (mechanical) according to the command from the engine control module (ECM) to ensure that the valves open and close at the best time. If the intake camshaft adjustment valve circuit voltage is higher than the calibrated maximum value, this fault code will appear.

des: Cylinder 1 Fuel Injector Offset Learning At Max Limit
knowledge: The function of the fuel injector is to atomize the fuel so that it meets the requirements of combustion. The working principle is that when the electromagnetic coil is energized, suction is generated, the needle valve is sucked up, the spray hole is opened, and the fuel is sprayed out at high speed through the annular gap between the needle pin at the head of the needle valve and the spray hole to form a mist. The electronic control unit controls the injection amount by controlling the time interval (also called pulse width) of the injector opening. If the electronic control unit (ECU) detects that the compensation learning of the 1st cylinder injector has reached the maximum learning limit, this fault code will appear.

des: Camshaft Position Sensor A Circuit Range/Performance (Bank 2)
knowledge: The function of the camshaft is to control the opening and closing of the valves. In the variable valve timing system, the electronic camshaft adjustment valve (or oil control valve, OCV) adjusts the angle of the camshaft according to the instructions from the engine control module (ECM) by changing the oil pressure to the camshaft adjuster (mechanical type) to ensure that the valves open and close at the best time. The function of the camshaft position (CMP) sensor is to transmit the camshaft position (relative position of the valve) to the electronic control unit (ECU) in the form of a voltage signal. This fault code indicates that the A (intake/left/front) camshaft position (CMP) sensor circuit is wrong. The causes of the fault include the camshaft position (CMP) sensor circuit, connector, its own fault, or electronic control module (PCM or ECM) fault, etc.

des: Exhaust Pressure Control Valve A Stuck Closed
knowledge: The exhaust pressure control valve is a variable position valve. Its main function is to help the engine heat up quickly by changing the exhaust pressure (boosting engine load) when the outside temperature is extremely low (<5 degrees Celsius). This fault code indicates that the exhaust pressure control valve A is stuck in the closed position.

des: Knock Sensor 4 Circuit Intermittent (Bank 2)
knowledge: The knock sensor is responsible for detecting vibrations when the engine speed changes. The knock sensor then expresses this vibration in the form of voltage. When necessary, the electronic control module (ECU) will delay the ignition to prevent knocking. If this voltage changes suddenly, this fault code will appear.

des: Serial Communication Link
knowledge: The Electronic Control Unit (ECU) has detected an internal error involving the serial communication connection. Causes include a malfunction of the Electronic Control Module (PCM or ECM) or a short circuit in the Controller Area Network (CAN) data line.

des: Drive Motor A Current Sensor Circuit
knowledge: Internal malfunction of the hybrid vehicle electronic control unit (HV ECU).

des: Hybrid Battery Voltage Sense L Circuit Range/Performance
knowledge: The function of the hybrid battery voltage monitoring circuit is to transmit the battery block voltage to the control module to monitor the charging and discharging of the battery block, as well as possible short circuits and open circuits.

des: Generator Temperature Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
knowledge: The starter/generator of a hybrid vehicle is the same motor, usually located in the transmission. Causes of failure include the generator temperature sensor, circuit, connector, control module, etc.

des: Hybrid Battery Temperature Sensor B Circuit Low
knowledge: The battery control module controls the battery fan on/off based on the signal from the battery temperature sensor. If the battery control module detects that the battery temperature sensor signal circuit voltage is lower than the calibrated minimum value, this fault code will appear.

des: Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Control B position Exceeded Learning Limit
knowledge: A turbocharger uses the inertial force of the exhaust gas discharged by the engine to drive the turbine, which in turn drives the coaxial impeller to increase the intake pressure, thereby increasing the power of the vehicle. A supercharger is an air compressor used to increase the intake air for an internal combustion engine. More intake air provides more oxygen to the engine, allowing the control module to provide more fuel, thereby increasing the output power. The function of the turbo/supercharger boost controller is that when the boost pressure reaches the set value, the air pressure pushes the wastegate actuator (pneumatic mechanical type) to bypass part of the exhaust gas from the turbine, thereby reducing the turbine speed and controlling the boost level. This fault code indicates that the turbo/supercharger boost control B position exceeds the normal range.

des: Cylinder 4 - Fuel Trim at Max Limit
knowledge: Fuel trimming refers to the electronic control unit (ECU) controlling fuel delivery by increasing or decreasing the time the injectors are open to achieve the best air-fuel ratio (14.7:1 air-to-gasoline mass ratio) for the engine. Too rich an air-fuel ratio means too much fuel is delivered, and too lean an air-fuel ratio means too little fuel is delivered. This fault code will appear if fuel trim reaches and stays at the maximum limit for more than a certain period of time.

des: High Voltage Service Disconnect Circuit High
Cruise Control Multi-Function Input A Circuit
knowledge: The cruise control system allows the driver to automatically maintain the vehicle speed without stepping on the accelerator pedal. Faults may include cruise control function switches, circuits, connectors, etc.

des: Crankshaft Position Sensor A Circuit Range/Performance
knowledge: The function of the crankshaft is to convert the up and down motion of the piston into rotational motion. The crankshaft position (CKP) sensor (also called the top dead center sensor) detects the top dead center (TDC) signal, crank angle signal and engine speed signal, and inputs them into the computer, so that the computer can issue the best ignition timing instruction according to the ignition sequence of the cylinders. If the electronic control unit (ECU) detects that the crankshaft sensor A circuit voltage is wrong, this fault code will appear.

des: Transmission Range Display Circuit
PCM/ECM/TCU Internal Temperature Sensor B Circuit Low
knowledge: The engine control module, also called the engine control unit (the engine control module and transmission control module on some cars are integrated into the powertrain control module), controls the operation of the entire engine. Its most important function is to control the optimal fuel injection amount and ignition timing of the engine. Another important function is to monitor the components responsible for exhaust emission control. The transmission control module (TCM or TCU) collects information from various sensors and the engine control module to help the transmission decide when and how to shift gears, so that the car can improve performance, shift smoothly, and save fuel. This fault code indicates that the voltage of the temperature sensor signal circuit inside the control module exceeds the maximum range of calibration. The cause of the fault is the internal temperature sensor, circuit, connector, or control module.

des: Traction Control Input Signal Low
knowledge: The function of the drive anti-skid traction control (TCS) system is to control the torque output by delaying the ignition time, shifting up early, starting in second gear, preventing the torque converter from locking, and braking to prevent skidding when the drive wheel slips.

des: Evaporative Emission System Purge Control Valve Circuit
knowledge: The evaporative emissions (EVAP) system directs gasoline vapor from the fuel tank into a tank containing activated carbon that absorbs gasoline vapor. The engine then uses fresh air to purge the gasoline vapor into the engine combustion chamber. This fault code will appear if the electronic control unit (ECU) detects that the voltage of the evaporative emission system purge solenoid valve control circuit is out of the normal calibration range. Fault causes include evaporative emission system purge actuator circuit failure, purge control valve failure, electronic control module (PCM or ECM) failure, etc.

des: Knock Sensor 1 Circuit High (Bank 1 or Single Sensor)
knowledge: The knock sensor is responsible for detecting vibrations when the engine speed changes. The knock sensor then expresses this vibration in the form of voltage. When necessary, the electronic control module (ECU) will delay the ignition to avoid knocking. If this voltage is higher than the calibrated maximum value, this fault code will appear. Fault causes include faults in the knock sensor circuit, loose knock sensor, faults in the knock sensor itself, incorrect fuel grade used, loose engine module parts, and faults in the electronic control module (PCM or ECM).

des: Ignition Coil H Primary/Secondary Circuit
knowledge: The function of the ignition coil is to convert the 12 volt voltage of the car battery into thousands or even tens of thousands of volts required for spark plug ignition. There are two sets of coils in the ignition coil, the primary coil and the secondary coil. The primary coil has thicker enameled wire and fewer turns; the secondary coil uses thinner enameled wire and has relatively more turns. When the primary coil is connected to the power supply, a strong magnetic field is generated around it as the current increases, and the iron core stores the magnetic field energy; when the switch device disconnects the primary coil circuit, the magnetic field of the primary coil decays rapidly, and the secondary coil will induce a high voltage. The electronic control unit (ECU) continuously monitors each ignition main circuit. If the ECU does not receive a valid ignition diagnostic monitor (IDM) pulse signal from the ignition module (integrated in the ECU), this fault code will appear. The causes of the fault include ignition start/run circuit, ignition coil circuit, ignition coil itself, electronic control module (PCM or ECM) failure, etc.

des: Fuel Composition Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
knowledge: The function of the fuel composition sensor is to transmit the ethanol content in gasoline to the electronic control unit (ECU) in the form of an electrical signal as a basis for modifying the injector pulse width and ignition timing. If the ECU detects an error in the signal voltage of the fuel composition sensor, this fault code will appear.

des: Motor Electronics Over Temperature
knowledge: The Motor Electronics Coolant Temperature (MECT) sensor indicates that the system is in an overtemperature condition. Faults may result from a fault in the MECT sensor circuit, connector, or sensor itself; a fault in the motor electronics cooling system; or a fault in the DC/DC converter.

des: Turbocharger/Supercharger Bypass Valve Control Circuit
knowledge: A turbocharger uses the inertial force of the exhaust gas discharged by the engine to drive the turbine, which in turn drives the coaxial impeller to increase the intake pressure, thereby increasing the power of the car. A supercharger is an air compressor used to increase the intake air for an internal combustion engine. More intake air provides more oxygen to the engine, allowing the control module to provide more fuel, thereby increasing the output power. The function of the supercharger bypass valve is to open the bypass valve to release part of the high-pressure air when the boost pressure is too high, thereby protecting the supercharger and the engine. This fault code indicates that the voltage of the turbine/supercharger bypass valve control circuit exceeds the normal range of calibration.

des: Shift Time Too Long
O2 Sensor Circuit High Voltage (Bank 2, Sensor 3)
knowledge: The function of the oxygen sensor is to measure the oxygen content in the engine exhaust to correct the injection amount so that the engine can obtain the best air-fuel ratio. In the OBD fault code, you will often see the oxygen sensor in the row. The first row refers to the row where cylinder 1 is located, and the remaining row is the second row. Regardless of which row, the first sensor always refers to the upstream oxygen sensor (before the catalyst box), and the second sensor always refers to the downstream oxygen sensor (after the catalyst box). This fault code will appear when the voltage of the heated oxygen sensor signal is continuously higher than 1.5 volts within a set period of time. The causes of the fault include the oxygen sensor signal circuit shorting to the positive pole, the oxygen sensor itself is faulty, and the electronic control module (PCM or ECM) is faulty, etc.

des: Camshaft Position Sensor A Circuit Intermittent (Bank 2)
knowledge: The function of the camshaft is to control the opening and closing of the valves. In the variable valve timing system, the electronic camshaft adjustment valve (or oil control valve, OCV) adjusts the angle of the camshaft according to the instructions from the engine control module (ECM) by changing the oil pressure to the camshaft adjuster (mechanical type) to ensure that the valves open and close at the best time. The function of the camshaft position (CMP) sensor is to transmit the camshaft position (relative position of the valve) to the electronic control unit (ECU) in the form of a voltage signal. If the electronic control unit (ECU) detects that the A (intake/left/front) camshaft position (CMP) sensor signal is unstable within the set time period, this fault code will appear.

des: Shift Solenoid E Performance/Stuck Off
knowledge: The shift solenoid valve controls the hydraulic pressure to the transmission clutch by opening or closing the transmission fluid control valve to control its separation and engagement, thereby achieving gear shifting. The causes of this fault code include low transmission fluid level, dirty transmission fluid, mechanical failure of the shift solenoid valve, circuit, connector, or transmission control module (TCM) failure, etc.

des: Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Control A Circuit High
knowledge: A turbocharger uses the inertial force of the exhaust gas discharged by the engine to drive the turbine, which in turn drives the coaxial impeller to increase the intake pressure, thereby increasing the power of the vehicle. A supercharger is an air compressor used to increase the intake air for an internal combustion engine. More intake air provides more oxygen to the engine, allowing the control module to provide more fuel, thereby increasing the output power. The function of the turbo/supercharger boost controller is that when the boost pressure reaches the set value, the air pressure pushes the wastegate actuator (pneumatic mechanical type) to bypass part of the exhaust gas from the turbine, thereby reducing the turbine speed and controlling the boost level. This fault code indicates that the turbo/supercharger boost control circuit voltage is higher than the calibrated maximum value.

des: Cold Start B Camshaft Position Timing Over-Advanced (Bank 2)
knowledge: The function of the camshaft is to control the opening and closing of the valve. When the cold engine is started, if the electronic control unit (ECU) detects that the B (exhaust/right/rear) camshaft timing exceeds the maximum setting value or is always in the advanced state, this fault code will appear.

des: Auto Configuration Engine Coolant Temperature Input Not Present
knowledge: The engine coolant temperature (ECT) sensor transmits the temperature of the engine coolant to the electronic control unit (ECU) in the form of an electrical signal through the principle of thermistor, which serves as a basis for correcting injection and ignition.

des: Hybrid Battery Positive Contactor Control Circuit/Open
knowledge: The System Main Relay (SMR) is responsible for turning the high voltage power supply on and off. If the Hybrid ECU detects a fault in the 2nd System Main Relay (SMR), this fault code will appear.

des: Cylinder 3 - Fuel Trim at Min Limit
knowledge: Fuel trimming refers to the electronic control unit (ECU) controlling fuel delivery by increasing or decreasing the time the injectors are open to achieve the best air-fuel ratio (14.7:1 air-to-gasoline mass ratio) for the engine. Too rich an air-fuel ratio means too much fuel is delivered, and too lean an air-fuel ratio means too little fuel is delivered. This fault code will appear if fuel trim reaches and stays at the minimum limit for more than a certain period of time.

des: Mass or Volume Air Flow A Circuit
knowledge: The function of the mass air flow (MAF) sensor is to convert the air flow into an electrical signal and send it to the electronic control unit (ECU) as one of the basic signals for determining the amount of fuel injection. If the ECU detects that the signal voltage of the mass air flow (MAF) sensor exceeds the normal calibrated range, this fault code will appear.

des: Injection Pump Fuel Metering Control B Range/Performance (Cam/Rotor/Injector)
knowledge: The causes of the fault include the fuel control actuator (FCA), its circuit, the fuel injection pump, or the electronic control module (ECU). The fuel control actuator (FCA) is usually located on the back side of the fuel injection pump. It is an electronically controlled solenoid valve. The ECU controls the amount of fuel entering the fuel injection pump by cycling the FCA open and closed.

des: Generator Temperature Sensor Circuit Low
knowledge: The starter/generator of a hybrid vehicle is the same motor, usually located in the transmission. Causes of failure include the generator temperature sensor, circuit, connector, control module, etc.

des: Hybrid System Performance
Unable to Engage Reverse
Camshaft Position Sensor B Circuit Intermittent (Bank 2)
knowledge: The function of the camshaft is to control the opening and closing of the valves. In the variable valve timing system, the electronic camshaft adjustment valve (or oil control valve, OCV) adjusts the angle of the camshaft according to the command from the engine control module (ECM) by changing the oil pressure to the camshaft adjuster (mechanical type) to ensure that the valves open and close at the best time. The function of the camshaft position (CMP) sensor is to transmit the camshaft position (relative position of the valve) to the electronic control unit (ECU) in the form of a voltage signal. If the electronic control unit (ECU) detects a sudden change in the voltage of the camshaft sensor B circuit, this fault code will appear.

des: Generator Voltage Sense Circuit Range/Performance
knowledge: The generator voltage monitoring circuit is used to transmit the generator voltage signal to the electronic control unit (ECU) as a reference for controlling the charging speed and determining whether the generator is working properly. This fault code indicates that the electronic control unit (ECU) has detected an error in the generator voltage monitoring circuit. The causes of the fault include the generator voltage monitoring circuit, the generator, or the ECU.

des: TCU Power Relay Sense Circuit High
knowledge: The transmission control module (TCM or TCU) collects information from various sensors and the engine control module to help the transmission decide when and how to shift gears, so that the car can improve performance, shift smoothly, and save fuel. The function of the control module relay is to continue to keep the control module powered after the ignition switch is turned off until the control module completes the shutdown process.

des: Camshaft Position Sensor B Circuit Range/Performance (Bank 1)
knowledge: The function of the camshaft is to control the opening and closing of the valves. In the variable valve timing system, the electronic camshaft adjustment valve (or oil control valve, OCV) adjusts the angle of the camshaft according to the command from the engine control module (ECM) by changing the oil pressure to the camshaft adjuster (mechanical type) to ensure that the valves open and close at the best time. The function of the camshaft position (CMP) sensor is to transmit the camshaft position (relative position of the valve) to the electronic control unit (ECU) in the form of a voltage signal. This fault code indicates that the B (exhaust/right/rear) camshaft position (CMP) sensor circuit is wrong. The causes of the fault include the camshaft position (CMP) sensor circuit, connector, its own fault, or electronic control module (PCM or ECM) fault, etc.

des: Cylinder 5 - Fuel Trim at Min Limit
knowledge: Fuel trimming refers to the electronic control unit (ECU) controlling fuel delivery by increasing or decreasing the time the injectors are open to achieve the best air-fuel ratio (14.7:1 air-to-gasoline mass ratio) for the engine. Too rich an air-fuel ratio means too much fuel is delivered, and too lean an air-fuel ratio means too little fuel is delivered. This fault code will appear if fuel trim reaches and stays at the minimum limit for more than a certain period of time.

des: Manifold Absolute Pressure/Barometric Pressure Circuit
knowledge: The function of the Manifold Absolute Pressure (MAP) sensor is to measure the pressure (vacuum) in the intake manifold. The powertrain control module (PCM) then uses the difference between the intake manifold pressure and the atmospheric pressure (which is linearly related to the engine load) as a basis for determining the basic injection amount of the injector to help the engine achieve the best air-fuel ratio under different loads. The atmospheric pressure sensor (sometimes called the high altitude compensator, HAC) is used to transmit the atmospheric pressure to the electronic control module in the form of an electrical signal. Atmospheric pressure varies with weather and altitude. The lower the pressure, the thinner the air. The powertrain control module (PCM) will correct the fuel supply based on the atmospheric pressure value to help the engine achieve the best air-fuel ratio. If the electronic control unit (ECU) detects that the manifold absolute pressure (MAP) sensor/barometric pressure sensor signal voltage is out of the normal range of calibration, this fault code will appear.

des: Cylinder 1 Glow Plug Circuit/Open
knowledge: The function of the glow plug is to heat the compressed gas in the diesel engine combustion chamber through the electric heating coil, so that the diesel engine can be started easily in cold weather. The glow plug control module can automate the preheating and cycling process of the glow plug. If the electronic control unit (ECU) detects a fault in the cylinder 1 glow plug circuit, this fault code will appear.

des: Auto Shift Manual Control Circuit Low
knowledge: Automatic shift manual transmissions allow the driver to put the transmission into manual mode and manually control upshifts or downshifts.

des: Drive Motor B Temperature Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
knowledge: The temperature sensor circuit of the drive motor B is faulty. The causes of the fault include the circuit, connector, electronic control unit, drive motor, etc. The drive motor temperature sensor of some vehicles is integrated with the drive motor. Therefore, if it is determined that the problem is with the temperature sensor itself, it may be necessary to replace the entire drive motor.

des: 2-3 Shift
knowledge: The Electronic Control Unit (ECU) commanded a 2-3 shift, but no corresponding drop in engine speed was detected. Causes include shift solenoid 1 failure, shift solenoid 2 failure, transmission friction material failure, or other transmission internal failures.

des: Traction Control Input Signal
knowledge: The function of the drive anti-skid traction control (TCS) system is to control the torque output by delaying the ignition time, shifting up early, starting in second gear, preventing the torque converter from locking, and braking to prevent skidding when the drive wheel slips.

des: Low Fuel Pressure - Forced Limited Power
knowledge: The fuel system needs to maintain a constant pressure. If the oil pressure is too low, the injector will spray too weakly or not at all. If the oil pressure is too high, the oil circuit or injector will be damaged. This fault code indicates that the electronic control unit (ECU) has detected that the fuel pressure is too low, and the engine power output has decreased. Low pressure may be caused by problems such as the fuel pump, fuel pump control module, fuel pressure regulator, fuel pressure sensor, fuel leakage, etc.

des: Injection Pump Fuel Metering Control B Low (Cam/Rotor/Injector)
knowledge: The causes of the fault include the fuel control actuator (FCA), its circuit, the fuel injection pump, or the electronic control module (ECU). The fuel control actuator (FCA) is usually located on the back side of the fuel injection pump. It is an electronically controlled solenoid valve. The ECU controls the amount of fuel entering the fuel injection pump by cycling the FCA open and closed.

des: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch B Circuit High
knowledge: In the electronic throttle control (ETC) system, the accelerator pedal position (APP) sensor transmits the position of the accelerator pedal to the throttle control module in the form of an electrical signal, which serves as a reference for the throttle actuator to control the throttle valve opening. This fault code indicates that the throttle pedal position sensor B circuit voltage is continuously higher than the calibrated maximum value (4.65 volts) within a set period of time. Fault causes include sensor interface failure, circuit short circuit to the positive pole, sensor failure, electronic control module (PCM or ECM) failure, etc.

des: Hybrid Battery Pack Air Flow Valve A Control Circuit Low
Starter Disable Circuit Low
Shift Solenoid C Control Circuit Low
knowledge: The shift solenoid valve controls the hydraulic pressure to the transmission clutch by opening or closing the transmission fluid control valve to control its separation and engagement, thereby achieving gear shifting. The causes of this fault code include low transmission fluid level, dirty transmission fluid, mechanical failure of the shift solenoid valve, circuit, connector, or transmission control module (TCM) failure, etc.

des: Hydraulic Pump Relay Circuit/Open
Cylinder 9 Contribution/Balance
knowledge: The Electronic Control Unit (ECU) has detected that the crankshaft acceleration contribution of the 9th cylinder is lower than the calibrated value. Fault causes include the 9th cylinder injection system; or other engine problems affecting the 9th cylinder.

des: Hybrid Battery Pack Current Sensor A Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
knowledge: The battery control module monitors the charge and discharge of the battery through the signal from the battery current sensor. If the control module finds that the battery current sensor signal circuit is faulty, this fault code will appear.

des: Hybrid Battery Voltage Sense A Circuit High
knowledge: The function of the hybrid battery voltage monitoring circuit is to transmit the battery block voltage to the control module to monitor the charging and discharging of the battery block, as well as possible short circuits and open circuits.

des: Hybrid Battery Temperature Sensor A Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
knowledge: The battery control module controls the battery fan on/off based on the signal from the battery temperature sensor. If the battery control module detects a sudden change in the voltage of the battery temperature sensor signal circuit, this fault code will appear.

des: Fuel Level Sensor A Circuit Low
knowledge: The fuel level sensor uses a float and variable resistor in the fuel tank to transmit the fuel level in the tank to the electronic control module in the form of an electrical signal. If the electronic control unit (ECU) finds that the fuel level input signal is lower than the calibrated minimum value, this fault code will appear.

des: Charge Air Temperature/Intake Air Temperature Correlation (Bank 2)
knowledge: The turbocharger uses the inertial force of the exhaust gas discharged by the engine to drive the turbine, which in turn drives the coaxial impeller to pressurize the intake air, thereby increasing the power of the vehicle. If the ECU detects that the difference between the charge air temperature sensor and the intake air temperature (IAT) sensor signal exceeds the set maximum value, this fault code will appear.

des: Transmission Park Position Sensor/Switch A Circuit/Open
knowledge: The function of the parking position sensor is to send a signal to the electronic control unit (ECU) indicating whether the shift lever is in the parking position. If the ECU detects that the parking position sensor circuit voltage is out of the normal calibrated range, this fault code will appear.

des: Engine Coolant Temperature/Intake Air Temperature Correlation
