knowledge: The function of the hybrid battery voltage monitoring circuit is to transmit the battery block voltage to the control module to monitor the charging and discharging of the battery block, as well as possible short circuits and open circuits.

des: B Camshaft Profile Control Circuit High (Bank 2)
knowledge: The function of the camshaft is to control the opening and closing of the valves. In the variable valve timing system, the electronic camshaft adjustment valve (or oil control valve, OCV) adjusts the angle of the camshaft according to the instructions from the engine control module (ECM) by changing the oil pressure to the camshaft adjuster (mechanical type) to ensure that the valve opens and closes at the best time. This optimizes the efficiency and power of the engine in all speed ranges. This fault code indicates that the voltage of the B (exhaust/right/rear) camshaft profile control circuit is higher than the calibrated maximum value.

des: TCU Power Relay Control Circuit/Open
knowledge: The transmission control module (TCM or TCU) collects information from various sensors and the engine control module to help the transmission decide when and how to shift gears, so that the car can improve performance, shift smoothly, and save fuel. The function of the control module relay is to continue to keep the control module powered after the ignition switch is turned off until the control module completes the shutdown process.

des: Cylinder 6 Injection Timing
knowledge: The function of the fuel injector is to atomize the fuel so that it meets the requirements of combustion. The working principle is that when the electromagnetic coil is energized, suction is generated, the needle valve is sucked up, the spray hole is opened, and the fuel is sprayed out at high speed through the annular gap between the needle pin at the head of the needle valve and the spray hole to form a mist. The electronic control unit controls the injection amount by controlling the time interval (also called pulse width) of the injector opening. If the electronic control unit (ECU) detects that the actual timing of the injector deviates from the ideal injection timing by more than the maximum limit, this fault code will appear.

des: Shift Timing Solenoid B Intermittent
knowledge: The shift solenoid valve controls the hydraulic pressure to the transmission clutch by opening or closing the transmission fluid control valve to control its separation and engagement, thereby achieving gear shifting. The causes of this fault code include low transmission fluid level, dirty transmission fluid, mechanical failure of the shift solenoid valve, circuit, connector, or transmission control module (TCM) failure, etc.

des: Exhaust Pressure Sensor B Circuit High
knowledge: The exhaust pressure sensor is used to transmit the exhaust system pressure to the electronic control unit (ECU) in the form of an electrical signal. If the ECU detects that the exhaust pressure sensor A signal circuit voltage is higher than 4.95 volts within a set period of time (2.5 seconds), this fault code will appear.

des: Battery Energy Control Module Requested MIL Illumination
knowledge: The malfunction indicator light (MIL), also known as the check engine light, illuminates a yellow or red engine symbol on the instrument panel when the control module detects a malfunction.

des: Cylinder 2 Misfire Detected
knowledge: Cylinder misfire refers to the phenomenon that the mixture cannot burn normally in the cylinder due to various reasons during the operation of the engine. If the electronic control unit (ECU) detects a misfire that may damage the catalytic converter, the fault indicator light will flash and the engine should be turned off immediately. This fault code indicates that the electronic control unit (ECU) has detected a misfire in cylinder 2. The causes of the fault include ignition system failure, fuel delivery failure, air leakage in the intake manifold or EGR, PCV, mechanical cylinder failure, etc.

des: Hybrid Battery Voltage Sense K Circuit
knowledge: The function of the hybrid battery voltage monitoring circuit is to transmit the battery block voltage to the control module to monitor the charging and discharging of the battery block, as well as possible short circuits and open circuits.

des: Generator Position Sensor Circuit B High
knowledge: The causes of the fault include the generator position sensor circuit, connector, or sensor itself; hybrid vehicle generator; hybrid vehicle electronic control unit (HV ECU).

des: Cylinder 12 Glow Plug Incorrect
knowledge: The function of the glow plug is to heat the compressed gas in the diesel engine combustion chamber through the electric heating coil, so that the diesel engine can be started easily in cold weather. The glow plug control module can automate the preheating and cycling process of the glow plug. This fault code indicates that there is an error in the cylinder 12 glow plug, its circuit, connector, or the glow plug control module (GPCM).

des: Engine Mount B Control Circuit Low
knowledge: Automobile electronically controlled suspension can adjust the suspension hardness, damping, and vehicle height according to driving needs, thereby improving the vehicle's form stability and handling.

des: Hybrid Battery Voltage Sense V Circuit
knowledge: The function of the hybrid battery voltage monitoring circuit is to transmit the battery block voltage to the control module to monitor the charging and discharging of the battery block, as well as possible short circuits and open circuits.

des: B Camshaft Profile Control Stuck On (Bank 2)
knowledge: The function of the camshaft is to control the opening and closing of the valves. In the variable valve timing system, the electronic camshaft adjustment valve (or oil control valve, OCV) adjusts the angle of the camshaft according to the instructions from the engine control module (ECM) by changing the oil pressure to the camshaft adjuster (mechanical type) to ensure that the valves open and close at the best time. This optimizes the efficiency and power of the engine in all speed ranges. This fault code indicates that the B (exhaust/right/rear) camshaft profile control has failed or is stuck in the open position.

des: Sensor Reference Voltage C Circuit Low
knowledge: The electronic control unit (ECU) has detected an error in the 5 volt reference voltage circuit C. Causes of the fault include a short circuit or short circuit from the 5 volt reference voltage circuit to a sensor, a short circuit or open circuit in one or more sensors, the ECU, etc.

des: Gear Shift Position Circuit Intermittent
knowledge: Shift position (monitors the shift lever forward/reverse position, odd/even gear) circuit fault.

des: Engine Coolant Temperature Sensor 1 Circuit High
knowledge: The engine coolant temperature (ECT) sensor transmits the temperature of the engine coolant in the form of an electrical signal to the electronic control unit (ECU) through the principle of thermistor, as a basis for correcting injection and ignition. If the ECU detects that the engine coolant temperature (ECT) sensor signal is higher than the maximum value of the self-test (4.6 volts or -50 degrees Celsius), this fault code will appear. The causes of the fault include ECT sensor short circuit to the positive pole, sensor failure, electronic control module (PCM or ECM) failure, etc.

des: VIN Not Programmed or Incompatible - TCU
knowledge: The Transmission Control Module (TCM or TCU) collects information from various sensors and the Engine Control Module to help the transmission decide when and how to shift gears, allowing the vehicle to improve performance, shift smoothly, and save fuel.

des: System Too Rich (Bank 1)
knowledge: Fuel trimming refers to the electronic control unit (ECU) controlling fuel delivery by increasing or decreasing the injector opening time to achieve the best air-fuel ratio (14.7:1 air-to-gasoline mass ratio) for the engine. Too rich an air-fuel ratio means too much fuel is delivered, and too lean an air-fuel ratio means too little fuel is delivered. This fault code will appear if the adaptive fuel control system has reached its compensation limit and the air-fuel ratio is still rich. Causes include intake air flow sensor or manifold absolute pressure (MAP) sensor failure, high fuel pressure, fuel pressure regulator failure, injector failure, oxygen sensor failure, camshaft timing error, oil overfill, evaporative emission system error, electronic control module (PCM or ECM) failure, etc.

des: Hybrid Battery Negative Contactor Circuit
knowledge: The System Main Relay (SMR) is responsible for turning the high voltage power supply on and off. If the 3rd System Main Relay (SMR) gets stuck, it may cause the high voltage system to not shut down. Therefore, if the hybrid vehicle electronic control unit detects a fault in any of these relays, it will terminate the entire system.

des: Fuel Rail Pressure Sensor A Circuit Range/Performance
knowledge: The fuel pressure regulator uses a spring-loaded valve to return excess gasoline to the tank, thereby maintaining constant pressure in the fuel line. There is a vacuum tube on the fuel pressure regulator that is connected to the intake manifold to provide the appropriate gasoline pressure under different engine operating conditions (engine load is determined by the vacuum level). Most cars have the fuel pressure regulator located on the fuel rail, but some cars have the fuel pressure regulator located inside the fuel tank. The fuel pressure sensor is responsible for measuring the fuel pressure near the injector. The electronic control unit (ECU) uses this signal to adjust the injector pulse width and measure the amount of fuel entering the combustion chamber. The electronic control unit (ECU) monitors the reference voltage of the fuel rail pressure sensor. If this voltage is out of the normal range for a set period of time, this fault code will appear.

des: Sensor Power Supply A Circuit High
Fuel Cooler Pump Control Circuit High
knowledge: The function of the fuel cooler is to reduce the fuel temperature and thus increase the viscosity of low-sulfur diesel. This fault code indicates that the voltage of the fuel cooler pump control circuit is higher than the calibrated maximum value.

des: PCM/ECM/TCU Internal Temperature B Too High
knowledge: The engine control module, also called the engine control unit (the engine control module and the transmission control module are integrated into the powertrain control module on some cars), controls the operation of the entire engine. Its most important function is to control the optimal fuel injection amount and ignition timing of the engine. Another important function is to monitor the components of exhaust emission control. The transmission control module (TCM or TCU) collects information from various sensors and the engine control module to help the transmission decide when and how to shift gears, so that the car can improve performance, shift smoothly, and save fuel.

des: Engine Speed Input Circuit Range/Performance
knowledge: Engine speed (also called input shaft speed) is an important basis for the transmission control module (TCU) to determine gear ratio and shifting. During engine operation, the electronic control unit (ECU) or transmission control module (TCU) detects an invalid engine speed input signal on the CAN high-speed transmission network. The cause of the fault includes the engine speed sensor, circuit, connector, or electronic control unit (ECU).

des: Secondary Air Injection System Switching Valve B Circuit Shorted
knowledge: When the engine is just started, the secondary air injection system oxidizes harmful gases such as hydrocarbons and carbon monoxide by forcing air into the exhaust manifold. This process also accelerates the warming process of the catalytic converter. If the electronic control unit (ECU) detects a short circuit in the secondary air injection system control solenoid valve circuit, this fault code will appear. The causes of the fault include an open circuit or short circuit to the positive pole of the secondary air injection actuator circuit, a switching valve failure, a secondary air injection pump failure, a relay failure, or an electronic control module (PCM or ECM) failure.

des: Fuel Injector Insufficient Flow - Forced Limited Power
knowledge: The function of the fuel injector is to atomize the fuel so that it meets the requirements of combustion. The working principle is that when the electromagnetic coil is energized, suction is generated, the needle valve is sucked up, the spray hole is opened, and the fuel is sprayed out at high speed through the annular gap between the needle pin at the head of the needle valve and the spray hole to form a mist. The electronic control unit controls the injection amount by controlling the time interval (also called pulse width) of the fuel injector opening. This fault code indicates that the engine power is reduced due to insufficient fuel supply. The causes of the fault include fuel pump, oil pressure regulator, fuel leakage, fuel injector and other problems.

des: Crankshaft Position Sensor A Circuit Low
knowledge: The function of the crankshaft is to convert the up and down motion of the piston into rotational motion. The crankshaft position (CKP) sensor (also called the top dead center sensor) detects the top dead center (TDC) signal, crank angle signal and engine speed signal, and inputs them into the computer, so that the computer can issue the best ignition timing instruction according to the ignition sequence of the cylinders. If the electronic control unit (ECU) detects that the crankshaft sensor A circuit voltage is lower than the calibrated minimum value, this fault code will appear.

des: Up and Down Shift Switch Circuit Low
Cylinder 2 Fuel Injector Offset Learning At Max Limit
knowledge: The function of the fuel injector is to atomize the fuel so that it meets the requirements of combustion. The working principle is that when the electromagnetic coil is energized, suction is generated, the needle valve is sucked up, the spray hole is opened, and the fuel is sprayed out at high speed through the annular gap between the needle pin at the head of the needle valve and the spray hole to form a mist. The electronic control unit controls the injection amount by controlling the time interval (also called pulse width) of the injector opening. If the electronic control unit (ECU) detects that the compensation learning of the 2nd cylinder injector has reached the maximum learning limit, this fault code will appear.

des: System Voltage Unstable
knowledge: The electronic control unit has detected a sudden change in system voltage.

des: Exhaust Gas Recirculation B Control Circuit Range/Performance
knowledge: The function of the exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) system is to introduce a small amount of exhaust gas into the intake manifold when the engine is running at high load. The presence of these exhaust gases reduces the temperature and pressure of the combustion chamber, thereby reducing the emission of nitrogen oxide pollutants. If the electronic control unit (ECU) detects an error in the voltage of the exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) valve control circuit, this fault code will appear.

des: Hybrid Battery Voltage Sense I Circuit
knowledge: The function of the hybrid battery voltage monitoring circuit is to transmit the battery block voltage to the control module to monitor the charging and discharging of the battery block, as well as possible short circuits and open circuits.

des: Power Steering Pressure Sensor/Switch Circuit High
knowledge: The power steering pressure (PSP) sensor transmits the power steering load pressure to the electronic control unit (ECU) in the form of a voltage signal based on the principle of a potentiometer. If the load pressure is too large, the ECU will increase the engine idle speed and shut down the air conditioning compressor if necessary to prevent the engine from stalling. If the electronic control unit (ECU) detects that the power steering pressure sensor signal voltage is higher than the highest value of the self-test, this fault code will appear. Fault causes include PSP sensor circuit or short circuit to the positive pole, PSP sensor failure, electronic control module (PCM or ECM) failure, etc.

des: Hybrid Battery Voltage Sense J Circuit High
knowledge: The function of the hybrid battery voltage monitoring circuit is to transmit the battery block voltage to the control module to monitor the charging and discharging of the battery block, as well as possible short circuits and open circuits.

des: Starter/Generator Control Module
knowledge: The starter/generator in a hybrid vehicle is the same motor, usually located inside the transmission. This fault code indicates an internal fault in the starter/generator control module.

des: Hybrid Battery Pack Deterioration
knowledge: The BCM calculates the battery pack resistance by measuring the battery pack voltage and current, and estimates the state of charge by measuring the amperage entering the battery pack. This fault code will appear if the BCM finds that: 1) the resistance of the hybrid battery pack exceeds the normal value; or 2) the difference between the maximum and minimum charge values exceeds the normal value.

des: Exhaust Pressure Sensor A Circuit Range/Performance
knowledge: The exhaust pressure sensor is used to transmit the exhaust system pressure to the electronic control unit (ECU) in the form of an electrical signal. If the ECU detects an error in the exhaust pressure sensor A circuit voltage, this fault code will appear.

des: Drive Motor A Current High
Generator Inverter Temperature Sensor Circuit
knowledge: The function of an inverter is to convert direct current into alternating current.

des: Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch D Circuit Low
knowledge: The shift solenoid valve controls the hydraulic pressure to the transmission clutch by opening or closing the transmission fluid control valve to control its separation and engagement, thereby achieving gear shifting. Accurate control of the transmission fluid pressure is very important for smooth gear shifting. The function of the transmission fluid pressure (TFP) sensor is to transmit the transmission fluid pressure in the form of an electrical signal to the transmission control module (TCU) as a reference for the operation of the transmission fluid pressure control solenoid valve.

des: Brake Switch A/B Correlation
knowledge: The function of the brake switch is to transmit the information of whether the brake pedal is pressed or not in the form of an electrical signal to the electronic control unit (ECU), which serves as an important basis for stopping the cruise control and disengaging the torque converter. The electronic control unit (ECU) detected an incorrect correlation between the brake pedal switch and the brake pedal position switch signal.

des: Hybrid Battery Voltage Sense O Circuit High
knowledge: The function of the hybrid battery voltage monitoring circuit is to transmit the battery block voltage to the control module to monitor the charging and discharging of the battery block, as well as possible short circuits and open circuits.

des: Drive Motor B Phase UVW Circuit High
Transmission Friction Element F Stuck On
O2 Sensor Circuit (Bank 2, Sensor 3)
knowledge: The function of the oxygen sensor is to measure the oxygen content in the engine exhaust to correct the injection amount so that the engine can obtain the best air-fuel ratio. In the OBD fault code, you will often see the oxygen sensor in the row. The first row refers to the row where cylinder 1 is located, and the remaining row is the second row. Regardless of which row, the first sensor always refers to the upstream oxygen sensor (before the catalyst box), and the second sensor always refers to the downstream oxygen sensor (after the catalyst box). If the electronic control unit (ECU) detects a problem with the circuit used to measure the oxygen content in the exhaust gas, this fault code will appear.

des: Generator Field/F Terminal Circuit High
knowledge: The electronic control unit (ECU) controls the generator through the generator start signal circuit. When the generator needs to run, the ECU will send a 5V signal to the voltage regulator through the generator start signal circuit. After receiving this signal, the voltage regulator will start to control the generator field circuit. If the electronic control unit (ECU) finds that the generator load is higher than the normal value, this fault code will appear. The most likely possibility is that the generator is short-circuited to the ground.

des: Cylinder 1 Fuel Injector Offset Learning At Min Limit
knowledge: The function of the fuel injector is to atomize the fuel so that it meets the requirements of combustion. The working principle is that when the electromagnetic coil is energized, suction is generated, the needle valve is sucked up, the spray hole is opened, and the fuel is sprayed out at high speed through the annular gap between the needle pin at the head of the needle valve and the spray hole to form a mist. The electronic control unit controls the injection amount by controlling the time interval (also called pulse width) of the injector opening. If the electronic control unit (ECU) detects that the compensation learning of the 1st cylinder injector has reached the minimum learning limit, this fault code will appear.

des: Drive Motor B Control Module
knowledge: An internal fault has occurred in the motor control module (MCM). Possible causes include the MCM processor, analog-to-digital converter, power supply voltage, serial communication, etc.

des: Cold Start A Camshaft Position Timing Over-Retarded (Bank 2)
knowledge: The function of the camshaft is to control the opening and closing of the valve. When the cold engine is started, if the electronic control unit (ECU) detects that the A (intake/left/front) camshaft timing exceeds the maximum setting value or is always in a lagging state, this fault code will appear.

des: Diesel Intake Air Flow Control Performance
knowledge: The diesel engine intake flow control system forms an effective intake vortex by automatically controlling the throttle opening angle and coordinating with the tangential airway or spiral airway. At the same time, it automatically controls the intensity of the intake vortex, effectively improving the engine's combustion, thereby optimizing the engine's power, economy and other performance indicators.

des: Drive Motor A Inverter Power Supply Circuit High
knowledge: The function of an inverter is to convert direct current into alternating current.

des: Shift Solenoid A Performance/Stuck Off
knowledge: The shift solenoid valve controls the hydraulic pressure to the transmission clutch by opening or closing the transmission fluid control valve to control its separation and engagement, thereby achieving gear shifting. The causes of this fault code include low transmission fluid level, dirty transmission fluid, mechanical failure of the shift solenoid valve, circuit, connector, or transmission control module (TCM) failure, etc.

des: Cruise Control Multi-Function Input B Circuit
knowledge: The cruise control system allows the driver to automatically maintain the vehicle speed without stepping on the accelerator pedal. Faults may include the cruise control multi-function input switch, circuit, connector, etc.

des: Auto Shift Manual Control Circuit High
knowledge: Automatic shift manual transmissions allow the driver to put the transmission into manual mode and manually control upshifts or downshifts.

des: Drive Motor Inverter Temperature Sensor B Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
knowledge: The inverter converts DC power into AC power. The hybrid electronic control unit (HV ECU) uses a temperature sensor integrated in the inverter to monitor the temperature of the drive motor inverter. If the output of this temperature sensor is abnormal, this fault code will appear.

des: Hybrid Battery Pack Cooling Fan 3 Control Circuit Low
knowledge: The fan motor controller is responsible for regulating the voltage of the hybrid battery pack cooling fan. If the cooling fan 1 control circuit voltage falls below the calibrated minimum value, this fault code will appear.

des: Knock Sensor 1 Circuit (Bank 1 or Single Sensor)
knowledge: The knock sensor is responsible for detecting vibrations when the engine speed changes. The knock sensor then expresses this vibration in the form of voltage. When necessary, the electronic control module (ECU) will delay the ignition to avoid knocking. If this voltage is out of the calibration range, this fault code will appear. Fault causes include faults in the knock sensor circuit, connector, itself, or electronic control module (PCM or ECM) failure.

des: Cylinder 2 Injector Circuit High
knowledge: The function of the fuel injector is to atomize the fuel so that it meets the requirements of combustion. The working principle is that when the electromagnetic coil is energized, suction is generated, the needle valve is sucked up, the spray hole is opened, and the fuel is sprayed out at high speed through the annular gap between the needle pin at the head of the needle valve and the spray hole to form a mist. The electronic control unit controls the injection amount by controlling the time interval (also called pulse width) of the injector opening. If the voltage of the second cylinder injector control circuit is higher than the calibrated maximum value, this fault code will appear. The causes of the fault include the injector control circuit, connector, or the injector itself; injector control module (FICM).

des: Hybrid Battery C Voltage
Cylinder 6 Glow Plug Incorrect
knowledge: The function of the glow plug is to heat the compressed gas in the diesel engine combustion chamber through the electric heating coil, so that the diesel engine can be started easily in cold weather. The glow plug control module can automate the preheating and cycling process of the glow plug. This fault code indicates that there is an error in the cylinder 6 glow plug, its circuit, connector, or the glow plug control module (GPCM).

des: Torque Converter Clutch Circuit Intermittent
knowledge: The torque converter acts like a clutch in a manual transmission, allowing the torque from the engine to be temporarily disconnected from the transmission, allowing for smooth gear changes. However, the difference is that the torque converter can also increase the torque like a downshift. The torque converter clutch (TCC) solenoid circuit, connector, or solenoid itself is faulty. A control module fault may also cause this fault code to appear.

des: Shift Solenoid G Stuck On
knowledge: The shift solenoid valve controls the hydraulic pressure to the transmission clutch by opening or closing the transmission fluid control valve to control its separation and engagement, thereby achieving gear shifting. The causes of this fault code include low transmission fluid level, dirty transmission fluid, mechanical failure of the shift solenoid valve, circuit, connector, or transmission control module (TCM) failure, etc.

des: Injector Circuit/Open - Cylinder 1
knowledge: The function of the fuel injector is to atomize the fuel so that it meets the requirements of combustion. The working principle is that when the electromagnetic coil is energized, suction is generated, the needle valve is sucked up, the spray hole is opened, and the fuel is sprayed out at high speed through the annular gap between the needle pin at the head of the needle valve and the spray hole to form a mist. The electronic control unit controls the injection amount by controlling the time interval (also called pulse width) of the injector opening. If the electronic control unit (ECU) detects that the injector control circuit is low when it should be high, or high when it should be low, this fault code will appear. The causes of the fault include the injector interface, circuit fault, injector fault itself, electronic control module (PCM or ECM) fault, etc.

des: Clutch Pedal Switch B Circuit Low
knowledge: The function of the clutch pedal switch is to transmit the information of whether the clutch is pressed to the electronic control unit in the form of an electrical signal, which serves as an important parameter for controlling the engine start and cruise control system.

des: Cylinder 7 Injector Circuit Range/Performance
knowledge: The function of the fuel injector is to atomize the fuel so that it meets the requirements of combustion. The working principle is that when the electromagnetic coil is energized, suction is generated, the needle valve is sucked up, the spray hole is opened, and the fuel is sprayed out at high speed through the annular gap between the needle pin at the head of the needle valve and the spray hole to form a mist. The electronic control unit controls the injection amount by controlling the time interval (also called pulse width) of the injector opening. If the electronic control unit (ECU) detects an error in the injector circuit of the 7th cylinder, this fault code will appear.

des: Drive Motor A Position Sensor Circuit A Low
Cylinder 4 Glow Plug Circuit/Open
knowledge: The function of the glow plug is to heat the compressed gas in the diesel engine combustion chamber through the electric heating coil, so that the diesel engine can be started easily in cold weather. The glow plug control module can automate the preheating and cycling process of the glow plug. If the electronic control unit (ECU) detects a fault in the cylinder 4 glow plug circuit, this fault code will appear.

des: Cylinder 4 Injection Timing
knowledge: The function of the fuel injector is to atomize the fuel so that it meets the requirements of combustion. The working principle is that when the electromagnetic coil is energized, suction is generated, the needle valve is sucked up, the spray hole is opened, and the fuel is sprayed out at high speed through the annular gap between the needle pin at the head of the needle valve and the spray hole to form a mist. The electronic control unit controls the injection amount by controlling the time interval (also called pulse width) of the injector opening. If the electronic control unit (ECU) detects that the actual timing of the injector deviates from the ideal injection timing by more than the maximum limit, this fault code will appear.

des: Cylinder 6 Misfire Detected
knowledge: Cylinder misfire refers to the phenomenon that the mixture cannot burn normally in the cylinder due to various reasons during the operation of the engine. If the electronic control unit (ECU) detects a misfire that may damage the catalytic converter, the fault indicator light will flash and the engine should be turned off immediately. This fault code indicates that the electronic control unit (ECU) has detected a misfire in cylinder 6. The causes of the fault include ignition system failure, fuel delivery failure, air leakage in the intake manifold or EGR, PCV, mechanical cylinder failure, etc.

des: Knock Sensor 4 Circuit Range/Performance (Bank 2)
knowledge: The knock sensor is responsible for detecting vibrations when the engine speed changes. The knock sensor then expresses this vibration in the form of a voltage. When necessary, the electronic control module (ECU) will delay the ignition to prevent knocking. If this voltage is wrong, this fault code will appear.

des: HO2S Heater Resistance (Bank 2, Sensor 1)
knowledge: The function of the oxygen sensor is to measure the oxygen content in the engine exhaust to correct the injection amount so that the engine can obtain the best air-fuel ratio. In the OBD fault code, you will often see the oxygen sensor in the row. The first row refers to the row where cylinder 1 is located, and the remaining row is the second row. Regardless of which row, the first sensor always refers to the upstream oxygen sensor (before the catalyst box), and the second sensor always refers to the downstream oxygen sensor (after the catalyst box). If the electronic control unit (ECU) detects that the current of the heated oxygen sensor heater control circuit is too low or too high, this fault code will appear.

des: Intake Valve Control Solenoid Circuit Range/Performance (Bank 2)
knowledge: The function of the camshaft is to control the opening and closing of the valves. In the variable valve timing system, the electronic camshaft adjustment valve (or oil control valve, OCV) adjusts the angle of the camshaft according to the instructions from the engine control module (ECM) by changing the oil pressure to the camshaft adjuster (mechanical type) to ensure that the valves open and close at the best time. If the actual position of the A (intake) camshaft differs from the ideal position by more than 20 degrees, this fault code will appear.

des: Internal Control Module Torque Performance
knowledge: The engine control module, also called the engine control unit (the engine control module and the transmission control module on some vehicles are integrated into a powertrain control module), controls the operation of the entire engine. Its most important function is to control the optimal fuel injection amount and ignition timing of the engine. Another important function is to monitor the exhaust emission control components.

des: Hybrid Battery Temperature Sensor D Circuit Low
knowledge: The battery control module controls the battery fan on/off based on the signal from the battery temperature sensor. If the battery control module detects that the battery temperature sensor signal circuit voltage is lower than the calibrated minimum value, this fault code will appear.

des: Secondary Air Injection System Switching Valve A Circuit Low
knowledge: When the engine is just started, the secondary air injection system oxidizes harmful gases such as hydrocarbons and carbon monoxide by forcing air into the exhaust manifold. This process also accelerates the warming process of the catalytic converter. If the voltage of the secondary air injection system switching valve A control circuit is lower than the calibrated minimum value, this fault code will appear.

des: Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch B Circuit Range/Performance
knowledge: The shift solenoid valve controls the hydraulic pressure to the transmission clutch by opening or closing the transmission fluid control valve to control its separation and engagement, thereby achieving gear shifting. Accurate control of the transmission fluid pressure is very important for smooth gear shifting. The function of the transmission fluid pressure (TFP) sensor is to transmit the transmission fluid pressure in the form of an electrical signal to the transmission control module (TCU) as a reference for the operation of the transmission fluid pressure control solenoid valve.

des: Auxiliary Transmission Fluid Pump Motor Phase U Current
knowledge: The function of the transmission fluid pump is to provide working pressure to the transmission fluid when the engine is running. The shift solenoid valve controls the hydraulic pressure to the transmission clutch by opening or closing the transmission fluid control valve to control its separation and combination, thereby achieving gear shifting. The function of the auxiliary transmission fluid pump is to provide pressure to the transmission fluid when the engine is not running (such as when towing) to prevent the transmission from overheating.

des: Drive Motor B Current Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
knowledge: Internal malfunction of the hybrid vehicle electronic control unit (HV ECU).

des: Sensor Power Supply A Circuit Low
Motor Electronics Coolant Temperature Sensor Circuit
knowledge: The Motor Electronics Cooling System (MECS) is an independent system that provides cooling for the transmission (e.g. eCVT) motor, control module and DC/DC converter. It has its own radiator, coolant pump, coolant temperature sensor, etc. The Motor Electronics Coolant Temperature (MECT) sensor uses the principle of thermistor to electronically transmit the temperature of the motor electronics coolant to the electronic control unit (ECU). If the control module detects that the Motor Electronics Coolant Temperature (MECT) sensor signal does not match the temperature signal calculated based on other signals, this fault code will appear.

des: Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch E Circuit Low
knowledge: The shift solenoid valve controls the hydraulic pressure to the transmission clutch by opening or closing the transmission fluid control valve to control its separation and engagement, thereby achieving gear shifting. Accurate control of the transmission fluid pressure is very important for smooth gear shifting. The function of the transmission fluid pressure (TFP) sensor is to transmit the transmission fluid pressure in the form of an electrical signal to the transmission control module (TCU) as a reference for the operation of the transmission fluid pressure control solenoid valve.

des: Shift Solenoid C Electrical
knowledge: The shift solenoid valve controls the hydraulic pressure to the transmission clutch by opening or closing the transmission fluid control valve to control its separation and engagement, thereby achieving gear shifting. The causes of this fault code include low transmission fluid level, dirty transmission fluid, mechanical failure of the shift solenoid valve, circuit, connector, or transmission control module (TCM) failure, etc.

des: Evaporative Emission System
knowledge: The evaporative emissions (EVAP) system directs gasoline vapor from the fuel tank into a tank containing activated carbon that absorbs gasoline vapor. The engine then uses fresh air to purge the gasoline vapor into the engine combustion chamber. If the evaporative emissions system fails, this fault code will appear. Causes include EVAP canister purge valve failure, EVAP canister padding, EVAP line failure, electronic control module (PCM or ECM) failure, etc.

des: Inverter B Cooling System Performance
knowledge: The function of an inverter is to convert direct current into alternating current.

des: Fuel Temperature Sensor A Circuit Range/Performance
knowledge: The fuel temperature sensor is responsible for monitoring the temperature of the fuel leading to the fuel pump to avoid vapor lock caused by excessive temperature (120 degrees Celsius), which may cause damage to the fuel pump or injector. If the electronic control unit (ECU) continuously monitors the fuel temperature sensor signal voltage and exceeds the calibrated normal value for a set period of time, this fault code will appear.

des: Drive Motor B Temperature Sensor Circuit High
knowledge: The temperature sensor circuit of the drive motor B is faulty. The causes of the fault include the circuit, connector, electronic control unit, drive motor, etc. The drive motor temperature sensor of some vehicles is integrated with the drive motor. Therefore, if it is determined that the problem is with the temperature sensor itself, it may be necessary to replace the entire drive motor.

des: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Circuit (Bank 2, Sensor 1)
knowledge: The exhaust temperature sensor transmits the exhaust temperature to the electronic control unit (ECU) in the form of an electrical signal. The exhaust temperature produced by the correct air-fuel ratio is lower than the exhaust temperature produced by an overly rich or lean air-fuel ratio. Excessive exhaust temperature (>160 degrees Celsius) can damage the engine. If the electronic control unit (ECU) finds that the exhaust temperature sensor changes by less than 40 degrees Celsius 10 minutes after the engine is cold started, this fault code will appear.

des: Drive Motor B Current Sensor Circuit High
knowledge: Internal malfunction of the hybrid vehicle electronic control unit (HV ECU).

des: Hybrid Battery Voltage Sense S Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
knowledge: The function of the hybrid battery voltage monitoring circuit is to transmit the battery block voltage to the control module to monitor the charging and discharging of the battery block, as well as possible short circuits and open circuits.

des: ECM/TCU Incompatible
knowledge: The engine control module, also called the engine control unit (in some cars, the engine control module and the transmission control module are integrated into a powertrain control module), controls the operation of the entire engine. Its most important function is to control the optimal fuel injection amount and ignition timing of the engine. Another important function is to monitor the components of exhaust emission control. The transmission control module (TCM or TCU) collects information from various sensors and the engine control module to help the transmission decide when and how to shift gears, so that the car can improve performance, shift smoothly, and save fuel. The causes of the failure include engine control module failure, transmission control module failure, short circuit between the engine control module and the transmission control module, etc.

des: System Voltage
knowledge: The electronic control unit detects that the system voltage is below 10V or above 16V for at least 5 seconds. Causes include alternator failure, battery failure, battery electrode corrosion, fuse failure, voltage regulator failure, etc.

des: Shift Solenoid D Intermittent
knowledge: The shift solenoid valve controls the hydraulic pressure to the transmission clutch by opening or closing the transmission fluid control valve to control its separation and engagement, thereby achieving gear shifting. The causes of this fault code include low transmission fluid level, dirty transmission fluid, mechanical failure of the shift solenoid valve, circuit, connector, or transmission control module (TCM) failure, etc.

des: Ambient Air Temperature Sensor Range/Performance
knowledge: The function of the ambient air temperature sensor is to transmit the external air temperature to the electronic control unit (ECU) in the form of an electrical signal to help the engine achieve the best air-fuel ratio. This fault code indicates that the ambient air temperature sensor signal circuit is wrong.

des: Intake Air Temperature Sensor 1 Circuit Low (Bank 1)
knowledge: The function of the intake air temperature (IAT) sensor is to transmit the engine's intake air temperature to the electronic control unit (ECU) in the form of a voltage signal, providing a reference for injection correction. If the electronic control unit (ECU) detects that the intake air temperature (IAT) sensor signal voltage is lower than the minimum value of the self-test (0.2 volts or 121 degrees Celsius), this fault code will appear. Fault causes include sensor circuit short circuit to ground, sensor failure, electronic control module (PCM or ECM) failure, etc.

des: Auto Shift Manual Mode Circuit Low
knowledge: Automatic shift manual transmissions allow the driver to put the transmission into manual mode and manually control upshifts or downshifts.

des: Hybrid Battery Temperature Sensor A Range/Performance
knowledge: The battery control module controls the opening/closing of the battery fan based on the signal from the battery temperature sensor. If the battery control module detects an error in the battery temperature sensor signal circuit, this fault code will appear.

des: Cylinder 3 Injector Circuit High
knowledge: The function of the fuel injector is to atomize the fuel so that it meets the requirements of combustion. The working principle is that when the electromagnetic coil is energized, suction is generated, the needle valve is sucked up, the spray hole is opened, and the fuel is sprayed out at high speed through the annular gap between the needle pin at the head of the needle valve and the spray hole to form a mist. The electronic control unit controls the injection amount by controlling the time interval (also called pulse width) of the injector opening. If the voltage of the 3rd cylinder injector control circuit is higher than the calibrated maximum value, this fault code will appear. The causes of the fault include the injector control circuit, connector, or the injector itself; injector control module (FICM).

des: Gear Shift Control Module B Communication Circuit
Camshaft Position Sensor A Circuit Low (Bank 2)
knowledge: The function of the camshaft is to control the opening and closing of the valves. In the variable valve timing system, the electronic camshaft adjustment valve (or oil control valve, OCV) adjusts the angle of the camshaft according to the command from the engine control module (ECM) by changing the oil pressure to the camshaft adjuster (mechanical type) to ensure that the valves open and close at the best time. The function of the camshaft position (CMP) sensor is to transmit the camshaft position (relative position of the valve) to the electronic control unit (ECU) in the form of a voltage signal. This fault code indicates that the signal voltage of the A (intake/left/front) camshaft position (CMP) sensor is lower than the calibrated minimum value. The causes of the fault include the camshaft position (CMP) sensor circuit, connector, its own fault, or electronic control module (PCM or ECM) fault, etc.

des: Brake Switch B Circuit
knowledge: The function of the brake switch is to transmit the information of whether the brake pedal is pressed or not in the form of an electrical signal to the electronic control unit (ECU), which is an important basis for stopping the cruise control and disengaging the torque converter. The electronic control unit (ECU) did not receive the input signal change of the brake pedal position (BPP) sensor. The causes of the fault include BPA/BPP switch failure, calibration error, circuit, connector failure, or failure of the electronic module connected to the BPA or BPP.

des: EVAP Purge Flow Sensor Circuit
knowledge: The EVAP system directs gasoline vapors from the fuel tank into a tank containing activated carbon that absorbs gasoline vapors. The engine then uses fresh air to purge these gasoline vapors into the engine combustion chambers. If the Electronic Control Unit (ECU) detects that the EVAP purge flow sensor signal voltage is out of the calibrated normal range, this fault code will appear.

des: Idle Air Control System Circuit Low
knowledge: The Idle Air Control (IAC) valve has a movable needle valve controlled by a precision moving stepper motor. With the throttle closed, the IAC valve controls the idle speed by varying the air flow in the bypass line to suit the idle speed under different conditions. This fault code will appear if the Electronic Control Unit (ECU) detects that the idle air control system circuit voltage is below the calibrated minimum value.

des: Pressure Control Solenoid C Electrical
knowledge: The shift solenoid valve controls the hydraulic pressure to the transmission clutch by opening or closing the transmission fluid control valve to control its separation and engagement, thereby achieving gear shifting. Accurate control of the transmission fluid pressure is very important for smooth gear shifting. The function of the pressure control solenoid valve is to control the pressure of the transmission fluid. Fault causes include low transmission fluid level, dirty transmission fluid, transmission fluid pressure control solenoid valve, circuit, connector, or control module, etc.

des: Shift Solenoid E Electrical
knowledge: The shift solenoid valve controls the hydraulic pressure to the transmission clutch by opening or closing the transmission fluid control valve to control its separation and engagement, thereby achieving gear shifting. The causes of this fault code include low transmission fluid level, dirty transmission fluid, mechanical failure of the shift solenoid valve, circuit, connector, or transmission control module (TCM) failure, etc.

des: Generator Lamp Control Circuit
knowledge: The cause of the fault includes the generator indicator light, circuit, connector, or electronic control unit (ECU)

des: MAP - Mass or Volume Air Flow Correlation (Bank 1)
knowledge: The function of the manifold absolute pressure (MAP) sensor is to measure the pressure (vacuum) in the intake manifold. The powertrain control module (PCM) then uses the difference between the intake manifold pressure and the atmospheric pressure (which is linearly related to the engine load) as a basis for determining the basic injection amount of the injector to help the engine achieve the best air-fuel ratio under different loads. If the ECU finds that the load estimated by the manifold absolute pressure (MAP) sensor and the air flow (MAF) sensor is too different, this fault code will appear.

des: Cruise Control Input Circuit Low
knowledge: The cruise control system allows the driver to automatically maintain the vehicle speed without stepping on the accelerator pedal.

des: Pressure Control Solenoid A Electrical
knowledge: The shift solenoid controls the hydraulic pressure to the transmission clutch by opening or closing the transmission fluid control valve to control its disengagement and engagement, thereby achieving gear shifting. Accurate control of the transmission fluid pressure is very important for smooth gear shifting. The function of the pressure control solenoid valve is to control the pressure of the transmission fluid. Fault causes include the pressure control (PC) solenoid valve circuit, connector, or the solenoid valve itself. A control module fault may also cause this fault code to appear.

des: HO2S Heater Control Circuit Low (Bank 2, Sensor 2)
knowledge: The function of the oxygen sensor is to measure the oxygen content in the engine exhaust to correct the injection amount so that the engine can obtain the best air-fuel ratio. In the OBD fault code, you will often see the oxygen sensor in which bank. Bank 1 refers to the bank where cylinder 1 is located, and the remaining bank is bank 2. Regardless of which bank, the first sensor always refers to the upstream oxygen sensor (before the catalyst box), and the second sensor always refers to the downstream oxygen sensor (after the catalyst box). The electronic control unit (ECU) maintains the temperature of the oxygen sensor at 780oC by controlling the on/off of the oxygen sensor heater. If the control circuit voltage of the heater is lower than the calibrated minimum value, this fault code will appear.

des: Transmission Friction Element G Stuck On
Hydraulic Pump Relay Circuit Low
Cold Start Engine Exhaust Temperature Out of Range
knowledge: The Electronic Control Unit (ECU) estimates the temperature change of the catalytic converter during cold start. If the ECU finds that the ratio of the actual temperature of the catalytic converter to the estimated temperature is outside the normal calibrated range, this fault code will appear. The causes of the fault include the exhaust temperature sensor, its circuit, connector, ECU, etc.

des: Cylinder 11 Injector Circuit High
knowledge: The function of the fuel injector is to atomize the fuel so that it meets the requirements of combustion. The working principle is that when the electromagnetic coil is energized, suction is generated, the needle valve is sucked up, the spray hole is opened, and the fuel is sprayed out at high speed through the annular gap between the needle pin at the head of the needle valve and the spray hole to form a mist. The electronic control unit controls the injection amount by controlling the time interval (also called pulse width) of the injector opening. If the voltage of the 11th cylinder injector control circuit is higher than the calibrated maximum value, this fault code will appear. The causes of the fault include the injector control circuit, connector, or the injector itself; injector control module (FICM).

des: Knock Sensor 1 Circuit Low (Bank 1 or Single Sensor)
knowledge: The knock sensor is responsible for detecting vibrations when the engine speed changes. The knock sensor then expresses this vibration in the form of voltage. When necessary, the electronic control module (ECU) will delay the ignition to avoid knocking. If this voltage is lower than the calibrated minimum value, this fault code will appear. Fault causes include faults in the knock sensor circuit, loose knock sensor, faults in the knock sensor itself, incorrect fuel grade used, loose engine module parts, and faults in the electronic control module (PCM or ECM).

des: Hybrid Battery Voltage Sense W Circuit Low
knowledge: The function of the hybrid battery voltage monitoring circuit is to transmit the battery block voltage to the control module to monitor the charging and discharging of the battery block, as well as possible short circuits and open circuits.

des: Transmission Park Position Sensor/Switch A Circuit Performance/Low
knowledge: The function of the parking position sensor is to send a signal to the electronic control unit (ECU) indicating whether the gear lever is in the parking position. If the ECU detects an error in the parking position sensor circuit, this fault code will appear.

des: Clutch Pedal Switch A Circuit Low
knowledge: The function of the clutch pedal switch is to transmit the information of whether the clutch is pressed to the electronic control unit in the form of an electrical signal, which serves as an important parameter for controlling the engine start and cruise control system.

des: A/C Refrigerant Pressure Sensor A Circuit
knowledge: The function of the air conditioning refrigerant pressure sensor is to transmit the air conditioning refrigerant pressure to the electronic control unit (ECU) in the form of an electrical signal as a basis for controlling the cooling fan switch and the compressor relay. This fault code indicates that the air conditioning refrigerant pressure sensor itself or its circuit is faulty, the powertrain control module (PCM) is faulty, etc.

des: Knock Sensor 3 Circuit (Bank 1)
knowledge: The knock sensor is responsible for detecting vibrations when the engine speed changes. The knock sensor then expresses this vibration in the form of voltage. When necessary, the electronic control module (ECU) will delay the ignition to prevent knocking. If this voltage is out of the calibrated range, this fault code will appear.

des: Drive Motor Inverter Temperature Sensor E Circuit Low
knowledge: The inverter converts DC power into AC power. The hybrid electronic control unit (HV ECU) uses a temperature sensor integrated in the inverter to monitor the temperature of the drive motor inverter. If the output of this temperature sensor is abnormal, this fault code will appear.

des: Knock Sensor 4 Circuit (Bank 2)
knowledge: The knock sensor is responsible for detecting vibrations when the engine speed changes. The knock sensor then expresses this vibration in the form of voltage. When necessary, the electronic control module (ECU) will delay the ignition to prevent knocking. If this voltage is out of the calibrated range, this fault code will appear.

des: O2 Sensor Circuit No Activity Detected (Bank 1, Sensor 3)
knowledge: The function of the oxygen sensor is to measure the oxygen content in the engine exhaust to correct the injection amount so that the engine can obtain the best air-fuel ratio. In the OBD fault code, you will often see the oxygen sensor in the bank. Bank 1 refers to the bank where cylinder 1 is located, and the remaining bank is bank 2. Regardless of which bank, the first sensor always refers to the upstream oxygen sensor (before the catalyst box), and the second sensor always refers to the downstream oxygen sensor (after the catalyst box). The electronic control unit (ECU) continuously monitors the heated oxygen sensor to determine that the oxygen sensor is working. If the heated oxygen sensor signal value continues to stay at the default value, the electronic control unit (ECU) will command an oscillating air/fuel ratio in an attempt to detect some changes in the signal value. If the ECU still cannot detect changes in the sensor signal at this time, this fault code will appear.

des: Hybrid Battery Pack Current Sensor B Circuit
knowledge: The battery control module monitors the charge and discharge of the battery through the signal from the battery current sensor. If the control module finds that the battery current sensor is faulty, this fault code will appear.

des: Turbocharger/Supercharger Bypass Valve Control Circuit Range/Performance
knowledge: A turbocharger uses the inertial force of the exhaust gas discharged by the engine to drive the turbine, which in turn drives the coaxial impeller to increase the intake pressure, thereby increasing the power of the car. A supercharger is an air compressor used to increase the intake air for an internal combustion engine. More intake air provides more oxygen to the engine, allowing the control module to provide more fuel, thereby increasing the output power. The function of the supercharger bypass valve is to open the bypass valve to release part of the high-pressure air when the boost pressure is too high, thereby protecting the supercharger and the engine. This fault code indicates that the turbine/supercharger bypass valve control circuit is wrong.

des: Cylinder 1 Injector Circuit Low
knowledge: The function of the fuel injector is to atomize the fuel so that it meets the requirements of combustion. The working principle is that when the electromagnetic coil is energized, suction is generated, the needle valve is sucked up, the spray hole is opened, and the fuel is sprayed out at high speed through the annular gap between the needle pin at the head of the needle valve and the spray hole to form a mist. The electronic control unit controls the injection amount by controlling the time interval (also called pulse width) of the injector opening. If the voltage of the injector control circuit of the first cylinder is lower than the calibrated minimum value, this fault code will appear. The causes of the fault include the injector control circuit, connector, or the injector itself; injector control module (FICM).

des: Drive Motor Inverter Temperature Sensor B Circuit Range/Performance
knowledge: The inverter converts DC power into AC power. The hybrid electronic control unit (HV ECU) uses a temperature sensor integrated in the inverter to monitor the temperature of the drive motor inverter. If the output of this temperature sensor is abnormal, this fault code will appear.

des: Pressure Control Solenoid B Electrical
knowledge: The shift solenoid valve controls the hydraulic pressure to the transmission clutch by opening or closing the transmission fluid control valve to control its separation and engagement, thereby achieving gear shifting. Accurate control of the transmission fluid pressure is very important for smooth gear shifting. The function of the pressure control solenoid valve is to control the pressure of the transmission fluid. Fault causes include the pressure control solenoid valve control circuit, connector, or the solenoid valve itself. A control module fault will also cause this fault code to appear.

des: Hybrid Battery Pack Current Sensor A Circuit Low
knowledge: The battery control module monitors the charge and discharge of the battery through the signal from the battery current sensor. If the control module finds that the battery current sensor signal circuit voltage is lower than the calibrated minimum value, this fault code will appear.

des: Charge Air Cooler Coolant Pump Control Circuit/Open
knowledge: The turbocharger uses the inertial force of the exhaust gas discharged by the engine to drive the turbine, which in turn drives the coaxial impeller to pressurize the intake air, thereby increasing the power of the car. The charge air cooler (also called the intercooler) is used to cool the supercharged air coming out of the supercharger. After the air passes through the supercharger, the pressure increases and the temperature rises. The charge air cooler can reduce the charge air temperature, thereby increasing the air density and the charging efficiency, so as to achieve the purpose of increasing engine power and reducing emissions. If the coolant pump control circuit of the charge air cooler fails, this fault code will appear.

des: Evaporative Emission System Leak Detected (large leak)
knowledge: The EVAP system directs gasoline vapors from the fuel tank into a tank containing activated charcoal that absorbs the gasoline vapors. The engine then uses fresh air to purge the gasoline vapors into the engine combustion chambers. The engine is running normally, but not at idle. If the ECU detects no purge flow from the EVAP system, it is usually caused by a fuel vapor line obstruction, a large fuel vapor leak, or multiple small fuel vapor leaks.

des: ECM/PCM Power Relay Sense Circuit Low
knowledge: The engine control module, also called the engine control unit (the engine control module and the transmission control module on some vehicles are integrated into a powertrain control module), controls the operation of the entire engine. Its most important function is to control the optimal amount of fuel injection and ignition timing of the engine. Another important function is to monitor the components responsible for exhaust emission control. The function of the engine control module relay is to continue to keep the engine control module powered after the ignition switch is turned off until the engine control module completes the shutdown process. If the passive anti-theft system (PATS) shows that the key is in the ON (run) or START (start) position, and the ignition switch position (ISP-R) circuit shows OFF (off), ACC (accessory), LOCK (lock), this fault code will appear. The causes of the fault include ignition circuit fuse, ignition switch, ISP-R circuit, ECU relay, passive anti-theft system, ECU, etc.

des: Hybrid Battery Positive Contactor Circuit Stuck Closed
knowledge: The System Main Relay (SMR) is responsible for turning the high voltage power supply on and off. If one of the 1st and 2nd System Main Relays (SMR) is stuck, it may cause the high voltage system to not shut down. Therefore, if the hybrid vehicle electronic control unit detects a fault in any of these relays, it will terminate the entire system.

des: Exhaust Gas Recirculation Throttle Control Circuit A Range/Performance
knowledge: The function of the exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) system is to introduce a small amount of exhaust gas into the intake manifold when the engine is running at high load. The presence of these exhaust gases reduces the temperature and pressure of the combustion chamber, thereby reducing the emission of nitrogen oxide pollutants. If the electronic control unit (ECU) receives incorrect information from the intake throttle actuator, such as a large deviation between the actual throttle position and the ideal throttle position, a return spring error, an incorrect input signal, etc., this fault code will appear.

des: Internal Control Module Memory Check Sum Error
knowledge: The causes of the failure include battery electrode corrosion (causing voltage instability), electronic control module circuit failure, reprogramming failure, electronic control module (PCM or ECM) failure, etc.

des: Cruise Control Multi-Function Input A Circuit Low
knowledge: The cruise control system allows the driver to automatically maintain the vehicle speed without stepping on the accelerator pedal. The electronic control unit (ECU) detected that the voltage of the cruise control multi-function input switch A circuit is lower than the calibrated minimum value. The causes of the fault include multi-function switch, circuit, connector, mechanical failure, etc.

des: Coolant Thermostat (Coolant Temperature Below Thermostat Regulating Temperature)
knowledge: The function of the thermostat is to close when the coolant temperature is low, allowing only the coolant to circulate in the engine to increase the warm-up speed; when the water temperature exceeds the set temperature, the thermostat opens, allowing the coolant to circulate to the water tank radiator, effectively improving the cooling efficiency. This fault code indicates that the thermostat has not reached the required engine operating temperature within the set time after the engine is started. Fault causes include the thermostat being stuck in the open position, the engine coolant temperature (ECT) sensor failure, etc.

des: Intake Air Temperature Sensor 2 Circuit High (Bank 2)
knowledge: The function of the intake air temperature (IAT) sensor is to transmit the engine's intake air temperature to the electronic control unit (ECU) in the form of a voltage signal, providing a reference for injection correction. If the electronic control unit (ECU) detects that the intake air temperature (IAT) sensor signal voltage is higher than the maximum value of the self-test (4.6 volts or -50 degrees Celsius), this fault code will appear.

des: Hybrid Battery Pack Air Temperature Sensor B Circuit Range/Performance
knowledge: The intake air temperature (IAT) sensor of a hybrid vehicle is located inside the battery assembly. The causes of this fault code include the hybrid battery (intake air temperature (IAT) sensor), battery pack control module, etc.

des: Hybrid Battery Temperature Sensor E Range/Performance
knowledge: The battery control module controls the opening/closing of the battery fan based on the signal from the battery temperature sensor. If the battery control module detects an error in the battery temperature sensor signal circuit, this fault code will appear.

des: Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Control A Supply Voltage Circuit Low
knowledge: A turbocharger uses the inertial force of the exhaust gas discharged by the engine to drive the turbine, which in turn drives the coaxial impeller to increase the intake pressure, thereby increasing the power of the vehicle. A supercharger is an air compressor used to increase the intake air for an internal combustion engine. More intake air provides more oxygen to the engine, allowing the control module to provide more fuel, thereby increasing the output power. The function of the turbo/supercharger boost controller is that when the boost pressure reaches the set value, the air pressure pushes the wastegate actuator (pneumatic mechanical type) to bypass part of the exhaust gas from the turbine, thereby reducing the turbine speed and controlling the boost level. This fault code indicates that the turbo/supercharger boost control A power supply voltage is lower than the calibrated minimum value.

des: Intake Air Temperature Sensor 1 Circuit Intermittent (Bank 2)
knowledge: The function of the intake air temperature (IAT) sensor is to transmit the engine's intake air temperature to the electronic control unit (ECU) in the form of a voltage signal, providing a reference for injection correction. If the electronic control unit (ECU) detects a sudden change in the intake air temperature (IAT) sensor signal voltage, this fault code will appear.

des: Cylinder 1 Contribution/Balance
knowledge: The Electronic Control Unit (ECU) has detected that the crankshaft acceleration contribution of cylinder 1 is lower than the calibrated value. Fault causes include the injection system of cylinder 1; or other engine problems affecting cylinder 1.

des: Catalyst System Efficiency Below Threshold (Bank 2)
knowledge: The catalytic converter (also known as the catalytic purification converter) is an exhaust purification device that uses the action of a catalyst to convert CO, HC and NOx in the exhaust into gases that are harmless to the human body. It is generally located before the muffler of the exhaust pipe. This fault code indicates that the electronic control unit (ECU) has detected that the efficiency of the catalytic converter system is lower than the acceptable minimum value. The causes of the fault include exhaust gas leakage near the exhaust pipe or exhaust manifold, catalyst box failure, engine coolant temperature (ECT) sensor failure, engine misfire or timing lag, dirty engine oil, oxygen sensor failure, and too high fuel system pressure.

des: Actuator Supply Voltage A Circuit Low
knowledge: The Powertrain Control Module (PCM) has detected that the voltage of the transmission actuator power supply A circuit is too low. Fault causes include circuit or connector failure, automatic transmission hydraulic sensor failure, solenoid valve failure, transmission control module failure, transmission input speed (RPM) sensor failure, transmission output speed (RPM) sensor failure, etc.

des: Exhaust Pressure Sensor A Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
knowledge: The exhaust pressure sensor is used to transmit the exhaust system pressure to the electronic control unit (ECU) in the form of an electrical signal. If the ECU detects a sudden change in the voltage of the exhaust pressure sensor A signal circuit, this fault code will appear.

des: Exhaust Valve Control Solenoid Circuit Low (Bank 1)
knowledge: The function of the camshaft is to control the opening and closing of the valves. In the variable valve timing system, the electronic camshaft adjustment valve (or oil control valve, OCV) adjusts the angle of the camshaft by changing the oil pressure to the camshaft adjuster (mechanical) according to the command from the engine control module (ECM) to ensure that the valves open and close at the best time. If the exhaust camshaft adjustment valve circuit voltage is lower than the calibrated minimum value, this fault code will appear.

des: Cylinder 2 Glow Plug Control Circuit High
knowledge: The function of the glow plug is to heat the compressed gas in the diesel engine combustion chamber through the electric heating coil, so that the diesel engine can be started easily in cold weather. The glow plug control module can automate the preheating and cycling process of the glow plug. If the electronic control unit (ECU) detects that the voltage of the cylinder 2 glow plug circuit is higher than the calibrated maximum value, this fault code will appear.

des: Cylinder 6 Fuel Injector Offset Learning At Max Limit
knowledge: The function of the fuel injector is to atomize the fuel so that it meets the requirements of combustion. The working principle is that when the electromagnetic coil is energized, suction is generated, the needle valve is sucked up, the spray hole is opened, and the fuel is sprayed out at high speed through the annular gap between the needle pin at the head of the needle valve and the spray hole to form a mist. The electronic control unit controls the injection amount by controlling the time interval (also called pulse width) of the injector opening. If the electronic control unit (ECU) detects that the compensation learning of the 6th cylinder injector has reached the maximum learning limit, this fault code will appear.

des: ECM/PCM Power Relay Control Circuit/Open
knowledge: The engine control module, also called the engine control unit (in some cars, the engine control module and the transmission control module are integrated into a powertrain control module), controls the operation of the entire engine. Its most important function is to control the optimal amount of fuel injection and ignition timing of the engine. Another important function is to monitor the components responsible for exhaust emission control. The function of the engine control module relay is to continue to keep the engine control module powered after the ignition switch is turned off until the engine control module completes the shutdown process. If the electronic control unit (ECU) is powered on through the power relay for more than a certain period of time, and the ignition switch position circuit (ISP-R) shows that the key is in the OFF, ACC, or LOCK position, this fault code will appear. The causes of the fault include the ECU relay control circuit, ECU relay, ECU, etc.

des: Shift Solenoid G Control Circuit High
knowledge: The shift solenoid valve controls the hydraulic pressure to the transmission clutch by opening or closing the transmission fluid control valve to control its separation and engagement, thereby achieving gear shifting. The causes of this fault code include low transmission fluid level, dirty transmission fluid, mechanical failure of the shift solenoid valve, circuit, connector, or transmission control module (TCM) failure, etc.

des: Exhaust Gas Recirculation A Flow Insufficient Detected
knowledge: The exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) system is used to introduce a small amount of exhaust gas into the intake manifold when the engine is running at high load. The presence of these exhaust gases reduces the temperature and pressure of the combustion chamber, thereby reducing the emission of nitrogen oxide pollutants. When the vehicle is driving normally and stably and the exhaust gas recirculation system (EGR) is on, if the electronic control unit (ECU) finds that the exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) flow rate is too low than the estimated value based on other information, this fault code will appear. The causes of the fault include DPFE sensor circuit, connector, or itself, DPFE pipeline failure, EGR valve failure or pipeline blockage, electronic control module, etc.

des: Engine Misfire Detected on Startup (First 1000 Revolutions)
knowledge: Cylinder misfire refers to the phenomenon that the mixture cannot burn normally in the cylinder due to various reasons during the operation of the engine. If the electronic control unit (ECU) detects a misfire that may damage the catalytic converter, the fault indicator light will flash and the engine should be turned off immediately. This fault code indicates that the electronic control unit (ECU) detects a cylinder misfire within 1000 revolutions after starting.

des: Hybrid Battery Voltage Sense D Circuit Range/Performance
knowledge: The function of the hybrid battery voltage monitoring circuit is to transmit the battery block voltage to the control module to monitor the charging and discharging of the battery block, as well as possible short circuits and open circuits.

des: Injector Circuit/Open - Cylinder 10
knowledge: The function of the fuel injector is to atomize the fuel so that it meets the requirements of combustion. The working principle is that when the electromagnetic coil is energized, suction is generated, the needle valve is sucked up, the spray hole is opened, and the fuel is sprayed out at high speed through the annular gap between the needle pin at the head of the needle valve and the spray hole to form a mist. The electronic control unit controls the injection amount by controlling the time interval (also called pulse width) of the injector opening. If the electronic control unit (ECU) detects an error in the injector control circuit, this fault code will appear. The causes of the fault include injector interface, circuit failure, injector failure, electronic control module (PCM or ECM) failure, etc.

des: Gear Shift Control Module A Communication Circuit Low
Hybrid Battery Temperature Sensor D Range/Performance
knowledge: The battery control module controls the opening/closing of the battery fan based on the signal from the battery temperature sensor. If the battery control module detects an error in the battery temperature sensor signal circuit, this fault code will appear.

des: HO2S Heater Control Circuit (Bank 2, Sensor 2)
knowledge: The function of the oxygen sensor is to measure the oxygen content in the engine exhaust to correct the injection amount so that the engine can obtain the best air-fuel ratio. In the OBD fault code, you will often see the oxygen sensor in the row. The first row refers to the row where cylinder 1 is located, and the remaining row is the second row. Regardless of which row, the first sensor always refers to the upstream oxygen sensor (before the catalyst box), and the second sensor always refers to the downstream oxygen sensor (after the catalyst box). The electronic control unit (ECU) maintains the temperature of the oxygen sensor at 780oC by controlling the on/off of the oxygen sensor heater. If the oxygen sensor does not reach the required temperature within the set time, or the ECU cannot maintain the set temperature, this fault code will appear.

des: Transmission Mode Switch A Circuit High
knowledge: The function of the transmission mode switch is to instruct the transmission to shift earlier or later, or start in high gear, etc. according to the mode selected by the user (sports/economy/winter, etc.). Fault causes include the transmission mode switch, circuit, connector, or control module.

des: Engine Coolant Temperature/Fuel Temperature Correlation
knowledge: The engine coolant temperature (ECT) sensor transmits the temperature of the engine coolant in the form of an electrical signal to the electronic control unit (ECU) through the principle of thermistor, as a basis for correcting injection and ignition. The electronic control unit (ECU) detects that the signal difference between the engine coolant temperature (ECT) sensor and the fuel temperature (FT) sensor exceeds the maximum allowable range of calibration.

des: Torque Converter Clutch Circuit Electrical
knowledge: The torque converter acts like a clutch in a manual transmission, allowing the torque from the engine to be temporarily disconnected from the transmission, allowing for smooth gear shifting. However, the difference is that the torque converter can also increase torque like downshifting. Causes of failure include torque converter clutch (TCC) solenoid valve circuit or connector failure, TCC solenoid valve mechanical failure, electronic control module (PCM or ECM) failure, etc.

des: Hybrid Battery Temperature Sensor F Circuit
knowledge: The battery control module controls the battery fan on/off based on the signal from the battery temperature sensor. If the battery control module detects that the battery temperature sensor signal circuit voltage is out of the normal range, this fault code will appear.

des: Gear Shift Position Circuit Range/Performance
knowledge: Shift position (monitors the shift lever forward/reverse position, odd/even gear) circuit fault.

des: Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Control A Position Exceeded Learning Limit
knowledge: A turbocharger uses the inertial force of the exhaust gas discharged by the engine to drive the turbine, which in turn drives the coaxial impeller to increase the intake pressure, thereby increasing the power of the vehicle. A supercharger is an air compressor used to increase the intake air for an internal combustion engine. More intake air provides more oxygen to the engine, allowing the control module to provide more fuel, thereby increasing the output power. The function of the turbo/supercharger boost controller is that when the boost pressure reaches the set value, the air pressure pushes the wastegate actuator (pneumatic mechanical type) to bypass part of the exhaust gas from the turbine, thereby reducing the turbine speed and controlling the boost level. This fault code indicates that the turbo/supercharger boost control A position exceeds the normal range.

des: Power Steering Control Circuit
knowledge: The Electronic Power Steering (EPS) system controls the bypass hydraulic oil flow on both sides of the power steering piston according to the signal from the vehicle speed sensor (VSS), thereby changing the steering force on the steering wheel.
