knowledge: Automatic shift manual transmissions allow the driver to put the transmission into manual mode and manually control upshifts or downshifts.

des: Engine Coolant Temperature Sensor 1 Circuit
knowledge: The engine coolant temperature (ECT) sensor transmits the temperature of the engine coolant in the form of an electrical signal to the electronic control unit (ECU) through the principle of thermistor, as a basis for correcting injection and ignition. If the ECU detects that the signal voltage of the engine coolant temperature (ECT) sensor exceeds the normal calibrated range, this fault code will appear.

des: Drive Motor B Position Sensor Circuit A Range/Performance
O2 Sensor Heater Circuit (Bank 2, Sensor 2)
knowledge: The function of the oxygen sensor is to measure the oxygen content in the engine exhaust to correct the injection amount so that the engine can obtain the best air-fuel ratio. In the OBD fault code, you will often see the oxygen sensor in the bank. Bank 1 refers to the bank where cylinder 1 is located, and the remaining bank is bank 2. Regardless of which bank, the first sensor always refers to the upstream oxygen sensor (before the catalyst box), and the second sensor always refers to the downstream oxygen sensor (after the catalyst box). The electronic control unit (ECU) continuously monitors the heated oxygen sensor heater to ensure that there is no open circuit, short circuit, or excessive current consumption. If the current consumption exceeds the calibrated limit, or an open circuit or short circuit is detected, the fault code will appear. The causes of the fault include the oxygen sensor heater circuit, connector failure, oxygen sensor itself failure, electronic control module (PCM or ECM) failure, etc.

des: O2 Sensor Signals Swapped (Bank 1, Sensor 2)/(Bank 2, Sensor 2)
knowledge: The function of the oxygen sensor is to measure the oxygen content in the engine exhaust to correct the injection amount so that the engine can obtain the best air-fuel ratio. In the OBD fault code, you will often see the oxygen sensor in the row. The first row refers to the row where cylinder 1 is located, and the remaining row is the second row. Regardless of which row, the first sensor always refers to the upstream oxygen sensor (before the catalyst box), and the second sensor always refers to the downstream oxygen sensor (after the catalyst box). The heated oxygen sensor monitor monitors whether the oxygen sensor signal response caused by the fuel change corresponds to the correct oxygen sensor row (Bank). Possible causes of this fault code include mixing up the oxygen sensor plugs and wiring, etc.

des: Hybrid Battery Voltage Sense G Circuit
knowledge: The function of the hybrid battery voltage monitoring circuit is to transmit the battery block voltage to the control module to monitor the charging and discharging of the battery block, as well as possible short circuits and open circuits.

des: Insufficient Coolant Temperature for Stable Operation
knowledge: The signal from the engine coolant temperature (ECT) or cylinder head temperature sensor (CHT) indicates that the engine has not reached the required temperature for closed-loop fuel control operation within the set time. Fault causes include coolant thermostat stuck in the normally open position, etc.

des: Cylinder 10 Glow Plug Circuit Range/Performance
knowledge: The function of the glow plug is to heat the compressed gas in the diesel engine combustion chamber through the electric heating coil, so that the diesel engine can be started easily in cold weather. The glow plug control module can automate the preheating and cycling process of the glow plug. If the electronic control unit (ECU) detects a fault in the cylinder 10 glow plug circuit, this fault code will appear.

des: Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Sensor B Circuit Range/Performance
knowledge: A turbocharger uses the inertial force of the exhaust gas discharged by the engine to drive the turbine, which in turn drives the coaxial impeller to increase the intake pressure, thereby increasing the power of the car. A supercharger is an air compressor used to increase the intake air for an internal combustion engine. More intake air provides more oxygen to the engine, allowing the control module to provide more fuel, thereby increasing the output power. The boost pressure sensor, also called the boost pressure sensor (BPS), is used to transmit the boost pressure to the electronic control unit (ECU) in the form of an electrical signal. If the ECU detects an error in the boost pressure sensor (BPS) signal circuit, this fault code will appear.

des: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch B Circuit Intermittent
knowledge: In the electronic throttle control (ETC) system, the function of the accelerator pedal position (APP) sensor is to transmit the position of the accelerator pedal to the throttle control module in the form of an electrical signal, which serves as a reference for the throttle actuator to control the throttle valve opening. This fault code indicates that the voltage of the throttle pedal position sensor B circuit changes suddenly.

des: Auxiliary Transmission Fluid Pump Motor Phase W Current High
knowledge: The function of the transmission fluid pump is to provide working pressure to the transmission fluid when the engine is running. The shift solenoid valve controls the hydraulic pressure to the transmission clutch by opening or closing the transmission fluid control valve to control its separation and combination, thereby achieving gear shifting. The function of the auxiliary transmission fluid pump is to provide pressure to the transmission fluid when the engine is not running (such as when towing) to prevent the transmission from overheating.

des: Cruise Control Multi-Function Input B Circuit Low
knowledge: The cruise control system allows the driver to automatically maintain the vehicle speed without stepping on the accelerator pedal. Faults may include the cruise control multi-function input switch, circuit, connector, etc.

des: Shift Timing Solenoid B
knowledge: The shift solenoid valve controls the hydraulic pressure to the transmission clutch by opening or closing the transmission fluid control valve to control its separation and engagement, thereby achieving gear shifting. The causes of this fault code include low transmission fluid level, dirty transmission fluid, mechanical failure of the shift solenoid valve, circuit, connector, or transmission control module (TCM) failure, etc.

des: Drive Motor B Phase V Current
knowledge: The Hybrid Vehicle Electronic Control Unit (HV ECU) is responsible for monitoring the drive motor inverter current sensor. If the HV ECU detects an error, this fault code will appear.

des: Fuel System Leak Detected - Large Leak
Auxiliary Transmission Fluid Pump Control Module Internal Temperature Sensor Circuit Low
knowledge: This fault code indicates that the voltage of the control module's internal temperature sensor signal circuit exceeds the maximum calibrated range. The cause of the fault is the internal temperature sensor, circuit, connector, or control module.

des: ECM/PCM Power Relay Sense Circuit/Open
knowledge: The engine control module, also called the engine control unit (the engine control module and the transmission control module on some vehicles are integrated into a powertrain control module), controls the operation of the entire engine. Its most important function is to control the optimal amount of fuel injection and ignition timing of the engine. Another important function is to monitor the components responsible for exhaust emission control. The function of the engine control module relay is to continue to keep the engine control module powered after the ignition switch is turned off until the engine control module completes the shutdown process. If the passive anti-theft system (PATS) shows that the key is in the ON (run) or START (start) position, and the ignition switch position (ISP-R) circuit shows OFF (off), ACC (accessory), LOCK (lock), this fault code will appear. The causes of the fault include ignition circuit fuse, ignition switch, ISP-R circuit, ECU relay, passive anti-theft system, ECU, etc.

des: Hybrid Battery Precharge Contactor Circuit Stuck Closed
knowledge: The System Main Relay (SMR) is responsible for turning the high voltage power supply on and off. If the hybrid vehicle ECU detects a fault in the 1st System Main Relay (SMR1), this fault code will appear.

des: Turbocharger/Supercharger Inlet Pressure Sensor - Circuit Range/Perfo
knowledge: A turbocharger uses the inertial force of the exhaust gas discharged by the engine to drive the turbine, which in turn drives the coaxial impeller to pressurize the intake air, thereby increasing the power of the vehicle. A supercharger is an air compressor used to increase the intake air for an internal combustion engine. More intake air provides more oxygen to the engine, allowing the control module to provide more fuel, thereby increasing output power. This fault code indicates that the circuit voltage of the inlet pressure sensor (downstream of the throttle valve) is wrong. This fault code may be a problem with the manifold absolute pressure (MAP) sensor (MAP) for some vehicles.

des: O2 Sensor Circuit Low Voltage (Bank 1, Sensor 3)
knowledge: The function of the oxygen sensor is to measure the oxygen content in the engine exhaust to correct the injection amount so that the engine can obtain the best air-fuel ratio. In the OBD fault code, you will often see the oxygen sensor in the row. The first row refers to the row where cylinder 1 is located, and the remaining row is the second row. Regardless of which row, the first sensor always refers to the upstream oxygen sensor (before the catalyst box), and the second sensor always refers to the downstream oxygen sensor (after the catalyst box). This fault code will appear when the voltage of the heated oxygen sensor signal is continuously lower than 156 millivolts within a set period of time. The causes of the fault include oxygen sensor contamination due to silicon in the fuel, oxygen sensor signal and ground circuit crossover, oxygen sensor signal circuit short circuit to ground, oxygen sensor itself failure, electronic control module (PCM or ECM) failure, etc.

des: Fuel Rail Pressure Sensor A Circuit
knowledge: The fuel pressure regulator uses a spring-loaded valve to return excess gasoline to the tank, thereby maintaining constant pressure in the fuel line. There is a vacuum tube on the fuel pressure regulator that is connected to the intake manifold to provide the appropriate gasoline pressure under different engine operating conditions (engine load is determined by the vacuum level). Most cars have fuel pressure regulators located on the fuel rail, but some cars have the fuel pressure regulator located inside the fuel tank. The fuel pressure sensor is responsible for measuring the fuel pressure near the injector. The electronic control unit (ECU) uses this signal to adjust the injector pulse width and measure the amount of fuel entering the combustion chamber. The electronic control unit (ECU) monitors the reference voltage of the fuel rail pressure sensor. If this voltage exceeds the normal range for a set period of time, this fault code will appear. Fault causes include fuel pressure regulator valve failure, fuel pressure sensor failure, fuel pump control module failure, fuel pump failure, etc.

des: Downshift Switch Circuit
Drive Motor B Phase W Current Low
knowledge: The Hybrid Vehicle Electronic Control Unit (HV ECU) is responsible for monitoring the drive motor inverter current sensor. If the HV ECU detects an error, this fault code will appear.

des: HO2S Heater Control Circuit Low (Bank 1, Sensor 1)
knowledge: The function of the oxygen sensor is to measure the oxygen content in the engine exhaust to correct the injection amount so that the engine can obtain the best air-fuel ratio. In the OBD fault code, you will often see the oxygen sensor in which bank. Bank 1 refers to the bank where cylinder 1 is located, and the remaining bank is bank 2. Regardless of which bank, the first sensor always refers to the upstream oxygen sensor (before the catalyst box), and the second sensor always refers to the downstream oxygen sensor (after the catalyst box). The electronic control unit (ECU) maintains the temperature of the oxygen sensor at 780oC by controlling the on/off of the oxygen sensor heater. If the control circuit voltage of the heater is lower than the calibrated minimum value, this fault code will appear.

des: Hydraulic Pressure Sensor Circuit High
Cylinder 7 - Fuel Trim at Min Limit
knowledge: Fuel trimming refers to the electronic control unit (ECU) controlling fuel delivery by increasing or decreasing the time the injectors are open to achieve the best air-fuel ratio (14.7:1 air-to-gasoline mass ratio) for the engine. Too rich an air-fuel ratio means too much fuel is delivered, and too lean an air-fuel ratio means too little fuel is delivered. This fault code will appear if fuel trim reaches and stays at the minimum limit for more than a certain period of time.

des: Hybrid Battery Pack Voltage Sense A Circuit High
Shift Solenoid B Intermittent
knowledge: The shift solenoid valve controls the hydraulic pressure to the transmission clutch by opening or closing the transmission fluid control valve to control its separation and engagement, thereby achieving gear shifting. The causes of this fault code include low transmission fluid level, dirty transmission fluid, mechanical failure of the shift solenoid valve, circuit, connector, or transmission control module (TCM) failure, etc.

des: Generator Torque Sensor Circuit Low
knowledge: The control module has detected that the generator torque sensor signal is outside the normal calibrated range.

des: Intake Air Temperature Sensor 2 Circuit (Bank 1)
knowledge: The function of the intake air temperature (IAT) sensor is to transmit the engine's intake air temperature to the electronic control unit (ECU) in the form of a voltage signal, providing a reference for injection correction. This fault code indicates that the intake air temperature (IAT) sensor signal voltage exceeds the calibrated normal value.

des: Gear 2 Incorrect Ratio
knowledge: The vehicle is running with the 2nd gear command on, and the electronic control unit (ECU) detects that the 2nd gear ratio is incorrect. Fault causes include low transmission fluid level, shift solenoid valve, transmission hydraulic sensor, solenoid valve failure in the valve body, input shaft speed sensor, output shaft speed sensor, circuit, connector, transmission control module failure, etc.

des: Fan 1 Control Circuit Low
knowledge: The Electronic Control Unit (ECU) has detected that the Fan 1 (Low Speed) Control Variable (FCV) circuit voltage is below the calibrated minimum value. Fault causes include the fan itself or its control circuit, connector, etc.

des: Cruise Control On Signal
knowledge: The cruise control system allows the driver to automatically maintain the vehicle speed without pressing the accelerator pedal. During the key-on engine running (KOER) self-test, the electronic control unit (ECU) found that the cruise control ON button was not pressed. The cause of the malfunction may be the cruise control main switch, circuit, connector, or electronic control unit (ECU).

des: Hybrid Battery Voltage Sense O Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
knowledge: The function of the hybrid battery voltage monitoring circuit is to transmit the battery block voltage to the control module to monitor the charging and discharging of the battery block, as well as possible short circuits and open circuits.

des: Cylinder 2 - Injector Leaking
knowledge: The function of the fuel injector is to atomize the fuel so that it meets the requirements of combustion. The working principle is that when the electromagnetic coil is energized, suction is generated, the needle valve is sucked up, the spray hole is opened, and the fuel is sprayed out at high speed through the annular gap between the needle pin at the head of the needle valve and the spray hole to form a mist. The electronic control unit controls the injection amount by controlling the time interval (also called pulse width) of the fuel injector opening. This fault code indicates that the fuel injector of the second cylinder is leaking.

des: Clutch Position Control Error
Hybrid Battery Pack Cooling Fan 2 Performance/Stuck Off
knowledge: The battery control module controls the battery fan to turn on or off based on the signal from the battery temperature sensor. If the actual battery pack temperature is higher than the battery pack temperature estimated based on the cooling fan performance by a set value, the control module considers that the battery pack fan is faulty or stuck in the off position.

des: Cylinder 2 Glow Plug Control Circuit Low
knowledge: The function of the glow plug is to heat the compressed gas in the diesel engine combustion chamber through the electric heating coil, so that the diesel engine can be started easily in cold weather. The glow plug control module can automate the preheating and cycling process of the glow plug. If the electronic control unit (ECU) detects that the voltage of the cylinder 2 glow plug circuit is lower than the calibrated minimum value, this fault code will appear.

des: Auto Shift Manual Mode Circuit Range/Performance
knowledge: Automatic shift manual transmissions allow the driver to put the transmission into manual mode and manually control upshifts or downshifts.

des: Battery Temperature Sensor Circuit Low
knowledge: The battery temperature sensor is located at the bottom of the vehicle battery tray. Its main function is to transmit the battery temperature to the electronic control unit (ECU) in the form of an electrical signal to help determine the charging speed. If the ECU detects that the battery temperature sensor circuit voltage is lower than the calibrated minimum value, this fault code will appear.

des: Hybrid Battery Voltage Sense J Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
knowledge: The function of the hybrid battery voltage monitoring circuit is to transmit the battery block voltage to the control module to monitor the charging and discharging of the battery block, as well as possible short circuits and open circuits.

des: Exhaust Pressure Sensor B Circuit
knowledge: The exhaust pressure sensor is used to transmit the exhaust system pressure to the electronic control unit (ECU) in the form of an electrical signal. If the ECU detects that the exhaust pressure sensor A circuit voltage is out of the normal calibrated range, this fault code will appear.

des: High Voltage System Interlock Circuit Performance
knowledge: The function of the high voltage system interlock is to close the system main relay when the vehicle is stationary if there is a problem with the safety device (for example, the charging connector or converter is not covered). If the control module detects a fault in the high voltage interlock circuit, this fault code will appear.

des: Auxiliary Transmission Fluid Pump Control Module Feedback Signal Range/Performance
knowledge: The function of the transmission fluid pump is to provide working pressure to the transmission fluid when the engine is running. The shift solenoid valve controls the hydraulic pressure to the transmission clutch by opening or closing the transmission fluid control valve to control its separation and combination, thereby achieving gear shifting. The function of the auxiliary transmission fluid pump is to provide pressure to the transmission fluid when the engine is not running (such as when towing) to prevent the transmission from overheating.

des: Auxiliary Transmission Fluid Pump Motor Control Module
knowledge: The function of the transmission fluid pump is to provide working pressure to the transmission fluid when the engine is running. The shift solenoid valve controls the hydraulic pressure to the transmission clutch by opening or closing the transmission fluid control valve to control its separation and combination, thereby achieving gear shifting. The function of the auxiliary transmission fluid pump is to provide pressure to the transmission fluid when the engine is not running (such as when towing) to prevent the transmission from overheating.

des: Internal Control Module O2 Sensor Processor Performance (Bank 2)
knowledge: The electronic control unit (ECU) monitors the oxygen sensor integrated circuit. If the ECU finds an internal circuit or communication problem, this fault code will appear. The cause of the fault is the electronic control unit (ECU).

des: ECM/PCM Power Relay De-Energized Performance - Too Early
knowledge: The engine control module, also called the engine control unit (the engine control module and the transmission control module on some vehicles are integrated into a powertrain control module), controls the operation of the entire engine. Its most important function is to control the optimal fuel injection amount and ignition timing of the engine. Another important function is to monitor the components for exhaust emission control. The function of the engine control module relay is to continue to maintain the power supply to the engine control module after the ignition switch is turned off until the engine control module completes the shutdown process.

des: Diesel Intake Air Flow Position Sensor Circuit
knowledge: The diesel engine intake flow control system forms an effective intake vortex by automatically controlling the throttle opening angle and coordinating with the tangential airway or spiral airway. At the same time, the intensity of the intake vortex is automatically controlled, which effectively improves the engine combustion, thereby optimizing the engine power, economy and other performance indicators. The causes of P02E6 failure include the intake flap control actuator position sensor, its circuit, connector, or control module (ECM).

des: Exhaust Gas Recirculation Temperature Sensor A Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
knowledge: The function of the exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) system is to introduce a small amount of exhaust gas into the intake manifold when the engine is running at high load. The presence of these exhaust gases reduces the temperature and pressure of the combustion chamber, thereby reducing the emission of nitrogen oxide pollutants. If the electronic control unit (ECU) detects a sudden change in the signal voltage of the exhaust gas recirculation valve (EGR) temperature sensor, this fault code will appear.

des: Cylinder 7 Injection Timing
knowledge: The function of the fuel injector is to atomize the fuel so that it meets the requirements of combustion. The working principle is that when the electromagnetic coil is energized, suction is generated, the needle valve is sucked up, the spray hole is opened, and the fuel is sprayed out at high speed through the annular gap between the needle pin at the head of the needle valve and the spray hole to form a mist. The electronic control unit controls the injection amount by controlling the time interval (also called pulse width) of the injector opening. If the electronic control unit (ECU) detects that the actual timing of the injector deviates from the ideal injection timing by more than the maximum limit, this fault code will appear.

des: Drive Motor Inverter Temperature Sensor A Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
knowledge: The inverter converts DC power into AC power. The hybrid electronic control unit (HV ECU) uses a temperature sensor integrated in the inverter to monitor the temperature of the drive motor inverter. If the output of this temperature sensor is abnormal, this fault code will appear.

des: Gear Shift Lock Solenoid/Actuator Control Circuit A High
Hybrid Battery Pack Voltage Sense B Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
A Camshaft Profile Control Performance/Stuck Off (Bank 1)
knowledge: The function of the camshaft is to control the opening and closing of the valves. In the variable valve timing system, the electronic camshaft adjustment valve (or oil control valve, OCV) adjusts the angle of the camshaft according to the instructions from the engine control module (ECM) by changing the oil pressure to the camshaft adjuster (mechanical type) to ensure that the valves open and close at the best time. This optimizes the efficiency and power of the engine in all speed ranges. This fault code indicates that the A (intake/left/front) camshaft profile control has failed or is stuck in the closed position.

des: Cylinder 9 Injection Timing
knowledge: The function of the fuel injector is to atomize the fuel so that it meets the requirements of combustion. The working principle is that when the electromagnetic coil is energized, suction is generated, the needle valve is sucked up, the spray hole is opened, and the fuel is sprayed out at high speed through the annular gap between the needle pin at the head of the needle valve and the spray hole to form a mist. The electronic control unit controls the injection amount by controlling the time interval (also called pulse width) of the injector opening. If the electronic control unit (ECU) detects that the actual timing of the injector deviates from the ideal injection timing by more than the maximum limit, this fault code will appear.

des: Transmission Park Position Sensor/Switch B Circuit/Open
knowledge: The function of the parking position sensor is to send a signal to the electronic control unit (ECU) indicating whether the shift lever is in the parking position. If the ECU detects that the parking position sensor circuit voltage is out of the normal calibrated range, this fault code will appear.

des: Transmission Park Position Sensor/Switch B Circuit Low
knowledge: The function of the parking position sensor is to send a signal to the electronic control unit (ECU) indicating whether the shift lever is in the parking position. If the ECU detects that the parking position sensor circuit voltage is lower than the calibrated minimum value, this fault code will appear.

des: Transmission Fluid Pressure High
knowledge: The shift solenoid valve controls the hydraulic pressure to the transmission clutch by opening or closing the transmission fluid control valve to control its disengagement and engagement, thereby achieving gear shifting. Accurate control of the transmission fluid pressure is very important for smooth gear shifting. The transmission fluid pressure (TFP) sensor transmits the transmission fluid pressure to the transmission control module (TCU) in the form of an electrical signal, and the transmission fluid pressure control solenoid valve is responsible for controlling the transmission fluid pressure.

des: Generator Inverter Temperature Sensor Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
knowledge: The function of an inverter is to convert direct current into alternating current.

des: O2 Sensor Heater Circuit (Bank 1, Sensor 3)
knowledge: The function of the oxygen sensor is to measure the oxygen content in the engine exhaust to correct the injection amount so that the engine can obtain the best air-fuel ratio. In the OBD fault code, you will often see the oxygen sensor in the bank. Bank 1 refers to the bank where cylinder 1 is located, and the remaining bank is bank 2. Regardless of which bank, the first sensor always refers to the upstream oxygen sensor (before the catalyst box), and the second sensor always refers to the downstream oxygen sensor (after the catalyst box). The electronic control unit (ECU) continuously monitors the heated oxygen sensor heater to ensure that there is no open circuit, short circuit, or excessive current consumption. If the current consumption exceeds the calibrated limit, or an open circuit or short circuit is detected, the fault code will appear. The causes of the fault include the oxygen sensor heater circuit, connector failure, oxygen sensor itself failure, electronic control module (PCM or ECM) failure, etc.

des: Knock Sensor 2 Circuit Range/Performance (Bank 2)
knowledge: The knock sensor is responsible for detecting vibrations when the engine speed changes. The knock sensor then expresses this vibration in the form of voltage. When necessary, the electronic control module (ECU) will delay the ignition to prevent knocking. If this voltage is wrong, this fault code will appear. Fault causes include faults in the knock sensor circuit, connectors, itself, or electronic control module (PCM or ECM) failure.

des: Cylinder 9 Fuel Injector Offset Learning At Min Limit
knowledge: The function of the fuel injector is to atomize the fuel so that it meets the requirements of combustion. The working principle is that when the electromagnetic coil is energized, suction is generated, the needle valve is sucked up, the spray hole is opened, and the fuel is sprayed out at high speed through the annular gap between the needle pin at the head of the needle valve and the spray hole to form a mist. The electronic control unit controls the injection amount by controlling the time interval (also called pulse width) of the injector opening. If the electronic control unit (ECU) detects that the compensation learning of the 9th cylinder injector has reached the minimum learning limit, this fault code will appear.

des: Fan 3 Control Circuit
knowledge: This fault code will appear if the electronic control unit (ECU) finds that the medium speed fan control circuit still has significant current consumption when it is grounded (fan on); or when the medium speed fan control circuit is not grounded (fan off) and no voltage is detected.

des: Incorrect Immobilizer Key
knowledge: The function of the anti-theft control module is to ensure that the car will not be allowed to start unless the special key exists and it matches various components.

des: Input/Turbine Speed Sensor A Circuit Range/Performance
knowledge: The turbine speed sensor (TSS), also called the input shaft speed sensor (ISS), is used to transmit the speed of the input shaft (that is, the torque converter) to the transmission control module (TCU) in the form of frequency. This information is particularly critical for adjusting the torque converter lock clutch. This fault code indicates that the voltage of the input shaft speed sensor signal circuit is wrong. The causes of the fault include low transmission fluid level or deterioration and dirtiness, transmission fluid temperature (TFT) sensor or its circuit connector failure, transmission fluid temperature (TFT) sensor calibration error, electronic control module (PCM or ECM) failure, etc.

des: O2 Sensor Delayed Response - Rich to Lean (Bank 2, Sensor 2)
knowledge: The function of the oxygen sensor is to measure the oxygen content in the engine exhaust to correct the injection amount so that the engine can obtain the best air-fuel ratio. In the OBD fault code, you will often see the oxygen sensor in the row. The first row refers to the row where cylinder 1 is located, and the remaining row is the second row. Regardless of which row, the first sensor always refers to the upstream oxygen sensor (before the catalyst box), and the second sensor always refers to the downstream oxygen sensor (after the catalyst box). The heated oxygen sensor monitor tracks the voltage change rate during the rise and fall of the oxygen sensor signal. If the electronic control unit (ECU) finds that the voltage change rate lags behind during the process of the air-fuel ratio changing from rich to lean, this fault code will appear.

des: Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Control B Supply Voltage Circuit Low
knowledge: A turbocharger uses the inertial force of the exhaust gas discharged by the engine to drive the turbine, which in turn drives the coaxial impeller to increase the intake pressure, thereby increasing the power of the vehicle. A supercharger is an air compressor used to increase the intake air for an internal combustion engine. More intake air provides more oxygen to the engine, allowing the control module to provide more fuel, thereby increasing the output power. The function of the turbo/supercharger boost controller is that when the boost pressure reaches the set value, the air pressure pushes the wastegate actuator (pneumatic mechanical type) to bypass part of the exhaust gas from the turbine, thereby reducing the turbine speed and controlling the boost level. This fault code indicates that the turbo/supercharger boost control B power supply voltage is lower than the calibrated minimum value.

des: Gear Shift Position Circuit High
knowledge: Shift position (monitors the shift lever forward/reverse position, odd/even gear) circuit fault.

des: Hybrid Battery Temperature Sensor E/F Correlation
knowledge: The battery control module controls the battery fan on/off based on the signal from the battery temperature sensor. If the battery control module detects that the signal difference of the battery temperature sensor E/F exceeds the maximum limit of calibration, this fault code will appear.

des: Cylinder 6 Glow Plug Circuit Range/Performance
knowledge: The function of the glow plug is to heat the compressed gas in the diesel engine combustion chamber through the electric heating coil, so that the diesel engine can be started easily in cold weather. The glow plug control module can automate the preheating and cycling process of the glow plug. If the electronic control unit (ECU) detects a fault in the cylinder 6 glow plug circuit, this fault code will appear.

des: Fuel Volume Regulator Control Circuit Range/Performance
knowledge: (In new cars where fuel injectors are widely used, fuel regulators are rarely used)

des: Hybrid Battery Voltage Sense Z Circuit Low
knowledge: The function of the hybrid battery voltage monitoring circuit is to transmit the battery block voltage to the control module to monitor the charging and discharging of the battery block, as well as possible short circuits and open circuits.

des: Four Wheel Drive (4WD) Switch Circuit Low
Hybrid Battery Pack Cooling Fan 2 Control Circuit Low
knowledge: The fan motor controller is responsible for regulating the voltage of the hybrid battery pack cooling fan. If the cooling fan 1 control circuit voltage falls below the calibrated minimum value, this fault code will appear.

des: Power Steering Pressure Sensor/Switch Circuit Range/Performance
knowledge: The power steering pressure (PSP) sensor transmits the power steering load pressure to the electronic control unit (ECU) in the form of a voltage signal based on the principle of a potentiometer. If the load pressure is too large, the ECU will increase the engine idle speed and shut down the air conditioning compressor if necessary to prevent the engine from stalling. This fault code indicates that the power steering pressure sensor circuit is faulty.

des: Charge Air Cooler Bypass Control B Circuit Low
knowledge: The turbocharger uses the inertial force of the exhaust gas discharged by the engine to drive the turbine, which in turn drives the coaxial impeller to supercharge the intake air, thereby increasing the power of the car. The charge air cooler (also called the intercooler) is used to cool the supercharged air coming out of the supercharger. After the air passes through the supercharger, the pressure increases and the temperature rises. The charge air cooler can reduce the temperature of the charge air, thereby increasing the air density and the charging efficiency, so as to achieve the purpose of increasing engine power and reducing emissions. The function of the charge air cooler bypass valve is to bypass part of the air around the air cooler. This air is then mixed with the air cooled by the air cooler and enters the engine to ensure that the intake temperature is higher than the dew temperature. If the air cooler bypass valve control circuit voltage is lower than the calibrated minimum value, this fault code will appear.

des: Fuel Pressure Relief Control Stuck On
knowledge: The function of the fuel system overpressure relief valve is to release the fuel line pressure when the fuel line pressure is too high due to a dirty filter, blocked line, etc. If the fuel pressure release control is stuck in the open position, this fault code will appear.

des: A Camshaft Position - Timing Over-Advanced or System Performance (Bank 1)
knowledge: The function of the camshaft is to control the opening and closing of the valve. In the variable valve timing system, the electronic camshaft adjustment valve (or oil control valve, OCV) adjusts the angle of the camshaft according to the command from the engine control module (ECM) by changing the oil pressure to the camshaft adjuster (mechanical type) to ensure that the valve opens and closes at the best time. The causes of P0011 include A intake/left/front camshaft timing is not set properly, the camshaft is mechanically stuck, or the actuator valve is stuck in the open position.

des: Cylinder 5 Glow Plug Circuit Range/Performance
knowledge: The function of the glow plug is to heat the compressed gas in the diesel engine combustion chamber through the electric heating coil, so that the diesel engine can be started easily in cold weather. The glow plug control module can automate the preheating and cycling process of the glow plug. If the electronic control unit (ECU) detects a fault in the cylinder 5 glow plug circuit, this fault code will appear.

des: O2 Sensor Circuit Low Voltage (Bank 2, Sensor 1)
knowledge: The function of the oxygen sensor is to measure the oxygen content in the engine exhaust to correct the injection amount so that the engine can obtain the best air-fuel ratio. In the OBD fault code, you will often see the oxygen sensor in the row. The first row refers to the row where cylinder 1 is located, and the remaining row is the second row. Regardless of which row, the first sensor always refers to the upstream oxygen sensor (before the catalyst box), and the second sensor always refers to the downstream oxygen sensor (after the catalyst box). This fault code will appear when the voltage of the heated oxygen sensor signal is continuously lower than 156 mV within the set time period. The causes of the fault include the oxygen sensor circuit, connector, oxygen sensor itself, electronic control module, etc.

des: Generator Temperature Sensor Circuit
knowledge: The starter/generator of a hybrid vehicle is the same motor, usually located in the transmission. Causes of failure include the generator temperature sensor, circuit, connector, control module, etc.

des: Turbocharger/Supercharger Inlet Pressure Sensor - Circuit Intermitten
knowledge: A turbocharger uses the inertial force of the exhaust gas discharged by the engine to drive the turbine, which in turn drives the coaxial impeller to pressurize the intake air, thereby increasing the power of the vehicle. A supercharger is an air compressor used to increase the intake air for an internal combustion engine. More intake air provides more oxygen to the engine, allowing the control module to provide more fuel, thereby increasing output power. This fault code indicates that the voltage of the inlet pressure sensor (downstream of the throttle valve) circuit suddenly changes. This fault code may be a problem with the manifold absolute pressure (MAP) sensor for some vehicles.

des: Drive Motor B Phase UVW Circuit/Open
Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch A Circuit Intermittent
knowledge: In the electronic throttle control (ETC) system, the accelerator pedal position (APP) sensor transmits the position of the accelerator pedal to the throttle control module in the form of an electrical signal, which serves as a reference for the throttle actuator to control the throttle valve opening. If the electronic control unit (ECU) detects a sudden change in the signal voltage of the electronic throttle pedal position sensor 1, this fault code will appear.

des: Exhaust Pressure Control Valve A Circuit High
knowledge: The exhaust pressure control valve is a variable position valve. Its main function is to help the engine warm up quickly by changing the exhaust pressure (boosting engine load) when the outside temperature is extremely low (<5 degrees Celsius). If the electronic control unit (ECU) detects that the exhaust pressure control valve A circuit voltage is higher than the calibrated maximum value, this fault code will appear.

des: Hybrid Battery Voltage Sense K Circuit Range/Performance
knowledge: The function of the hybrid battery voltage monitoring circuit is to transmit the battery block voltage to the control module to monitor the charging and discharging of the battery block, as well as possible short circuits and open circuits.

des: Misfire Detected With Low Fuel
knowledge: Cylinder misfire refers to the phenomenon that the mixture cannot burn normally in the cylinder due to various reasons during the operation of the engine. If the electronic control unit (ECU) detects a misfire that may damage the catalytic converter, the fault indicator light will flash and the engine should be turned off immediately. This fault code indicates that the electronic control unit (ECU) has detected 1) cylinder misfire, 2) the fuel level is very low.

des: Gear Shift Position Control Error
knowledge: Shift position (monitoring the shift lever forward/reverse position, odd/even gear) control error.

des: Gear Lever Y Position Circuit Low
Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch A Circuit Intermittent
knowledge: The shift solenoid valve controls the hydraulic pressure to the transmission clutch by opening or closing the transmission fluid control valve to control its separation and engagement, thereby achieving gear shifting. Accurate control of the transmission fluid pressure is very important for smooth gear shifting. The function of the transmission fluid pressure (TFP) sensor is to transmit the transmission fluid pressure in the form of an electrical signal to the transmission control module (TCU) as a reference for the operation of the transmission fluid pressure control solenoid valve.

des: Cylinder 8 - Fuel Trim at Min Limit
knowledge: Fuel trimming refers to the electronic control unit (ECU) controlling fuel delivery by increasing or decreasing the time the injectors are open to achieve the best air-fuel ratio (14.7:1 air-to-gasoline mass ratio) for the engine. Too rich an air-fuel ratio means too much fuel is delivered, and too lean an air-fuel ratio means too little fuel is delivered. This fault code will appear if fuel trim reaches and stays at the minimum limit for more than a certain period of time.

des: Manifold Absolute Pressure - Barometric Pressure Correlation
knowledge: The function of the Manifold Absolute Pressure (MAP) sensor is to measure the pressure (vacuum) in the intake manifold. The powertrain control module (PCM) then uses the difference between the intake manifold pressure and the atmospheric pressure (which is linearly related to the engine load) as a basis for determining the basic injection amount of the injector to help the engine achieve the best air-fuel ratio under different loads. The atmospheric pressure sensor (sometimes called the high altitude compensator, HAC) is to transmit the atmospheric pressure to the electronic control module in the form of an electrical signal. Atmospheric pressure varies with weather and altitude. The lower the pressure, the thinner the air. The powertrain control module (PCM) will correct the fuel supply based on the atmospheric pressure value to help the engine achieve the best air-fuel ratio. If the electronic control unit (ECU) finds that the signal difference between the manifold absolute pressure (MAP) sensor and the atmospheric pressure sensor exceeds the calibrated value (usually 10.35KPa) within a set period of time (2.5 seconds), this fault code will appear.

des: Misfire Detected - Fueling Disabled
knowledge: Cylinder misfire refers to the phenomenon that the mixture cannot burn normally in the cylinder due to various reasons during the operation of the engine. If the electronic control unit (ECU) detects a misfire that may damage the catalytic converter, the fault indicator light will flash and the engine should be turned off immediately. This fault code indicates that the electronic control unit (ECU) has detected a misfire. To prevent damage to the catalytic converter, fuel delivery has been terminated.

des: O2 Sensor Circuit Slow Response (Bank 2, Sensor 2)
knowledge: The function of the oxygen sensor is to measure the oxygen content in the engine exhaust to correct the injection amount so that the engine can obtain the best air-fuel ratio. In the OBD fault code, you will often see the oxygen sensor in the bank. Bank 1 refers to the bank where cylinder 1 is located, and the remaining bank is bank 2. Regardless of which bank, the first sensor always refers to the upstream oxygen sensor (before the catalyst box), and the second sensor always refers to the downstream oxygen sensor (after the catalyst box). The heated oxygen sensor monitor tracks the voltage change rate during the rise and fall of the oxygen sensor signal. When the voltage change rate is lower than the calibration value, the electronic control unit (ECU) will begin to modify the air-fuel ratio and try to increase the voltage change rate of the oxygen sensor. If the ECU has reached the acceptable fuel trim limit or has exceeded the acceptable fuel trim time, and still does not monitor an acceptable voltage change rate, this fault code will appear. Fault causes include oxygen sensor contamination due to silicon in the fuel, open circuit of oxygen sensor signal circuit, oxygen sensor itself failure, exhaust pipe or exhaust manifold leakage, electronic control module (PCM or ECM) failure, etc.

des: Hydraulic Oil Temperature Sensor Circuit Low
TCU Power Relay Sense Circuit Range/Performance
knowledge: The transmission control module (TCM or TCU) collects information from various sensors and the engine control module to help the transmission decide when and how to shift gears, so that the car can improve performance, shift smoothly, and save fuel. The function of the control module relay is to continue to keep the control module powered after the ignition switch is turned off until the control module completes the shutdown process.

des: Positive Crankcase Ventilation Heater Control Circuit /Open
knowledge: The function of the crankcase positive ventilation (PCV) system is to introduce the blowby gas in the crankcase (at the end of the engine's combustion process, some unburned mixture leaks from the piston ring into the crankcase under high pressure, and the industry calls this leakage blowby gas) into the intake manifold through the vacuum generated by the engine. Then the blowby gas will enter the cylinder together with the fresh air and burn, thereby reducing pollution and improving engine efficiency. This fault code indicates that the electronic control unit (PCV) detects that the crankcase positive ventilation heater circuit voltage is out of the normal range.

des: O2 Sensor Circuit Low Voltage (Bank 2, Sensor 2)
knowledge: The function of the oxygen sensor is to measure the oxygen content in the engine exhaust to correct the injection amount so that the engine can obtain the best air-fuel ratio. In the OBD fault code, you will often see the oxygen sensor in the row. The first row refers to the row where cylinder 1 is located, and the remaining row is the second row. Regardless of which row, the first sensor always refers to the upstream oxygen sensor (before the catalyst box), and the second sensor always refers to the downstream oxygen sensor (after the catalyst box). This fault code will appear when the voltage of the heated oxygen sensor signal is continuously lower than 156 millivolts within a set period of time. The causes of the fault include oxygen sensor contamination due to silicon in the fuel, oxygen sensor signal and ground circuit crossover, oxygen sensor signal circuit short circuit to ground, oxygen sensor itself failure, electronic control module (PCM or ECM) failure, etc.

des: Fuel Pump Secondary Circuit Intermittent
knowledge: The fuel pump circuit is divided into a main circuit and a secondary circuit. The main circuit is responsible for controlling the fuel pump. The fuel pump relay uses a low current from the electronic control unit (ECU) to control the electromagnetic coil, thereby connecting the fuel pump high current. The secondary circuit refers to the fuel pump monitor (FPM) circuit, which is responsible for monitoring the circuit feedback of the fuel pump. The causes of P0233 include the circuit from the fuel pump monitor (FPM) to the fuel pump relay, the fuel pump relay circuit, the fuel pump relay, the electronic control unit (ECU), etc.

des: Fuel Composition Sensor Circuit Low
knowledge: The function of the fuel composition sensor is to transmit the ethanol content in gasoline to the electronic control unit (ECU) in the form of an electrical signal as a basis for modifying the injector pulse width and ignition timing. If the ECU detects that the fuel composition sensor signal voltage is lower than the calibrated minimum value, this fault code will appear.

des: Fuel Pump Module Control Circuit/Open
knowledge: The fuel pump control module (FPM, or FPCM) is a computer microprocessor that controls the voltage to the fuel pump (usually located in the fuel tank) in order to achieve the optimal fuel pressure required by the electronic control module (ECU).

des: Evaporative Emission System Purge Control Valve Circuit Shorted
knowledge: The evaporative emissions (EVAP) system directs gasoline vapor from the fuel tank into a tank containing activated carbon that absorbs gasoline vapor. The engine then uses fresh air to purge the gasoline vapor into the engine combustion chamber. This fault code will appear if the electronic control unit (ECU) detects a short circuit in the evaporative emissions system purge solenoid valve control circuit. Fault causes include EVAP power supply circuit failure, EVAP solenoid valve control circuit failure, EVAP solenoid valve failure, EVAP charcoal canister leakage, electronic control module (PCM or ECM) failure, etc.

des: Drive Motor A Temperature Sensor Circuit Intermittent
knowledge: The temperature sensor circuit of the drive motor A is faulty. The causes of the fault include the circuit, connector, electronic control unit, drive motor, etc. The drive motor temperature sensor of some vehicles is integrated with the drive motor. Therefore, if it is determined that the problem is with the temperature sensor itself, it may be necessary to replace the entire drive motor.

des: Exhaust Gas Recirculation Sensor A Circuit High
knowledge: The function of the exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) system is to introduce a small amount of exhaust gas into the intake manifold when the engine is running at high load. The presence of these exhaust gases reduces the temperature and pressure of the combustion chamber, thereby reducing the emission of nitrogen oxide pollutants. If the electronic control unit (ECU) detects that the signal voltage of the exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) sensor is higher than the calibrated maximum value, this fault code will appear. The causes of the fault include DPFE sensor connector failure, circuit short circuit to the positive pole, sensor failure, electronic control module (PCM or ECM) failure, etc.

des: Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch D Circuit High
knowledge: The shift solenoid valve controls the hydraulic pressure to the transmission clutch by opening or closing the transmission fluid control valve to control its separation and engagement, thereby achieving gear shifting. Accurate control of the transmission fluid pressure is very important for smooth gear shifting. The function of the transmission fluid pressure (TFP) sensor is to transmit the transmission fluid pressure in the form of an electrical signal to the transmission control module (TCU) as a reference for the operation of the transmission fluid pressure control solenoid valve.

des: Exhaust Valve Control Solenoid Circuit Low (Bank 2)
knowledge: The function of the camshaft is to control the opening and closing of the valves. In the variable valve timing system, the electronic camshaft adjustment valve (or oil control valve, OCV) adjusts the angle of the camshaft by changing the oil pressure to the camshaft adjuster (mechanical) according to the command from the engine control module (ECM) to ensure that the valves open and close at the best time. If the exhaust camshaft adjustment valve circuit voltage is lower than the calibrated minimum value, this fault code will appear.

des: Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch H Circuit Intermittent
knowledge: The shift solenoid valve controls the hydraulic pressure to the transmission clutch by opening or closing the transmission fluid control valve to control its separation and engagement, thereby achieving gear shifting. Accurate control of the transmission fluid pressure is very important for smooth gear shifting. The function of the transmission fluid pressure (TFP) sensor is to transmit the transmission fluid pressure in the form of an electrical signal to the transmission control module (TCU) as a reference for the operation of the transmission fluid pressure control solenoid valve.

des: Drive Motor B Phase V Current Low
knowledge: The Hybrid Vehicle Electronic Control Unit (HV ECU) is responsible for monitoring the drive motor inverter current sensor. If the HV ECU detects an error, this fault code will appear.

des: Ignition/Distributor Engine Speed Input Circuit
knowledge: This fault code will appear if the electronic control unit (ECU) detects 2 consecutive unstable Hall pickup (PIP) pulses on the input signal from the engine speed sensor to the ECU. Fault causes include ignition coil, distributor, ignition control module, engine speed sensor, crankshaft position (CKP) sensor, circuit, connector, etc.

des: Output Speed Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
knowledge: The task of the output speed sensor (OSS) is to transmit the speed signal of the transmission output shaft to the electronic control unit (ECU). When the car is running normally, if the ECU detects interference with the OSS signal, this fault code will appear. The causes of the fault include interference of the OSS sensor by non-standard accessories, failure of the OSS sensor itself, circuit or connector failure, electronic control module (PCM or ECM) failure, etc.

des: Hybrid Battery Temperature Sensor C Range/Performance
knowledge: The battery control module controls the opening/closing of the battery fan based on the signal from the battery temperature sensor. If the battery control module detects an error in the battery temperature sensor signal circuit, this fault code will appear.

des: Crankcase Pressure Sensor Circuit Low
knowledge: The function of the crankcase pressure sensor is to transmit the pressure in the crankcase to the electronic control unit (ECU) in the form of an electrical signal to detect the working status of the crankcase forced ventilation system. If the ECU detects that the voltage of the crankcase pressure sensor signal circuit is lower than the calibrated minimum value, this fault code will appear.

des: Unable to Engage Gear 1
knowledge: The shift solenoid valve controls the hydraulic pressure to the transmission clutch by opening or closing the transmission fluid control valve to control its separation and engagement, thereby achieving gear shifting. The causes of this fault code include low transmission fluid level, dirty transmission fluid, mechanical failure of the shift solenoid valve, circuit, connector, or transmission control module (TCM) failure, etc.

des: Shift Solenoid A Control Circuit Low
knowledge: The shift solenoid valve controls the hydraulic pressure to the transmission clutch by opening or closing the transmission fluid control valve to control its separation and engagement, thereby achieving gear shifting. The causes of this fault code include low transmission fluid level, dirty transmission fluid, mechanical failure of the shift solenoid valve, circuit, connector, or transmission control module (TCM) failure, etc.

des: Injector Circuit/Open - Cylinder 2
knowledge: The function of the fuel injector is to atomize the fuel so that it meets the requirements of combustion. The working principle is that when the electromagnetic coil is energized, suction is generated, the needle valve is sucked up, the spray hole is opened, and the fuel is sprayed out at high speed through the annular gap between the needle pin at the head of the needle valve and the spray hole to form a mist. The electronic control unit controls the injection amount by controlling the time interval (also called pulse width) of the injector opening. If the electronic control unit (ECU) detects an error in the injector control circuit, this fault code will appear. The causes of the fault include injector interface, circuit failure, injector failure, electronic control module (PCM or ECM) failure, etc.

des: Pressure Control Solenoid B
knowledge: The shift solenoid valve controls the hydraulic pressure to the transmission clutch by opening or closing the transmission fluid control valve to control its separation and engagement, thereby achieving gear shifting. Accurate control of the transmission fluid pressure is very important for smooth gear shifting. The function of the pressure control solenoid valve is to control the pressure of the transmission fluid. Fault causes include the pressure control solenoid valve control circuit, connector, or the solenoid valve itself. A control module fault will also cause this fault code to appear.

des: Hybrid Battery B Voltage Low

In the OBD fault code, you will often see the oxygen sensor in the bank. Bank 1 refers to the bank where cylinder 1 is located, and the remaining bank is bank 2. Regardless of which bank, the first sensor always refers to the upstream oxygen sensor (before the catalyst box), and the second sensor always refers to the downstream oxygen sensor (after the catalyst box). The electronic control unit (ECU) continuously monitors the heated oxygen sensor to determine that the oxygen sensor is working. If the heated oxygen sensor signal value continues to stay at the default value, the electronic control unit (ECU) will command an oscillating air/fuel ratio to try to detect some changes in the signal value. If the ECU still cannot detect changes in the sensor's signal at this time, this fault code will appear. The causes of the fault include leaks in the exhaust manifold or exhaust pipe, faults in the oxygen sensor itself or its circuit or connector, and faults in the electronic control module (PCM or ECM).

des: Cruise Control Vacuum Control Circuit Low

When the set speed is reached, the vacuum solenoid valve and the ventilation solenoid valve are closed at the same time. At this time, the vacuum in the sealing sleeve remains unchanged, and the car maintains a constant speed. When deceleration is required, the ventilation solenoid valve opens to allow air to enter the sealing sleeve, the diaphragm spring presses the diaphragm back to its original position, the throttle opening decreases, and the car decelerates. P0583 indicates that the vacuum control circuit voltage is lower than the calibrated minimum value. The causes of the fault include the cruise control vacuum control solenoid valve, circuit, connector, etc.

Most cars have fuel pressure regulators located on the fuel rail, but some cars have fuel pressure regulators located inside the fuel tank. If the electronic control unit (ECU) detects that the voltage of the fuel pressure regulator 1 control circuit is lower than the calibrated minimum value, this fault code will appear.

Hybrid Battery Voltage Sense H Circuit
knowledge: The function of the hybrid battery voltage monitoring circuit is to transmit the battery block voltage to the control module to monitor the charging and discharging of the battery block, as well as possible short circuits and open circuits.

des: Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Sensor A Circuit Range/Performance
knowledge: A turbocharger uses the inertial force of the exhaust gas discharged by the engine to drive the turbine, which in turn drives the coaxial impeller to increase the intake pressure, thereby increasing the power of the car. A supercharger is an air compressor used to increase the intake air for an internal combustion engine. More intake air provides more oxygen to the engine, allowing the control module to provide more fuel, thereby increasing the output power. The boost pressure sensor, also called the boost pressure sensor (BPS), is used to transmit the boost pressure to the electronic control unit (ECU) in the form of an electrical signal. If the ECU detects an error in the boost pressure sensor (BPS) signal circuit, this fault code will appear.

des: Hybrid Battery Pack Coolant Pump Supply Voltage Circuit High
Drive Motor Inverter Temperature Sensor F Circuit Range/Performance
knowledge: The inverter converts DC power into AC power. The hybrid electronic control unit (HV ECU) uses a temperature sensor integrated in the inverter to monitor the temperature of the drive motor inverter. If the output of this temperature sensor is abnormal, this fault code will appear.

des: Drive Motor Inverter Temperature Sensor B Circuit High
knowledge: The inverter converts DC power into AC power. The hybrid electronic control unit (HV ECU) uses a temperature sensor integrated in the inverter to monitor the temperature of the drive motor inverter. If the output of this temperature sensor is abnormal, this fault code will appear.

des: PCM/ECM/TCU Internal Temperature Sensor A Range/Performance
knowledge: The engine control module, also called the engine control unit (the engine control module and transmission control module on some cars are integrated into the powertrain control module), controls the operation of the entire engine. Its most important function is to control the optimal fuel injection amount and ignition timing of the engine. Another important function is to monitor the components responsible for exhaust emission control. The transmission control module (TCM or TCU) collects information from various sensors and the engine control module to help the transmission decide when and how to shift gears, so that the car can improve performance, shift smoothly, and save fuel. This fault code indicates that the voltage of the temperature sensor signal circuit inside the control module is wrong. The cause of the fault is the internal temperature sensor, circuit, connector, or control module.

des: Mass or Volume Air Flow Sensor A/B Correlation
knowledge: The function of the mass air flow (MAF) sensor is to convert the air flow into an electrical signal and send it to the electronic control unit (ECU) as one of the basic signals for determining the amount of fuel injection. If the signal difference between the mass air flow (MAF) sensors A and B detected by the ECU exceeds the set maximum value, this fault code will appear.

des: Shift Solenoid C Control Circuit High
knowledge: The shift solenoid valve controls the hydraulic pressure to the transmission clutch by opening or closing the transmission fluid control valve to control its separation and engagement, thereby achieving gear shifting. The causes of this fault code include low transmission fluid level, dirty transmission fluid, mechanical failure of the shift solenoid valve, circuit, connector, or transmission control module (TCM) failure, etc.

des: Camshaft Position Sensor A Circuit (Bank 2)
knowledge: The function of the camshaft is to control the opening and closing of the valves. In the variable valve timing system, the electronic camshaft adjustment valve (or oil control valve, OCV) adjusts the angle of the camshaft according to the instructions from the engine control module (ECM) by changing the oil pressure to the camshaft adjuster (mechanical type) to ensure that the valves open and close at the best time. The function of the camshaft position (CMP) sensor is to transmit the camshaft position (relative position of the valve) to the electronic control unit (ECU) in the form of a voltage signal. If the electronic control unit (ECU) fails to detect the A (intake/left/front) camshaft position (CMP) sensor signal within the set time period, this fault code will appear. The causes of the fault include the camshaft position (CMP) sensor circuit, connector, its own fault, or electronic control module (PCM or ECM) fault, etc.

des: Drive Motor Inverter Temperature Sensor F Circuit
knowledge: The inverter converts DC power into AC power. The hybrid electronic control unit (HV ECU) uses a temperature sensor integrated in the inverter to monitor the temperature of the drive motor inverter. If the output of this temperature sensor is abnormal, this fault code will appear.

des: Hybrid Battery Temperature Sensor H Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
knowledge: The battery control module controls the battery fan on/off based on the signal from the battery temperature sensor. If the battery control module detects a sudden change in the voltage of the battery temperature sensor signal circuit, this fault code will appear.

des: 14 Volt Power Module Current Sensor Circuit
Transmission Mode Switch B Circuit
knowledge: The function of the transmission mode switch is to instruct the transmission to shift earlier or later, or start in high gear, etc. according to the mode selected by the user (sports/economy/winter, etc.). Fault causes include the transmission mode switch, circuit, connector, or control module.

des: Exhaust Gas Recirculation B Control Position Exceeded Learning Limit
knowledge: The exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) system is used to introduce a small amount of exhaust gas into the intake manifold when the engine is running at high load. The presence of these exhaust gases reduces the temperature and pressure of the combustion chamber, thereby reducing the emission of nitrogen oxide pollutants.

des: Cylinder 10 Injector Circuit Low
knowledge: The function of the fuel injector is to atomize the fuel so that it meets the requirements of combustion. The working principle is that when the electromagnetic coil is energized, suction is generated, the needle valve is sucked up, the spray hole is opened, and the fuel is sprayed out at high speed through the annular gap between the needle pin at the head of the needle valve and the spray hole to form a mist. The electronic control unit controls the injection amount by controlling the time interval (also called pulse width) of the injector opening. If the voltage of the 10th cylinder injector control circuit is lower than the calibrated minimum value, this fault code will appear. The causes of the fault include the injector control circuit, connector, or the injector itself; injector control module (FICM).

des: Gate Select Control Error

des: Drive Motor A Current Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
knowledge: Internal malfunction of the hybrid vehicle electronic control unit (HV ECU).

This fault code indicates that the flow rate of exhaust gas recirculation B is lower than the normal range.

des: Engine Coolant Temperature Sensor 1 Circuit Intermittent
knowledge: The engine coolant temperature (ECT) sensor transmits the temperature of the engine coolant in the form of an electrical signal to the electronic control unit (ECU) through the principle of thermistor, as a basis for correcting injection and ignition. If the ECU detects that the coolant temperature sensor (for cars not equipped with a coolant temperature sensor, this refers to the cylinder head temperature sensor) circuit is intermittently open or short-circuited when the engine is running, this fault code will appear.

knowledge: The function of the camshaft is to control the opening and closing of the valves. In the variable valve timing system, the electronic camshaft adjustment valve (or oil control valve, OCV) adjusts the angle of the camshaft according to the instructions from the engine control module (ECM) by changing the oil pressure to the camshaft adjuster (mechanical type) to ensure that the valves open and close at the best time. This optimizes the efficiency and power of the engine in all speed ranges. If the electronic control unit (ECU) detects that the voltage of the A (intake/left/front) camshaft profile control circuit is lower than the calibrated minimum value for a period of time, this fault code will appear.

des: Ignition Coil L Primary/Secondary Circuit
knowledge: The function of the ignition coil is to convert the 12 volt voltage of the car battery into thousands or even tens of thousands of volts required for spark plug ignition. There are two sets of coils in the ignition coil, the primary coil and the secondary coil. The primary coil has thicker enameled wire and fewer turns; the secondary coil uses thinner enameled wire and has relatively more turns. When the primary coil is connected to the power supply, a strong magnetic field is generated around it as the current increases, and the iron core stores the magnetic field energy; when the switch device disconnects the primary coil circuit, the magnetic field of the primary coil decays rapidly, and the secondary coil will induce a high voltage. The electronic control unit (ECU) continuously monitors each ignition main circuit. If the ECU does not receive a valid ignition diagnostic monitor (IDM) pulse signal from the ignition module (integrated in the ECU), this fault code will appear. The causes of the fault include ignition start/run circuit, ignition coil circuit, ignition coil itself, electronic control module (PCM or ECM) failure, etc.

des: Shift Solenoid H
knowledge: The shift solenoid valve controls the hydraulic pressure to the transmission clutch by opening or closing the transmission fluid control valve to control its separation and engagement, thereby achieving gear shifting. The causes of this fault code include low transmission fluid level, dirty transmission fluid, mechanical failure of the shift solenoid valve, circuit, connector, or transmission control module (TCM) failure, etc.

des: Cylinder 6 - Injector Leaking
knowledge: The function of the fuel injector is to atomize the fuel so that it meets the requirements of combustion. The working principle is that when the electromagnetic coil is energized, suction is generated, the needle valve is sucked up, the spray hole is opened, and the fuel is sprayed out at high speed through the annular gap between the needle pin at the head of the needle valve and the spray hole to form a mist. The electronic control unit controls the injection amount by controlling the time interval (also called pulse width) of the fuel injector opening. This fault code indicates that the fuel injector of the 6th cylinder is leaking.

des: Exhaust Gas Recirculation Temperature Sensor A Circuit
knowledge: The function of the exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) system is to introduce a small amount of exhaust gas into the intake manifold when the engine is running at high load. The presence of these exhaust gases reduces the temperature and pressure of the combustion chamber, thereby reducing the emission of nitrogen oxide pollutants. If the electronic control unit (ECU) detects that the signal voltage of the exhaust gas recirculation valve (EGR) temperature sensor exceeds the normal range of calibration, this fault code will appear.

des: Transmission Park Position Sensor/Switch B Circuit Performance High
knowledge: The function of the parking position sensor is to send a signal to the electronic control unit (ECU) indicating whether the gear lever is in the parking position. If the ECU detects an error in the parking position sensor circuit, this fault code will appear.

des: Drive Motor A Phase W Current Sensor Circuit
knowledge: The Hybrid Vehicle Electronic Control Unit (HV ECU) is responsible for monitoring the drive motor inverter current sensor. If the HV ECU detects an error, this fault code will appear.

des: Hybrid Battery Voltage Sense V Circuit High
knowledge: The function of the hybrid battery voltage monitoring circuit is to transmit the battery block voltage to the control module to monitor the charging and discharging of the battery block, as well as possible short circuits and open circuits.

des: Exhaust Gas Recirculation A Control Circuit Low
knowledge: The function of the exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) system is to introduce a small amount of exhaust gas into the intake manifold when the engine is running at high load. If the electronic control unit (ECU) detects that the exhaust gas recirculation sensor A signal voltage is lower than the calibrated minimum value, this fault code will appear.
