knowledge: The function of the hybrid battery voltage monitoring circuit is to transmit the battery block voltage to the control module to monitor the charging and discharging of the battery block, as well as possible short circuits and open circuits.

des: Cylinder 8 Misfire Detected
knowledge: Cylinder misfire refers to the phenomenon that the mixture cannot burn normally in the cylinder due to various reasons during the operation of the engine. If the electronic control unit (ECU) detects a misfire that may damage the catalytic converter, the fault indicator light will flash and the engine should be turned off immediately. This fault code indicates that the electronic control unit (ECU) has detected a misfire in cylinder 8. The causes of the fault include ignition system failure, fuel delivery failure, air leakage in the intake manifold or EGR, PCV, mechanical cylinder failure, etc.

des: Hybrid Battery Pack Cooling Fan 2 Stuck On
knowledge: The battery control module controls the battery fan to turn on or off based on the signal from the battery temperature sensor. If the actual battery pack temperature is lower than the battery pack temperature estimated based on the cooling fan performance by a set value, the control module considers the battery pack fan to be stuck in the on position.

des: Sensor Reference Voltage C Circuit/Open
knowledge: The electronic control unit (ECU) has detected an error in the 5 volt reference voltage circuit C. Causes of the fault include a short circuit or short circuit from the 5 volt reference voltage circuit to a sensor, a short circuit or open circuit in one or more sensors, the ECU, etc.

des: Exhaust Gas Recirculation A Control Circuit High
knowledge: The function of the exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) system is to introduce a small amount of exhaust gas into the intake manifold when the engine is running at high load. The presence of these exhaust gases reduces the temperature and pressure of the combustion chamber, thereby reducing the emission of nitrogen oxide pollutants. If the electronic control unit (ECU) detects that the signal voltage of the exhaust gas recirculation sensor A is higher than the calibrated maximum value, this fault code will appear.

des: Cruise Control System - Vehicle Speed Too High
knowledge: The cruise control system allows the driver to automatically maintain the vehicle speed without stepping on the accelerator pedal.

des: Timing Reference High Resolution Signal B
knowledge: The optical sensor provides a high-resolution signal to the Powertrain Control Module (PCM) by counting the pulses on the sensor disk located inside the injection pump. This signal is one of the important references for the PCM to control fuel and timing. The causes of this fault code include the optical sensor, its circuit, connector or PCM.

des: Transmission Park Position Sensor/Switch B Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
knowledge: The function of the parking position sensor is to send a signal to the electronic control unit (ECU) indicating whether the gear lever is in the parking position. If the ECU detects a sudden change in the voltage of the parking position sensor circuit, this fault code will appear.

des: Drive Motor Inverter Temperature Sensor C Circuit High
knowledge: The inverter converts DC power into AC power. The hybrid electronic control unit (HV ECU) uses a temperature sensor integrated in the inverter to monitor the temperature of the drive motor inverter. If the output of this temperature sensor is abnormal, this fault code will appear.

des: Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch C Circuit Range/Performance
knowledge: The shift solenoid valve controls the hydraulic pressure to the transmission clutch by opening or closing the transmission fluid control valve to control its separation and engagement, thereby achieving gear shifting. Accurate control of the transmission fluid pressure is very important for smooth gear shifting. The function of the transmission fluid pressure (TFP) sensor is to transmit the transmission fluid pressure in the form of an electrical signal to the transmission control module (TCU) as a reference for the operation of the transmission fluid pressure control solenoid valve.

des: O2 Sensor Circuit (Bank 2, Sensor 1)
knowledge: The function of the oxygen sensor is to measure the oxygen content in the engine exhaust to correct the injection amount so that the engine can obtain the best air-fuel ratio. In the OBD fault code, you will often see the oxygen sensor in the row. The first row refers to the row where cylinder 1 is located, and the remaining row is the second row. Regardless of which row, the first sensor always refers to the upstream oxygen sensor (before the catalyst box), and the second sensor always refers to the downstream oxygen sensor (after the catalyst box). The electronic control unit (ECU) monitors the circuit of the heated oxygen sensor. When the ECU detects a problem with the circuit used to measure the oxygen content in the exhaust gas, this fault code will appear. The causes of the fault include leakage in the exhaust manifold or exhaust pipe, failure of the oxygen sensor itself or its circuit or connector, and failure of the electronic control module (PCM or ECM).

des: Turbocharger/Supercharger Wastegate Solenoid B High
knowledge: A turbocharger uses the inertial force of the exhaust gas discharged by the engine to drive the turbine, which in turn drives the coaxial impeller to increase the intake pressure, thereby increasing the power of the vehicle. A supercharger is an air compressor used to increase the intake air for an internal combustion engine. More intake air provides more oxygen to the engine, allowing the control module to provide more fuel, thereby increasing output power. The function of the wastegate solenoid valve is to adjust the turbine speed and thus the maximum boost pressure by controlling the exhaust gas flow entering the turbine (bypassing the rest of the exhaust gas). If the electronic control unit (ECU) detects that the voltage of the wastegate solenoid valve B circuit is higher than the calibrated maximum value, this fault code will appear.

des: Traction Control Input Signal High
knowledge: The function of the drive anti-skid traction control (TCS) system is to control the torque output by delaying the ignition time, shifting up early, starting in second gear, preventing the torque converter from locking, and braking to prevent skidding when the drive wheel slips.

des: Park/Neutral Switch Input Circuit
knowledge: The function of the park/neutral position switch is to transmit information about whether the automatic transmission is in park/neutral or other gears to the electronic control unit (ECU) as a reference for determining whether the engine is idling or increasing the load. The switch is also used in the starter relay circuit to prevent the car from starting in gears other than park/neutral.

des: Glow Plug Sense Circuit
knowledge: The function of the glow plug is to heat the compressed gas in the diesel engine combustion chamber through the electric heating coil, so that the diesel engine can be started easily in cold weather. The glow plug control module can automate the preheating and cycling process of the glow plug. This fault code indicates that the glow plug monitoring circuit has a fault.

des: Cylinder 9 - Injector Leaking
knowledge: The function of the fuel injector is to atomize the fuel so that it meets the requirements of combustion. The working principle is that when the electromagnetic coil is energized, suction is generated, the needle valve is sucked up, the spray hole is opened, and the fuel is sprayed out at high speed through the annular gap between the needle pin at the head of the needle valve and the spray hole to form a mist. The electronic control unit controls the injection amount by controlling the time interval (also called pulse width) of the fuel injector opening. This fault code indicates that the 9th cylinder fuel injector is leaking.

des: A Camshaft Position - Timing Over-Retarded (Bank 2)
knowledge: The function of the camshaft is to control the opening and closing of the valve. In the variable valve timing system, the electronic camshaft adjustment valve (or oil control valve, OCV) adjusts the angle of the camshaft according to the command from the engine control module (ECM) by changing the oil pressure to the camshaft adjuster (mechanical type) to ensure that the valve opens and closes at the best time. The causes of P0022 include A intake/left/front camshaft timing is not set properly, the camshaft is mechanically stuck, or the actuator valve is stuck in the open position.

des: Intake Air Temperature Too High
knowledge: The function of the intake air temperature (IAT) sensor is to transmit the engine's intake air temperature to the electronic control unit (ECU) in the form of a voltage signal, providing a reference for injection correction. If the ECU detects that the intake air temperature (IAT) sensor signal is too high, this fault code will appear. Fault causes include (turbocharger) intercooler pump failure, intercooler coolant is too low, etc.

des: Internal Control Module Engine Air Mass Performance
knowledge: The engine control module, also called the engine control unit (the engine control module and the transmission control module on some vehicles are integrated into a powertrain control module), controls the operation of the entire engine. Its most important function is to control the optimal fuel injection amount and ignition timing of the engine. Another important function is to monitor the exhaust emission control components.

des: Knock Sensor 3 Circuit Range/Performance (Bank 1)
knowledge: The knock sensor is responsible for detecting vibrations when the engine speed changes. The knock sensor then expresses this vibration in the form of a voltage. When necessary, the electronic control module (ECU) will delay the ignition to prevent knocking. If this voltage is wrong, this fault code will appear.

des: Secondary Air Injection System Insufficient Flow (Bank 1)
knowledge: When the engine is just started, the secondary air injection system (AIR) oxidizes the hydrocarbons, carbon monoxide and other harmful gases by forcing air into the exhaust manifold. This process also accelerates the warming process of the catalytic converter. If the electronic control unit (ECU) finds that there is not enough air flow change when the secondary air injection system pump is alternately turned on and off, this fault code will appear. The causes of the fault include air pump output blockage, AIR bypass solenoid valve leakage or blockage, AIR bypass solenoid valve stuck, valve failure, electronic air injection pump pipeline leakage, electronic air injection pump failure, electronic control module (PCM or ECM) failure, etc.

des: Intermediate Shaft Speed Sensor A Circuit Intermittent
knowledge: The main components of the transmission include the planetary gear system located on the intermediate shaft. One end of it is connected to the input shaft and the other end is connected to the output shaft. The causes of failure include the intermediate shaft speed (ISS) sensor, circuit, connector, control module, etc.

des: Battery Temperature Sensor Circuit
knowledge: The battery temperature sensor is located at the bottom of the vehicle battery tray. Its main function is to transmit the battery temperature to the electronic control unit (ECU) in the form of an electrical signal to help determine the charging speed. This fault code indicates that the battery temperature sensor circuit is faulty.

des: Cylinder 2 Contribution/Balance
knowledge: The Electronic Control Unit (ECU) has detected that the crankshaft acceleration contribution of cylinder 2 is lower than the calibrated value. Fault causes include the cylinder 2 injection system; or other engine problems affecting cylinder 2.

des: Hybrid Powertrain Control Module
knowledge: An internal fault has occurred in the Hybrid Vehicle Electronic Control Unit (HV ECU).

des: Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch C Circuit Intermittent
knowledge: The shift solenoid valve controls the hydraulic pressure to the transmission clutch by opening or closing the transmission fluid control valve to control its separation and engagement, thereby achieving gear shifting. Accurate control of the transmission fluid pressure is very important for smooth gear shifting. The function of the transmission fluid pressure (TFP) sensor is to transmit the transmission fluid pressure in the form of an electrical signal to the transmission control module (TCU) as a reference for the operation of the transmission fluid pressure control solenoid valve.

des: Cylinder 5 - Fuel Trim at Max Limit
knowledge: Fuel trimming refers to the electronic control unit (ECU) controlling fuel delivery by increasing or decreasing the time the injectors are open to achieve the best air-fuel ratio (14.7:1 air-to-gasoline mass ratio) for the engine. Too rich an air-fuel ratio means too much fuel is delivered, and too lean an air-fuel ratio means too little fuel is delivered. This fault code will appear if fuel trim reaches and stays at the maximum limit for more than a certain period of time.

des: Fuel Tank System/Large Leak Detected - Mechanical Fault
knowledge: The evaporative emissions (EVAP) system directs gasoline vapors from the fuel tank into a tank containing activated carbon that absorbs gasoline vapors. The engine then uses fresh air to purge these gasoline vapors into the engine combustion chamber. If the electronic control module detects a leak in the fuel tank system that is larger than a certain diameter, this fault code will appear. Fault causes include the fuel tank cap not being tightened, other leaks related to the fuel tank system, etc.

des: Secondary Air Injection System - Insufficient Flow Detected (Bank 1)
knowledge: When the engine is just started, the secondary air injection system oxidizes the hydrocarbons, carbon monoxide and other harmful gases produced by forcing air into the exhaust manifold. This process also accelerates the warming process of the catalytic converter.

des: Secondary Air Injection System - Insufficient Flow Detected (Bank 1)
knowledge: When the engine is just started, the secondary air injection system oxidizes the hydrocarbons, carbon monoxide and other harmful gases produced by forcing air into the exhaust manifold. This process also accelerates the warming process of the catalytic converter.

des: Evaporative Emission (EVAP) Canister Purge Valve, Vent Control - Voltage High
knowledge: The evaporative emissions (EVAP) system directs gasoline vapors from the fuel tank into a tank containing activated carbon that absorbs the gasoline vapors. The engine then uses fresh air to purge the gasoline vapors into the engine combustion chamber.

knowledge: The evaporative emissions (EVAP) system directs gasoline vapors from the fuel tank into a tank containing activated carbon that absorbs the gasoline vapors. The engine then uses fresh air to purge the gasoline vapors into the engine combustion chamber.

des: Secondary Air Injection System - Insufficient Flow Detected
knowledge: When the engine is just started, the secondary air injection system oxidizes the hydrocarbons, carbon monoxide and other harmful gases produced by forcing air into the exhaust manifold. This process also accelerates the warming process of the catalytic converter.

des: A/C Compressor Clutch Relay - Voltage High
knowledge: The air conditioner pulley just idles when the air conditioner is turned off. Only when the air conditioner clutch (under the action of the solenoid valve) is engaged, will the compressor be driven to operate. The function of the air conditioner clutch relay is to control the separation and engagement of the clutch.

des: Engine Fuel Shutoff Solenoid - Malfunction
knowledge: The function of the fuel shut-off valve is to cut off the fuel supply to the engine in the event of an emergency (such as a rollover).

des: Intake Manifold Runner Control - Stuck Open (Bank 1)
knowledge: The intake manifold passage control (IMRC) assembly is located between the intake manifold and the cylinder head. To improve engine performance, each cylinder corresponds to two intake passages, one of which is always open and the other is opened only when the speed is higher than a certain value (for example, 3000RPM). The function of the IMRC actuator motor is to open/close the valve flap of the intake passage according to the command of the electronic control unit (ECU). Fault causes include short circuit of the IMRC monitor signal circuit, IMRC actuator failure, electronic control module (PCM or ECM) failure, etc.

des: Intake Manifold Air Control System, Bank 1 - Valve Stuck Open (Sagem/Lucas GEMS 8.2)
knowledge: The intake manifold air control (IMAC) assembly is located between the intake manifold and the cylinder head. To improve engine performance, each cylinder has two intake passages, one of which is always open and the other is opened only when the speed is higher than a certain value (for example, 3000RPM). The function of the IMAC actuator motor is to open/close the valve flap of the intake passage according to the instructions of the electronic control unit (ECU). Fault causes include short circuit of the IMRC monitor signal circuit, IMRC actuator failure, electronic control module (PCM or ECM) failure, etc.

des: A/C Compressor Request, Compressor Relay - Short to Ground (Except Sagem/Lucas GEMS 8.2)
knowledge: The function of the air conditioning compressor is to pressurize the refrigerant to help it liquefy after passing through the condenser. The liquefied high-temperature and high-pressure refrigerant vaporizes and absorbs heat in the process of flowing to the evaporator, thereby achieving a cooling effect. The power of the car air conditioner is directly provided by the engine through a belt transmission.

des: Ignition Coil/Amplifier, Cylinder 2 - Short to Positive
knowledge: The function of the ignition coil is to convert the 12 volt voltage of the car battery into thousands or even tens of thousands of volts required for spark plug ignition. There are two sets of coils in the ignition coil, the primary coil and the secondary coil. The primary coil has thicker enameled wire and fewer turns; the secondary coil uses thinner enameled wire and has relatively more turns. When the primary coil is connected to the power supply, a strong magnetic field is generated around it as the current increases, and the iron core stores the magnetic field energy; when the switch device disconnects the primary coil circuit, the magnetic field of the primary coil decays rapidly, and the secondary coil will induce a very high voltage. New cars no longer use distributors, but electronically control multiple independent ignition coils to provide ignition for individual cylinders.

knowledge: The function of the ignition coil is to convert the 12 volt voltage of the car battery into thousands or even tens of thousands of volts required for spark plug ignition. There are two sets of coils in the ignition coil, the primary coil and the secondary coil. The primary coil has thicker enameled wire and fewer turns; the secondary coil uses thinner enameled wire and has relatively more turns. When the primary coil is connected to the power supply, a strong magnetic field is generated around it as the current increases, and the iron core stores the magnetic field energy; when the switch device disconnects the primary coil circuit, the magnetic field of the primary coil decays rapidly, and the secondary coil will induce a very high voltage.

More intake air provides more oxygen to the engine, allowing the control module to provide more fuel, thereby increasing the output power. To prevent the turbo/supercharger from over-boosting, when the pressure reaches the set maximum value, the air pressure will push the wastegate actuator (pneumatic mechanical type) to bypass part of the exhaust gas from the turbine, thereby reducing the turbine speed and reducing the boost level. The camshaft does not directly control the valve, but pushes the valve through a multi-stage rocker arm. At low speeds, the rocker arm corresponding to the larger angle cam is allowed to idle, and the smaller angle cam is used to push the valve. When the speed reaches the set critical point, the latch moves to fix the entire rocker arm, allowing the larger angle cam to push the entire rocker arm, while the smaller angle cam will idle because it cannot touch the rocker arm, so as to achieve the purpose of two-stage control of valve timing and lift. This fault code indicates that the electronic control module has detected a VTEC (variable timing electronic control) operation fault. The cause of the fault indicates a VTEC solenoid valve fault, a VTEC switch fault, an electronic control module (PCM or ECM) fault, etc.

des: Fuel Pressure Sensor - Implausible Signal
knowledge: The fuel pressure regulator uses a spring-loaded valve to return excess fuel to the tank, thereby maintaining constant pressure in the fuel line. The fuel pressure regulator has a vacuum line connected to the intake manifold to provide appropriate fuel pressure under different engine operating conditions (engine load is determined by the vacuum level). Most cars have the fuel pressure regulator located on the fuel rail, but some cars have the fuel pressure regulator located inside the fuel tank. The fuel pressure sensor is responsible for measuring the fuel pressure near the injector. The electronic control unit (ECU) uses this signal to adjust the injector pulse width and measure the amount of fuel entering the combustion chamber.

knowledge: The cruise control system controls the throttle angle and thus the vehicle speed by controlling the vacuum in the servo. When acceleration is required, the vacuum solenoid valve opens and communicates with the intake manifold (or a special vacuum pump). The vacuum degree in the sealing sleeve increases, sucking the diaphragm, overcoming the spring force, and increasing the throttle opening by pulling the wire, so that the vehicle accelerates. When the set speed is reached, the vacuum solenoid valve and the ventilation solenoid valve are closed at the same time. At this time, the vacuum degree in the sealing sleeve remains unchanged, and the car maintains a constant speed. When deceleration is required, the ventilation solenoid valve opens to allow air to enter the sealing sleeve, and the diaphragm spring presses the diaphragm back to its original position, the throttle opening decreases, and the car decelerates.

des: VTEC System Malfunction
knowledge: VTEC is the abbreviation of Variable Valve Timing and Valve Lift Electronic Control System. In a dual camshaft (DOHC) engine with VTEC, the camshaft that controls the intake valve has two sets of cams with different angles. The camshaft does not directly control the valve, but pushes the valve through a multi-stage rocker arm. At low speeds, the rocker arm corresponding to the larger angle cam is allowed to idle, and the cam with a smaller angle pushes the valve. When the speed reaches the set critical point, the latch moves to fix the entire rocker arm, allowing the larger angle cam to push the entire rocker arm, while the smaller angle cam will idle because it cannot touch the rocker arm, so as to achieve the purpose of two-stage control of valve timing and lift. This fault code indicates that the electronic control module detects that the voltage of the VTEC (variable timing electronic control) solenoid valve circuit is abnormal. The cause of the fault indicates that the VTEC solenoid valve control circuit is faulty, the VTEC solenoid valve is faulty, the electronic control module (PCM or ECM) is faulty, etc.

knowledge: The function of the ignition coil is to convert the 12 volt voltage of the car battery into thousands or even tens of thousands of volts required for spark plug ignition. There are two sets of coils in the ignition coil, the primary coil and the secondary coil. The primary coil has thicker enameled wire and fewer turns; the secondary coil uses thinner enameled wire and has relatively more turns. When the primary coil is connected to the power supply, a strong magnetic field is generated around it as the current increases, and the iron core stores the magnetic field energy; when the switch device disconnects the primary coil circuit, the magnetic field of the primary coil decays rapidly, and the secondary coil will induce a very high voltage. New cars no longer use distributors, but electronically control multiple independent ignition coils to provide ignition for individual cylinders.

des: Cruise Control Vent Solenoid
knowledge: The cruise control system controls the throttle angle and thus the vehicle speed by controlling the vacuum in the servo. When acceleration is required, the vacuum solenoid valve opens and communicates with the intake manifold (or a special vacuum pump). The vacuum in the sealing sleeve increases, sucking the diaphragm, overcoming the spring force, and increasing the throttle opening by pulling the wire, so that the vehicle accelerates. When the set speed is reached, the vacuum solenoid valve and the ventilation solenoid valve are closed at the same time. At this time, the vacuum in the sealing sleeve remains unchanged, and the car maintains a constant speed. When deceleration is required, the ventilation solenoid valve opens to allow air to enter the sealing sleeve, and the diaphragm spring presses the diaphragm back to its original position, the throttle opening decreases, and the car decelerates. This fault code indicates that the ventilation control solenoid valve of the cruise control system itself or its circuit is faulty, or the electronic control module (PCM or ECM) is faulty, etc.

des: Ignition Coil/Amplifier, Cylinder 1 - Circuit Open
knowledge: The function of the ignition coil is to convert the 12 volt voltage of the car battery into thousands or even tens of thousands of volts required for spark plug ignition. There are two sets of coils in the ignition coil, the primary coil and the secondary coil. The primary coil has thicker enameled wire and fewer turns; the secondary coil uses thinner enameled wire and has relatively more turns. When the primary coil is connected to the power supply, a strong magnetic field is generated around it as the current increases, and the iron core stores the magnetic field energy; when the switch device disconnects the primary coil circuit, the magnetic field of the primary coil decays rapidly, and the secondary coil will induce a very high voltage. New cars no longer use distributors, but electronically control multiple independent ignition coils to provide ignition for individual cylinders.

des: Fuel Trim - Rich Mixture (Bank 1)
knowledge: Fuel trimming refers to the electronic control unit (ECU) controlling fuel delivery by increasing or decreasing the injector opening time so that the engine can obtain the best air-fuel ratio (air to gasoline mass ratio of 14.7:1). Too rich an air-fuel ratio means that the fuel delivery is too large, and too lean an air-fuel ratio means that the fuel delivery is too small. Fault causes include air filter, evaporative emission (EVAP) system failure, high fuel pressure or injector leakage, oxygen sensor or its circuit, connector failure, etc.

Ignition Control Module - Ignition Coil Secondary Coil Signal, Circuit 1
knowledge: The ignition control module is a solid-state switching device that is responsible for controlling the operation of the ignition coil. The possible locations of the ignition control module are outside the engine, inside the distributor, and can also be integrated with the powertrain control module (PCM). The function of the ignition coil is to convert the 12 volt voltage of the car battery into thousands or even tens of thousands of volts required for spark plug ignition. There are two sets of coils in the ignition coil, the primary coil and the secondary coil. The primary coil has thicker enameled wire and fewer turns; the secondary coil uses thinner enameled wire and has relatively more turns. When the primary coil is connected to the power supply, a strong magnetic field is generated around it as the current increases, and the iron core stores the magnetic field energy; when the switch device disconnects the primary coil circuit, the magnetic field of the primary coil decays rapidly, and the secondary coil will induce a very high voltage.

The function of the coolant flow control valve is to allow coolant to flow between the cylinder head and the hot storage tank during preheating, and to allow coolant to flow between the cylinder head and the hot storage tank heater after normal operation. The primary coil has thicker enameled wire and fewer turns; the secondary coil uses thinner enameled wire and has relatively more turns. When the primary coil is connected to the power supply, a strong magnetic field is generated around it as the current increases, and the iron core stores the magnetic field energy; when the switch device disconnects the primary coil circuit, the magnetic field of the primary coil decays rapidly, and the secondary coil will induce a very high voltage. des: Ignition Coil/Amplifier, Cylinder 4 - Circuit Open
knowledge: The function of the ignition coil is to convert the 12 volt voltage of the car battery into thousands or even tens of thousands of volts required for spark plug ignition. There are two sets of coils in the ignition coil, the primary coil and the secondary coil. The primary coil has thicker enameled wire and fewer turns; the secondary coil uses thinner enameled wire and has relatively more turns. When the primary coil is connected to the power supply, a strong magnetic field is generated around it as the current increases, and the iron core stores the magnetic field energy; when the switch device disconnects the primary coil circuit, the magnetic field of the primary coil decays rapidly, and the secondary coil will induce a very high voltage. New cars no longer use distributors, but electronically control multiple independent ignition coils to provide ignition for individual cylinders.

des: Engine Control Module (ECM), Accelerator Pedal Position Sensor Signal via Controller Area Network (CAN) - Out of Range
knowledge: The engine control module, also called the engine control unit (in some cars, the engine control module and the transmission control module are integrated into a powertrain control module), controls the operation of the entire engine. In the electronic throttle control (ETC) system, the accelerator pedal position (APP) sensor is used to transmit the position of the accelerator pedal to the throttle control module in the form of an electrical signal, which serves as a reference for the throttle actuator to control the throttle valve opening. Controller Area Network (CAN) (Controller Area Network, referred to as CAN or CAN bus) is an automotive communication protocol, which allows devices on the network to communicate directly with each other, and the host does not need to control the communication on the network. If the transmission control module (TCM) does not receive a valid accelerator pedal position (APP) sensor signal from the powertrain control module (PCM) for more than 2 seconds, this fault code will appear.

des: Ignition Coil/Amplifier, Cylinder 4 - Short to Positive

There are two sets of coils in the ignition coil, the primary coil and the secondary coil. The primary coil has thicker enameled wire and fewer turns; the secondary coil uses thinner enameled wire and has relatively more turns. When the primary coil is connected to the power supply, a strong magnetic field is generated around it as the current increases, and the iron core stores the magnetic field energy; when the switch device disconnects the primary coil circuit, the magnetic field of the primary coil decays rapidly, and the secondary coil will induce a very high voltage. New cars no longer use distributors, but electronically control multiple independent ignition coils to provide ignition for individual cylinders.

des: Engine Control Module (ECM), Engine Coolant Temperature Sensor Signal via Controller Area Network (CAN)
knowledge: The engine control module, also called the engine control unit (in some cars, the engine control module and the transmission control module are integrated into a powertrain control module), controls the operation of the entire engine. Its most important function is to control the optimal fuel injection amount and ignition timing of the engine. Another important function is to monitor the exhaust emission control components. The engine coolant temperature (ECT) sensor transmits the temperature of the engine coolant to the electronic control unit (ECU) in the form of an electrical signal through the principle of thermistor, as a basis for correcting injection and ignition. Controller Area Network (CAN) (Controller Area Network, referred to as CAN or CAN bus) is an automotive communication protocol, which allows devices on the network to communicate directly with each other, and the host does not need to control the communication on the network. If the transmission control module (TCM) receives an invalid engine coolant temperature sensor signal from the powertrain control module (PCM) for more than 2 seconds, this fault code will appear.

des: Cruise Control Vacuum Switching Valve 3 - Circuit Malfunction

When the set speed is reached, the vacuum solenoid valve and the ventilation solenoid valve are closed at the same time. At this time, the vacuum degree in the sealing sleeve remains unchanged, and the car maintains a constant speed. des: Ignition Coil/Amplifier, Cylinder 6 - Short to Ground
knowledge: The function of the ignition coil is to convert the 12 volt voltage of the car battery into thousands or even tens of thousands of volts required for spark plug ignition. There are two sets of coils in the ignition coil, the primary coil and the secondary coil. The primary coil has thicker enameled wire and fewer turns; the secondary coil uses thinner enameled wire and has relatively more turns. When the primary coil is connected to the power supply, a strong magnetic field is generated around it as the current increases, and the iron core stores the magnetic field energy; when the switch device disconnects the primary coil circuit, the magnetic field of the primary coil decays rapidly, and the secondary coil will induce a very high voltage. New cars no longer use distributors, but electronically control multiple independent ignition coils to provide ignition for individual cylinders.

des: VTEC control system malfunction
knowledge: VTEC is the abbreviation of Variable Valve Timing and Valve Lift Electronic Control System. In a dual camshaft (DOHC) engine with VTEC, the camshaft that controls the intake valve has two sets of cams with different angles. The camshaft does not directly control the valve, but pushes the valve through a multi-stage rocker arm. At low speeds, the rocker arm corresponding to the larger angle cam is allowed to idle, and the smaller angle cam is used to push the valve. When the speed reaches the set critical point, the latch moves to fix the entire rocker arm, allowing the larger angle cam to push the entire rocker arm, while the smaller angle cam will idle because it cannot touch the rocker arm, so as to achieve the purpose of two-stage control of valve timing and lift. This fault code indicates that the electronic control module has detected a VTEC (variable timing electronic control) operation fault. The cause of the fault indicates a VTEC solenoid valve fault, a VTEC switch fault, an electronic control module (PCM or ECM) fault, etc.

knowledge: VTEC is the abbreviation of Variable Valve Timing and Valve Lift Electronic Control System. In a dual camshaft (DOHC) engine with VTEC, the camshaft that controls the intake valve has two sets of cams with different angles. The camshaft does not directly control the valve, but pushes the valve through a multi-stage rocker arm. At low speeds, the rocker arm corresponding to the larger angle cam is allowed to idle, and the smaller angle cam is used to push the valve. When the speed reaches the set critical point, the latch moves to fix the entire rocker arm, allowing the larger angle cam to push the entire rocker arm, while the smaller angle cam will idle because it cannot touch the rocker arm, so as to achieve the purpose of two-stage control of valve timing and lift. This fault code indicates that the electronic control module has detected a VTEC (variable timing electronic control) operation fault. The cause of the fault indicates a VTEC solenoid valve fault, a VTEC switch fault, an electronic control module (PCM or ECM) fault, etc.

des: Cruise Control Vacuum Solenoid

When acceleration is required, the vacuum solenoid valve opens and communicates with the intake manifold (or a special vacuum pump). The vacuum in the sealing sleeve increases, sucking the diaphragm, overcoming the spring force, and increasing the throttle opening by pulling the wire, so that the vehicle accelerates. When the set speed is reached, the vacuum solenoid valve and the ventilation solenoid valve are closed at the same time. At this time, the vacuum in the sealing sleeve remains unchanged, and the car maintains a constant speed. des: Ignition Amplifier, Primary Circuit 2 - Circuit Open
knowledge: The function of the ignition coil is to convert the 12 volt voltage of the car battery into thousands or even tens of thousands of volts required for spark plug ignition. There are two sets of coils in the ignition coil, the primary coil and the secondary coil. The primary coil has thicker enameled wire and fewer turns; the secondary coil uses thinner enameled wire and has relatively more turns. When the primary coil is connected to the power supply, a strong magnetic field is generated around it as the current increases, and the iron core stores the magnetic field energy; when the switch device disconnects the primary coil circuit, the magnetic field of the primary coil decays rapidly, and the secondary coil will induce a very high voltage. New cars no longer use distributors, but electronically control multiple independent ignition coils to provide ignition for individual cylinders.

VTEC System Malfunction
knowledge: VTEC is the abbreviation of Variable Valve Timing and Valve Lift Electronic Control System. In a dual camshaft (DOHC) engine with VTEC, the camshaft that controls the intake valve has two sets of cams with different angles. The camshaft does not directly control the valve, but pushes the valve through a multi-stage rocker arm. At low speeds, the rocker arm corresponding to the larger angle cam is allowed to idle, and the smaller angle cam is used to push the valve. When the speed reaches the set critical point, the latch moves to fix the entire rocker arm, allowing the larger angle cam to push the entire rocker arm, while the smaller angle cam will idle because it cannot touch the rocker arm, so as to achieve the purpose of two-stage control of valve timing and lift. This fault code indicates that the electronic control module has detected a VTEC (variable timing electronic control) operation fault. The cause of the fault indicates a VTEC solenoid valve fault, a VTEC switch fault, an electronic control module (PCM or ECM) fault, etc.

There are two sets of coils in the ignition coil, the primary coil and the secondary coil. The primary coil has thicker enameled wire and fewer turns; the secondary coil uses thinner enameled wire and has relatively more turns. When the primary coil is connected to the power supply, a strong magnetic field is generated around it as the current increases, and the iron core stores the magnetic field energy; when the switch device disconnects the primary coil circuit, the magnetic field of the primary coil decays rapidly, and the secondary coil will induce a very high voltage. New cars no longer use distributors, but electronically control multiple independent ignition coils to provide ignition for individual cylinders.

des: Turbocharger Boost Pressure Sensor/MAP Sensor/BARO Sensor - Correlation

The boost pressure sensor, also known as the boost pressure sensor (BPS), transmits the boost pressure to the electronic control unit (ECU) in the form of an electrical signal. The manifold absolute pressure (MAP) sensor measures the pressure (vacuum) in the intake manifold. The powertrain control module (PCM) then uses the difference between the intake manifold pressure and the atmospheric pressure (which is linearly related to the engine load) as a basis for determining the basic injection amount of the injector to help the engine achieve the best air-fuel ratio under different loads. The atmospheric pressure sensor (sometimes called the high altitude compensator, HAC) transmits the atmospheric pressure to the electronic control module in the form of an electrical signal. The atmospheric pressure varies with weather and altitude. The lower the pressure, the thinner the air. The powertrain control module (PCM) corrects the fuel supply based on the atmospheric pressure value to help the engine achieve the best air-fuel ratio.

There are two sets of coils in the ignition coil, the primary coil and the secondary coil. The primary coil has thicker enameled wire and fewer turns; the secondary coil uses thinner enameled wire and has relatively more turns. When the primary coil is connected to the power supply, a strong magnetic field is generated around it as the current increases, and the iron core stores the magnetic field energy; when the switch device disconnects the primary coil circuit, the magnetic field of the primary coil decays rapidly, and the secondary coil will induce a very high voltage.

The primary coil has thicker enameled wire and fewer turns; the secondary coil uses thinner enameled wire and has relatively more turns. When the primary coil is connected to the power supply, a strong magnetic field is generated around it as the current increases, and the iron core stores the magnetic field energy; when the switch device disconnects the primary coil circuit, the magnetic field of the primary coil decays rapidly, and the secondary coil will induce a very high voltage. The function of the reductant pressure sensor is to provide feedback to the PCM to control the pump speed through pulse width modulation (Pulse Width Modulation) to regulate the system pressure. The function of the reductant pressure sensor is to provide feedback to the PCM to control the pump speed through pulse width modulation (Pulse Width Modulation) to regulate the system pressure. When the PCM requests reductant injection, the reductant injector opens and the pump runs, providing pressure to the original agent pressure line and injector and purging air from the system. des: Ignition Coil - Signal Error

The primary coil has thicker enameled wire and fewer turns; the secondary coil uses thinner enameled wire and has relatively more turns. When the primary coil is connected to the power supply, a strong magnetic field is generated around it as the current increases, and the iron core stores the magnetic field energy; when the switch device disconnects the primary coil circuit, the magnetic field of the primary coil decays rapidly, and the secondary coil will induce a very high voltage.

des: Ignition Coil , Cylinder 5 - Signal Error
knowledge: The function of the ignition coil is to convert the 12 volt voltage of the car battery into thousands or even tens of thousands of volts required for spark plug ignition. There are two sets of coils in the ignition coil, the primary coil and the secondary coil. The primary coil has thicker enameled wire and fewer turns; the secondary coil uses thinner enameled wire and has relatively more turns. When the primary coil is connected to the power supply, a strong magnetic field is generated around it as the current increases, and the iron core stores the magnetic field energy; when the switch device disconnects the primary coil circuit, the magnetic field of the primary coil decays rapidly, and the secondary coil will induce a very high voltage.

des: Ignition Coil , Cylinder 4 - Signal Error
knowledge: The function of the ignition coil is to convert the 12 volt voltage of the car battery into thousands or even tens of thousands of volts required for spark plug ignition. There are two sets of coils in the ignition coil, the primary coil and the secondary coil. The primary coil has thicker enameled wire and fewer turns; the secondary coil uses thinner enameled wire and has relatively more turns. When the primary coil is connected to the power supply, a strong magnetic field is generated around it as the current increases, and the iron core stores the magnetic field energy; when the switch device disconnects the primary coil circuit, the magnetic field of the primary coil decays rapidly, and the secondary coil will induce a very high voltage.

des: Intake Manifold Flap Motor 2 - No Signal

des: Ignition Coil , Cylinder 3 - Signal Error

There are two sets of coils in the ignition coil, the primary coil and the secondary coil. The primary coil has thicker enameled wire and fewer turns; the secondary coil uses thinner enameled wire and has relatively more turns. When the primary coil is connected to the power supply, a strong magnetic field is generated around it as the current increases, and the iron core stores the magnetic field energy; when the switch device disconnects the primary coil circuit, the magnetic field of the primary coil decays rapidly, and the secondary coil will induce a very high voltage.
